01.1Chapter 1 · The Machine Learning Landscape

Machine Learning Kya Hai?

Aaj machine learning science fiction nahi raha — roz arabon log iska istemal karte hain, bina soche: spam filter, voice assistant, automatic translation, image search, product recommendations. Lekin asal me machine ka "seekhna" matlab kya hota hai? Is section me yahi buniyaad clear karenge.

Machine learning ka matlab

Seedha saaf definition: machine learning woh science (aur art) hai jisme computers ko data se seekhne ke liye program kiya jaata hai.

Ek aur mashhoor definition kehti hai: machine learning woh field hai jo computers ko bina explicitly program kiye seekhne ki ability deta hai.

Engineering wali definition thodi aur precise hai: ek program experience E se task T ke baare me seekhta hai, performance measure P ke hisaab se, agar T par uski performance P se maapi jaaye aur woh experience E ke saath improve hoti jaaye.

Spam filter iska perfect example hai: task T hai naye emails ko spam ya non-spam flag karna, experience E hai training data (users ne jo emails spam flag kiye + normal emails), aur performance measure P hai sahi classify kiye gaye emails ka ratio — jise accuracy kehte hain.

Training set, instance aur model — teen zaroori shabd

  • Training set: woh examples jinse system seekhta hai. Spam filter ke case me flagged spam emails + normal emails.
  • Training instance (ya sample): training set ka ek ek example.
  • Model: system ka woh hissa jo seekhta hai aur predictions banata hai. Neural networks aur random forests models ke examples hain.

Sirf data download kar lena machine learning nahi hai. Agar aap poori Wikipedia download kar lein, to computer ke paas data to bahut aa gaya, lekin woh kisi task me behtar nahi hua — isliye woh ML nahi hai.

Traditional programming vs machine learning

Traditional tareeke se spam filter likhna ho to aapko pehle dekhna padega ki spam kaisa dikhta hai — jaise subject line me "4U", "credit card", "free", "amazing" jaise shabd. Phir har pattern ke liye ek detection rule likhna padega. Problem mushkil hai, to program rules ki lambi list ban jaata hai, jise maintain karna bahut mushkil hota hai.

ML wala spam filter khud seekhta hai ki kaunse shabd spam ke ache predictors hain — woh spam examples me unusually frequent patterns dhoondhta hai, ham examples ke comparison me. Program chhota hota hai, maintain karna aasan hota hai, aur zyada accurate bhi hota hai.

Aur sabse bada faayda: jab spammers "4U" ki jagah "For U" likhne lagte hain, to traditional filter ko haath se update karna padega — lekin ML filter khud notice kar lega ki "For U" spam me frequent ho gaya hai, aur bina aapki madad ke unhe flag karne lagega.

ML kab kaam aata hai? Chaar bade cases

  • Lambi rules wali problems: jahan existing solution me bahut fine-tuning ya rules ki lambi list chahiye — ML model code simplify kar deta hai aur aksar behtar perform karta hai.
  • Complex problems: jahan traditional tareeke se koi achha solution hi nahi milta — jaise speech recognition, hazaron shabd, lakhon alag awaazein, shor bhara mahaul, kai bhashayein.
  • Badalta hua mahaul: ML system ko naye data par dobara train karna aasan hai, to woh hamesha up-to-date rehta hai.
  • Data se insights: trained model ko inspect karke pata chal sakta hai ki usne kya seekha — kabhi kabhi unsuspected correlations ya naye trends dikh jaate hain. Bade data me chhupe patterns dhoondhna data mining kehlata hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 1

01.2Chapter 1 · The Machine Learning Landscape

ML Systems ki Types: Supervised, Unsupervised aur Aage

ML systems itne alag-alag hote hain ki unhe classify karna hi padta hai. Teen bade criteria hain: training ke time kitni supervision milti hai, system on-the-fly seekh sakta hai ya nahi, aur woh generalize kaise karta hai. Is section me pehla criteria — supervision — poora cover karenge.

Supervised learning — labelled data se seekhna

Supervised learning me training set me desired solutions bhi hote hain, jinhe labels kehte hain. Do sabse common supervised tasks hain:

  • Classification: jaise spam filter — email ko spam ya ham classify karna. Target ko label kehte hain.
  • Regression: ek numeric value predict karna — jaise car ki price, uski mileage, age, brand jaise features se. Target ko yahan target kehte hain.

Kuch regression models classification ke liye bhi use ho sakte hain, aur vice versa. Jaise logistic regression classification ke liye commonly use hota hai, kyunki woh ek class se belong karne ki probability de sakta hai.

Unsupervised learning — bina teacher ke seekhna

Yahan training data unlabeled hota hai. System bina bataye khud patterns dhoondhta hai. Chaar common tasks:

  • Clustering: similar visitors ya customers ke groups dhoondhna. Jaise blog visitors me ek group teenagers ka ho sakta hai, doosra weekend par aane wale adults ka.
  • Visualization: complex unlabeled data ko 2D ya 3D diagram me dikhana, taaki structure samajh aaye aur unsuspected patterns dikhein.
  • Dimensionality reduction: data ko simplify karna bina zyada information khoye — jaise car ki mileage aur age ko merge karke ek "wear and tear" feature banana. Ise feature extraction bhi kehte hain. Training data ke dimensions kam karne se algorithm fast chalta hai, kam memory lagti hai, aur kabhi kabhi performance bhi behtar hoti hai.
  • Anomaly detection: unusual credit card transactions ya manufacturing defects pakadna. System mostly normal instances dekh kar seekhta hai, phir naye instance ko normal ya anomaly batata hai. Isse milta-julta task hai novelty detection — jo sirf bilkul naye patterns dhoondhta hai, aur iske liye bahut clean training set chahiye.
  • Association rule learning: bade data me attributes ke beech interesting relations dhoondhna — jaise supermarket me jo log barbecue sauce aur chips khareedte hain, woh steak bhi lete hain.

Semi-supervised, self-supervised aur reinforcement learning

  • Semi-supervised learning: labelling data me time aur paisa lagta hai, to aksar bahut saare unlabeled instances aur kuch labelled instances hote hain. Kuch algorithms partially labelled data se kaam kar lete hain — jaise pehle clustering se similar photos group karna, phir har group ko ek label dekar poora dataset label kar dena.
  • Self-supervised learning: fully unlabeled dataset se fully labelled dataset generate karna. Jaise image ka ek chhota hissa mask karke model ko original image recover karna sikhana — masked image input, original image label. Aise trained model ko phir asli task ke liye fine-tune kiya jaata hai — jaise pet species classify karna. Ek task ka knowledge doosre task me transfer karna transfer learning kehlata hai, aur yeh aaj ki sabse important techniques me se ek hai.
  • Reinforcement learning: yeh bilkul alag hai. Yahan learning system (agent) environment ko observe karta hai, actions leta hai, aur reward ya penalty paata hai. Use khud best strategy — policy — seekhni hoti hai, jisse time ke saath sabse zyada reward mile. Jaise robot ko chalna sikhana, ya game khelne wala bot banana.

ML kahan use hota hai — kuch real examples

  • Production line par products ki images classify karna (image classification, CNNs).
  • Brain scans me tumors detect karna (semantic image segmentation — har pixel classify hota hai).
  • News articles classify karna, offensive comments flag karna, documents summarize karna (NLP / text classification).
  • Company ki next year revenue forecast karna (regression).
  • Voice commands samajhna (speech recognition).
  • Credit card fraud detect karna (anomaly detection).
  • Clients ko unki purchases ke hisaab se segment karna (clustering).
  • Product recommend karna (recommender systems).
  • Game khelne wala intelligent bot banana (reinforcement learning).

Yeh criteria exclusive nahi hain — inhe combine kiya ja sakta hai. Jaise ek state-of-the-art spam filter online, model-based, supervised learning system ho sakta hai.

01.3Chapter 1 · The Machine Learning Landscape

Batch vs Online, Instance vs Model-Based Learning

Supervision ke baad doosra criteria hai: system incrementally seekh sakta hai ya nahi. Teesra criteria hai: woh generalize kaise karta hai — examples yaad karke, ya model bana kar. Dono ko ek real example se samjhenge.

Batch learning (offline learning)

Batch learning me system incrementally seekh nahi sakta — use saara available data ek saath train karna padta hai. Training me bahut time aur computing resources lagte hain, to yeh typically offline hoti hai: pehle train karo, phir production me launch karo, aur phir system sirf apply karta hai, seekhta nahi.

Problem: duniya badalti rehti hai, model wahi rehta hai — isliye uski performance dheere dheere decay karti hai. Ise model rot ya data drift kehte hain. Solution hai model ko up-to-date data par regularly retrain karna — kabhi daily, kabhi weekly. Naye data ke liye poora system scratch se dobara train karna padta hai, sirf naye data par nahi.

Batch learning ki limits: poora data train karna ghanton le sakta hai aur bahut paisa kharch ho sakta hai; data bahut bada ho to impossible bhi ho sakta hai; aur limited resources wale devices (jaise smartphone app) par to yeh bilkul fit nahi hota.

Online learning (incremental learning)

Online learning me system ko data instances ek-ek karke ya chhote groups (mini-batches) me feed kiya jaata hai. Har learning step fast aur cheap hota hai, to system naye data ke baare me on-the-fly seekh sakta hai — jaise stock market ke naye patterns detect karna.

Isse huge datasets bhi train kiye ja sakte hain jo ek machine ki memory me fit nahi hote — ise out-of-core learning kehte hain. Algorithm data ka ek hissa load karta hai, ek training step chalata hai, aur repeat karta hai jab tak saara data cover na ho jaaye.

Ek important parameter hai learning rate — system naye data ke saath kitni jaldi adapt kare. High learning rate ho to system jaldi adapt karega, lekin purana data jaldi bhool bhi jaayega. Low learning rate ho to system dheere seekhega, lekin noise aur outliers se kam sensitive rahega.

Bada risk: agar system ko kharab data feed ho jaaye (jaise kharab sensor, ya koi system ko game karne ki koshish kare), to performance jaldi gir sakti hai. Isliye system ko closely monitor karna padta hai, aur performance drop dikhe to learning turant band karke pehle wale working state par revert karna padta hai.

Instance-based learning — yaad karke generalize karna

Sabse simple tareeka hai ratta maar lena. Spam filter aise banaya jaaye to woh sirf un emails ko flag karega jo pehle flag kiye gaye spam se identical hain. Thoda behtar version: jo emails known spam se bahut similar hain, unhe bhi flag karo — iske liye do emails ke beech similarity measure chahiye, jaise common words ginna.

Ise instance-based learning kehte hain: system examples yaad kar leta hai, phir naye cases ko similarity measure se compare karke generalize karta hai. Jaise naye instance ko triangle classify karna kyunki uske sabse similar instances me zyada tar triangles hain.

Model-based learning — model bana kar predict karna

Doosra tareeka hai examples ka ek model banana, phir us model se predictions karna. Classic example: kya paisa logon ko khush karta hai? Deshon ka GDP per capita aur life satisfaction ka data plot karo to trend dikhta hai — life satisfaction lagbhag linearly badhti hai GDP per capita ke saath.

To aap ek linear model select karte hain: life_satisfaction = theta0 + theta1 × GDP_per_capita. Yeh step hai model selection. Model ke do model parameters hain, theta0 aur theta1 — inhe tweak karke koi bhi linear function represent ki ja sakti hai.

Phir performance measure define karte hain — regression me aksar ek cost function, jo model ki predictions aur training examples ke beech distance maapti hai; objective hota hai is distance ko minimize karna. Linear regression algorithm training examples ko feed karke woh parameters dhoondhta hai jo model ko data se best fit karte hain — yahi hai training the model. Is example me optimal values theta0 = 3.75 aur theta1 = 6.78 × 10^-5 nikli.

Phir model predictions ke liye ready hai (inference). Jaise ek desh ka GDP per capita $37,655 ho to prediction hoti hai 3.75 + 37,655 × 6.78 × 10^-5 = lagbhag 6.30.

Ek baat dhyaan rakho: "model" shabd ke teen matlab hote hain — model ka type (jaise linear regression), poori specified architecture, ya final trained model jo predictions ke liye ready hai.

Typical ML project ka workflow — chaar steps

  1. Data study karo.
  2. Model select karo.
  3. Model ko training data par train karo (learning algorithm woh parameter values dhoondhta hai jo cost function minimize karte hain).
  4. Model ko naye cases par predictions ke liye apply karo, aur ummeed karo ki woh achhe se generalize karega.

Instance-based alternative me bhi yahi kaam hota hai — bas model ki jagah similarity measure use hota hai. Jaise 3-nearest neighbors regression: naye desh ke sabse kareeb teen deshon ki life satisfaction ka average lena.

Code: <Linear model train karke prediction> — GitHub
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Download and prepare the data
data_root = "https://github.com/ageron/data/raw/main/"
lifesat = pd.read_csv(data_root + "lifesat/lifesat.csv")
X = lifesat[["GDP per capita (USD)"]].values
y = lifesat[["Life satisfaction"]].values

# Visualize the data
lifesat.plot(kind='scatter', grid=True,
             x="GDP per capita (USD)", y="Life satisfaction")
plt.axis([23_500, 62_500, 4, 9])
plt.show()

# Select a linear model
model = LinearRegression()

# Train the model
model.fit(X, y)

# Make a prediction for Cyprus
X_new = [[37_655.2]] # Cyprus' GDP per capita in 2020
print(model.predict(X_new)) # output: [[6.30165767]]

GitHub: 01_the_machine_learning_landscape.ipynb

Code: <K-nearest neighbors se wahi prediction> — GitHub
# Select a 3-Nearest Neighbors regression model
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsRegressor

model = KNeighborsRegressor(n_neighbors=3)

# Train the model
model.fit(X, y)

# Make a prediction for Cyprus
print(model.predict(X_new)) # outputs [[6.33333333]]

01.4Chapter 1 · The Machine Learning Landscape

ML ki Challenges: Bad Data, Overfitting aur Testing

ML project me do cheezein galat ho sakti hain: "bad model" aur "bad data". Dono ko samajhna zaroori hai — warna model training data par perfect dikhega, lekin naye cases par fail ho jaayega.

Bad data — chaar bade problems

  • Insufficient quantity: bachche ko seb pehchanne ke liye do-chaar examples kaafi hain, lekin ML ko simple problems ke liye bhi hazaaron examples chahiye, aur image ya speech recognition jaise complex problems ke liye lakhon. Ek mashhoor 2001 ke paper ne dikhaya ki kaafi data milne par bahut alag-alag algorithms bhi lagbhag equally achha perform karte hain — data kabhi kabhi algorithm se zyada matter karta hai. Lekin chhote aur medium datasets abhi bhi bahut common hain, to algorithms ko chhodna mat.
  • Nonrepresentative training data: training set un cases ka representative hona chahiye jin par generalize karna hai. Sample chhota ho to sampling noise aa jaata hai; bada sample bhi nonrepresentative ho sakta hai agar sampling method flawed ho — ise sampling bias kehte hain. Classic example: 1936 ke ek bade US election poll ne 24 lakh answers ke basis par galat winner predict kiya tha, kyunki addresses telephone directories aur magazine subscriber lists se liye gaye the — jo ameer logon ki taraf biased the — aur sirf 25% se kam logon ne jawab diya tha (nonresponse bias).
  • Poor-quality data: errors, outliers aur noise se patterns dhoondhna mushkil ho jaata hai. Data scientists apna bahut saara time data clean karne me lagate hain — outliers discard karna ya fix karna, missing values ko median se bharna ya un instances ko ignore karna.
  • Irrelevant features: garbage in, garbage out. System tabhi seekh paayega jab training data me kaafi relevant features hon aur zyada irrelevant na hon. Achhe features banana feature engineering kehlata hai: feature selection (sabse useful features chunna), feature extraction (existing features combine karke behtar feature banana), aur naye data se naye features banana.

Overfitting — training data par perfect, naye data par fail

Overfitting ka matlab hai model training data par achha perform karta hai, lekin generalize nahi karta. Jaise high-degree polynomial model life satisfaction data ko training par simple linear model se bahut behtar fit karta hai — lekin kya aap uski predictions par bharosa karenge?

Complex models jaise deep neural networks subtle patterns detect kar sakte hain, lekin agar training set noisy ya bahut chhota hai, to model noise me hi patterns dhoondhne lagta hai. Jaise model yeh "seekh" le ki jin deshon ke naam me "w" hai, unki life satisfaction 7 se zyada hai — sirf isliye kyunki training data me aisa coincidence tha. Yeh pattern naye deshon par bilkul generalize nahi karega.

Overfitting tab hota hai jab model training data ki quantity aur noisiness ke hisaab se bahut complex ho. Solutions:

  • Model simplify karo — kam parameters wala model chuno, attributes kam karo, ya model ko constrain karo.
  • Zyada training data jama karo.
  • Training data ka noise kam karo — errors fix karo, outliers hatao.

Regularization aur hyperparameters

Model ko constrain karke simple banana aur overfitting ka risk kam karna regularization kehlata hai. Linear model me theta1 ko zero force kar do to algorithm ke paas sirf ek degree of freedom bachta hai — line sirf upar-neeche move kar sakti hai. Theta1 ko chhota rakhne par force karo to model beech ka kuch banta hai. Goal hai perfect fit aur simplicity ke beech sahi balance dhoondhna.

Kitni regularization apply karni hai, yeh ek hyperparameter se control hota hai. Hyperparameter learning algorithm ka parameter hota hai (model ka nahi) — ise training se pehle set karna padta hai aur training ke dauraan constant rehta hai. Hyperparameters tune karna ML system banane ka important hissa hai.

Underfitting — model bahut simple

Underfitting overfitting ka ulta hai: model itna simple hota hai ki data ki underlying structure seekh hi nahi paata. Jaise life satisfaction ka linear model underfit karne wala hai — reality model se zyada complex hai, to predictions training examples par bhi inaccurate hongi. Fixes: zyada powerful model chuno, behtar features do (feature engineering), ya model par constraints kam karo (regularization hyperparameter ghatao).

Testing aur validating — "hope" par bharosa mat karo

Model naye cases par generalize karega ya nahi, yeh jaanne ka ek tareeka hai use production me daal kar monitor karna — lekin agar model bahut kharab nikla to users complain karenge. Behtar tareeka: data ko do hisson me baanto — training set aur test set. Training set se train karo, test set se test karo. Naye cases par error rate ko generalization error (ya out-of-sample error) kehte hain. Test set par evaluate karke iska estimate milta hai.

Aam taur par 80% data training aur 20% testing ke liye use hota hai. Agar training error low hai lekin generalization error high hai, to model training data ko overfit kar raha hai.

Hyperparameter tuning aur model selection — validation set

Do models me se kaunsa behtar hai, yeh test set se compare karke pata chal sakta hai. Lekin agar aap test set par baar-baar measure karke hyperparameters tune karte hain, to model usi test set ke liye best ban jaata hai — aur naye data par utna achha perform nahi karega. Yeh trap hai.

Solution hai holdout validation: training set ka ek hissa alag rakh lo — validation set (ya dev set). Kai candidate models ko reduced training set par train karo, validation set par best chuno, phir best model ko full training set (validation set samet) par dobara train karo, aur aakhir me test set par evaluate karo.

Validation set bahut chhota ho to evaluations imprecise hongi; bahut bada ho to bacha hua training set bahut chhota ho jaayega. Iska solution hai repeated cross-validation — kai chhote validation sets use karna, har model ko har set par evaluate karna, aur average lena. Isse zyada accurate measure milta hai, lekin training time utne guna badh jaata hai jitne validation sets hain.

Data mismatch — train-dev set

Kabhi kabhi training ke liye bahut data aasani se mil jaata hai, lekin woh production data ka perfectly representative nahi hota. Jaise flowers ki species pehchanne wala app: web se lakhon flower photos mil jaayengi, lekin mobile app se li gayi sirf 1,000 representative photos hongi.

Rule: validation set aur test set production data ke jitne representative ho sake, utne hone chahiye — isliye inme sirf representative pictures honi chahiye. Phir ek aur set banao — train-dev set — training data (web photos) me se hold out karke. Agar model train-dev set par kharab perform kare, to usne training set ko overfit kiya hai. Agar train-dev par achha aur dev set par kharab kare, to problem data mismatch ki hai — jaise web images ko preprocess karke mobile photos jaisa banana.

No Free Lunch theorem — koi universal best model nahi

Model data ka simplified representation hota hai. Model type select karte hi aap data ke baare me kuch assumptions bana lete hain — jaise linear model chunna matlab assume karna ki data fundamentally linear hai. 1996 ke ek mashhoor paper ne dikhaya ki agar data ke baare me bilkul koi assumption na banayi jaaye, to koi bhi model kisi aur se behtar hone ka reason nahi hai — ise No Free Lunch theorem kehte hain. Kuch datasets ke liye linear model best hai, kuch ke liye neural network. Practical tareeka: data ke baare me reasonable assumptions banao aur kuch reasonable models evaluate karo.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 1
← Previous01.3 · Batch vs Online, Instance vs Model-Based Learning→ Next02.1 · Problem Frame Karo, Data Lao, Test Set Alag Rakho
02.1Chapter 2 · End-to-End Machine Learning Project

Problem Frame Karo, Data Lao, Test Set Alag Rakho

Is chapter me ek poora ML project end-to-end karenge — ek real estate company ke data scientist ban kar, California census data se housing prices predict karenge. Project ke aath main steps hain: big picture dekho, data lao, data explore karo, data prepare karo, model select karke train karo, model fine-tune karo, solution present karo, aur launch-monitor-maintain karo.

Pehle big picture — business objective kya hai?

Model banana end goal nahi hota. Pehla sawaal boss se: company model ka istemal kaise karegi aur kya faayda hoga? Yahan model ka output (district ki median housing price ka prediction) ek downstream ML system ko feed hoga, jo decide karega ki kisi area me invest karna worth hai ya nahi. Yeh seedha revenue ko affect karta hai.

Doosra sawaal: current solution kya hai? Experts manually prices estimate karte hain — costly, time-consuming, aur estimates aksar 30% se zyada galat hote hain. Isliye company ko lagta hai ki model train karna useful hoga.

Phir problem frame karo: yeh clearly supervised learning hai (har instance ke saath expected output — median housing price — hai), ek regression task hai (value predict karni hai), multiple regression hai (multiple features use honge), univariate hai (sirf ek value predict karni hai), aur plain batch learning kaafi hai — data ka continuous flow nahi hai, jaldi adapt karne ki zaroorat nahi, aur data memory me fit ho jaata hai.

Performance measure chuno — RMSE vs MAE

Regression ke liye typical performance measure hai root mean square error (RMSE) — system typically kitni error karta hai, badi errors ko zyada weight dekar. Formula: predictions aur actual values ke beech squared differences ka mean, phir uska square root.

Agar bahut saare outlier districts hon, to mean absolute error (MAE) behtar ho sakta hai — yeh absolute differences ka average hai. RMSE Euclidean norm (l2 norm) se correspond karta hai, MAE Manhattan norm (l1 norm) se. Norm index jitna bada, utna zyada focus badi values par — isliye RMSE outliers ke prati MAE se zyada sensitive hai. Lekin jab outliers exponentially rare hon (jaise bell-shaped curve me), to RMSE bahut achha perform karta hai aur generally preferred hai.

Notation yaad rakho: m = instances ki count, x(i) = ith instance ka feature vector, y(i) = uska label, X = saare feature values ka matrix, h = prediction function (hypothesis), aur y-hat = h(x(i)) prediction hai.

Assumptions check karo — pehle hi

Ab tak ki assumptions list karo aur verify karo. Jaise: downstream system ko actual prices chahiye, ya sirf categories (cheap/medium/expensive)? Agar sirf categories chahiye, to problem classification hoti, regression nahi! Months kaam karne ke baad yeh pata chalna disaster hota. Yahan downstream team se confirm hua ki unhe actual prices hi chahiye — lights green hain.

Data lao — California Housing dataset

Real data se experiment karna best hai — open datasets ke liye OpenML, Kaggle, PapersWithCode, UC Irvine ML Repository, Amazon AWS datasets aur TensorFlow datasets jaise sources hain. Is project me California Housing Prices dataset use hota hai, jo 1990 California census par based hai — 20,640 districts, 10 attributes: longitude, latitude, housing_median_age, total_rooms, total_bedrooms, population, households, median_income, median_house_value, aur ocean_proximity.

Data manually download karne ki jagah ek function likho jo fetch kare — khaas taur par jab data regularly change hota ho, ya multiple machines par install karna ho.

GitHub: 02_end_to_end_machine_learning_project.ipynb

Code: <Housing data download aur load karo> — GitHub
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import tarfile
import urllib.request

def load_housing_data():
    tarball_path = Path("datasets/housing.tgz")
    if not tarball_path.is_file():
        Path("datasets").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        url = "https://github.com/ageron/data/raw/main/housing.tgz"
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, tarball_path)
    with tarfile.open(tarball_path) as housing_tarball:
            housing_tarball.extractall(path="datasets")
    return pd.read_csv(Path("datasets/housing/housing.csv"))

housing = load_housing_data()

Data ko jaldi se dekho — head, info, describe, histograms

  • head(): pehli paanch rows — har row ek district hai.
  • info(): total rows, har attribute ka type, non-null values. Yahan total_bedrooms me sirf 20,433 non-null values hain — matlab 207 districts me yeh feature missing hai.
  • value_counts(): ocean_proximity categorical hai — categories: <1H OCEAN (9,136), INLAND (6,551), NEAR OCEAN (2,658), NEAR BAY (2,290), ISLAND (sirf 5).
  • describe(): count, mean, std (standard deviation — values kitne dispersed hain), min, max, aur percentiles (25%, 50% median, 75%).
  • hist(): har numerical attribute ka histogram. Yahan se pata chala: median income dollars me nahi hai — scaled aur capped hai (0.5 se 15 tak, roughly tens of thousands dollars); median house value bhi $500,000 par capped hai — jo target attribute hai, to yeh serious problem ho sakta hai; attributes ke scales bahut alag hain; aur kai histograms right-skewed hain.

Test set banao — aur use kabhi mat dekho

Aage badhne se pehle test set banao aur use side me rakh do — kabhi mat dekho. Kyun? Aapka dimaag ek amazing pattern detection system hai, lekin woh overfitting ke liye bhi prone hai: agar aap test set dekh kar koi pattern dhoondh lein aur us hisaab se model chunein, to generalization error ka estimate bahut optimistic hoga. Ise data snooping bias kehte hain.

Simple tareeka: randomly 20% instances alag kar do. Lekin dobara run karne par alag test set ban jaayega. Fix: random seed set karo (jaise random_state=42), ya test set ko save karke dobara load karo. Dataset update hone par bhi stable split chahiye to instance ke identifier ka hash use karo — hash 20% se kam ho to instance test set me.

Scikit-Learn ka train_test_split() yahi karta hai, random_state parameter ke saath. Lekin purely random sampling me sampling bias ka risk hai — jaise survey me 1,000 log randomly chunne par female ratio skewed ho sakta hai. Solution hai stratified sampling: population ko homogeneous subgroups (strata) me baanto aur har stratum se sahi ratio me sample lo.

Yahan median income sabse important attribute hai, to uski categories banao (pd.cut se 5 categories: 0–1.5, 1.5–3, 3–4.5, 4.5–6, 6+), phir StratifiedShuffleSplit ya train_test_split(stratify=...) se stratified test set banao. Result: stratified test set ke income proportions full dataset se lagbhag identical hote hain, jabki random test set skewed hota hai. Kaam khatam ho to income_cat column drop kar do.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← Previous01.4 · ML ki Challenges: Bad Data, Overfitting aur Testing→ Next02.2 · Data Explore Karo aur ML ke Liye Prepare Karo
02.2Chapter 2 · End-to-End Machine Learning Project

Data Explore Karo aur ML ke Liye Prepare Karo

Test set side me rakh diya — ab sirf training set explore karo. Goal hai insights gain karna, data quirks dhoondhna, aur phir data ko ML algorithms ke liye prepare karna. Yeh step project ka sabse bada hissa hai — aur sabse important bhi.

Geographical data visualize karo

Latitude-longitude scatterplot banao — alpha=0.2 set karne se high-density areas dikhne lagte hain: Bay Area, Los Angeles aur San Diego ke aas-paas, aur Central Valley me Sacramento aur Fresno ke paas. Phir price ko color aur population ko circle size bana kar plot karo: prices location se bahut related hain (ocean ke kareeb mehenga), aur population density se bhi. Clustering algorithm yahan useful ho sakta hai — cluster centers ke kareeb hone ke naye features banane ke liye.

Correlations dhoondho

corr() se har attribute pair ka standard correlation coefficient (r) nikalo — range -1 se 1. Median house value ke saath sabse strong correlation median income ki hai (0.688), phir total_rooms (0.137), housing_median_age (0.102). Latitude ka halka negative correlation hai (-0.14) — uttar me jaane par prices thodi kam hoti hain.

scatter_matrix() se promising attributes ko ek doosre ke against plot karo. Median income vs house value ke plot me price cap $500,000 par ek horizontal line ki tarah saaf dikhta hai — aur $450,000, $350,000, $280,000 ke aas-paas aur bhi lines hain. In districts ko hatane par algorithms yeh data quirks reproduce karna nahi seekhenge.

Dhyaan rakho: correlation coefficient sirf linear correlations maapta hai. Nonlinear relationships ko woh poori tarah miss kar sakta hai — correlation 0 hone par bhi axes independent nahi hote.

Attribute combinations try karo

Total rooms akele utna useful nahi — rooms per household zyada meaningful hai. Isi tarah bedrooms ratio aur people per household banao:

  • rooms_per_house = total_rooms / households
  • bedrooms_ratio = total_bedrooms / total_rooms
  • people_per_house = population / households

Result: bedrooms_ratio ka correlation -0.256 nikla — total rooms ya bedrooms se kahin zyada informative! Kam bedroom/room ratio wale ghar mehenga hote hain. Rooms per household bhi total rooms se zyada informative hai — bade ghar mehenga hote hain, obvious si baat.

Data clean karo — missing values

Zyada tar ML algorithms missing features ke saath kaam nahi kar sakte. Teen options hain: corresponding districts hata do, poora attribute hata do, ya missing values ko kisi value se bhar do (zero, mean, median) — ise imputation kehte hain.

Best practice: Scikit-Learn ka SimpleImputer use karo (strategy="median") — woh har feature ka median seekh kar store kar leta hai (statistics_ attribute me), to training set ke saath-saath validation set, test set aur naye data par bhi wahi medians apply ho sakte hain. Mean, most_frequent, ya constant value se bharna bhi options hain. Aur bhi powerful imputers hain: KNNImputer (k-nearest neighbors ke values ka mean) aur IterativeImputer (har feature ke liye regression model train karke missing values predict karna).

Scikit-Learn API design — paanch principles

  • Consistency: sab objects ka simple interface — estimators fit() se parameters estimate karte hain, transformers transform() se data transform karte hain, predictors predict() se predictions aur score() se quality maapte hain.
  • Inspection: hyperparameters public instance variables hain (jaise imputer.strategy), aur seekhe hue parameters underscore suffix ke saath (jaise imputer.statistics_).
  • Nonproliferation of classes: datasets NumPy arrays ya SciPy sparse matrices hote hain, homemade classes nahi.
  • Composition: existing building blocks reuse hote hain — jaise Pipeline me transformers ki sequence.
  • Sensible defaults: zyada tar parameters ke reasonable default values hote hain, to baseline system jaldi ban jaata hai.

Ek aur zaroori baat: Scikit-Learn transformers NumPy arrays output karte hain, DataFrames nahi — to column names wapas paane ke liye get_feature_names_out() se DataFrame wrap karna padta hai.

Text aur categorical attributes handle karo

ocean_proximity ek categorical attribute hai. OrdinalEncoder use karke categories ko numbers (0–4) me convert kar sakte ho, lekin problem hai: ML algorithms maan lete hain ki paas wale numbers zyada similar hote hain — jo ocean_proximity ke liye galat hai.

Solution hai one-hot encoding: har category ke liye ek binary attribute — sirf ek attribute 1 (hot) hota hai, baaki 0 (cold). OneHotEncoder yeh karta hai, aur default output SciPy sparse matrix hota hai (mostly zeros wale bade matrices ke liye memory efficient).

Pandas ka get_dummies() bhi one-hot karta hai, lekin OneHotEncoder behtar hai kyunki woh seekhe hue categories yaad rakhta hai: production me model ko training wale hi features milne chahiye — na zyada, na kam. Unknown category aaye to OneHotEncoder exception deta hai, ya handle_unknown="ignore" set karo to use zeros se represent karta hai. Agar categories bahut zyada hon (jaise country code), to unhe useful numerical features se replace karna behtar hai — jaise ocean se distance — ya embeddings use karna.

Feature scaling — min-max vs standardization

ML algorithms tab achha perform nahi karte jab input attributes ke scales bahut alag hon. Yahan total_rooms 6 se 39,320 tak hai, jabki median income sirf 0 se 15 tak — bina scaling ke models median income ko ignore karke rooms par focus karenge.

  • Min-max scaling (normalization): values ko 0–1 range me laana — min subtract karke (max − min) se divide karna. MinMaxScaler use hota hai, feature_range se range badli ja sakti hai (neural networks ke liye -1 se 1 behtar hota hai). Outliers se bahut affect hota hai.
  • Standardization: mean subtract karo (zero mean), phir standard deviation se divide karo (std 1). StandardScaler use hota hai. Values kisi range me restricted nahi hoti, lekin outliers se kam affect hoti hai.

Scalers ko sirf training data par fit karo — kabhi bhi validation ya test set par fit() mat chalao. Trained scaler se transform() kisi bhi set par chal sakta hai.

Heavy tails, bucketizing aur RBF features

Jab feature ka distribution heavy-tailed ho (door ki values exponentially rare na hon), to scaling se pehle use transform karna chahiye: square root ya log lena (population feature power law follow karta hai — log lene par woh lagbhag bell-shaped Gaussian ban jaata hai). Bucketizing bhi ek tareeka hai — distribution ko equal-sized buckets me kaat kar har value ko uske bucket index se replace karna.

Multimodal distribution (jaise housing_median_age ke do peaks) ke liye buckets ko categories ki tarah one-hot encode kiya ja sakta hai, ya har mode ke liye ek similarity feature add kiya ja sakta hai — Gaussian RBF se, jaise exp(-gamma × (x − 35)^2). Target values ko bhi transform kiya ja sakta hai (jaise log), lekin phir predictions ko wapas original scale me convert karna padta hai — TransformedTargetRegressor yeh automatically kar deta hai.

Custom transformers aur pipelines

Scikit-Learn me bahut transformers hain, lekin kabhi kabhi apne likhne padte hain. Training na chahiye ho to FunctionTransformer kaafi hai — jaise np.log ya rbf_kernel wrap karna. Trainable transformer chahiye to ek class likho jisme fit() (self return kare), transform() aur fit_transform() hon — BaseEstimator aur TransformerMixin se get_params/set_params aur fit_transform free me mil jaate hain.

Example: ClusterSimilarity transformer — fit() me KMeans se 10 cluster centers dhoondhta hai, transform() me har district ki har cluster center se Gaussian RBF similarity maapta hai. Yeh geographic features latitude-longitude se zyada useful hote hain.

Pipeline class transformation steps ki sequence ko ek object me band kar deti hai: pehle impute, phir standardize. ColumnTransformer alag columns par alag transformers apply karta hai — numerical par num_pipeline, categorical par cat_pipeline — aur outputs ko horizontally concatenate kar deta hai. Full preprocessing pipeline me yeh sab hota hai: median se imputation, most frequent category se imputation, one-hot encoding, ratio features (bedrooms_ratio, rooms_per_house, people_per_house), log transforms, cluster similarity features, aur standardization — total 24 features.

GitHub: 02_end_to_end_machine_learning_project.ipynb

Code: <Pipeline aur ColumnTransformer se preprocessing> — GitHub
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer

num_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
    ("standardize", StandardScaler()),
])

num_attribs = ["longitude", "latitude", "housing_median_age", "total_rooms",
               "total_bedrooms", "population", "households", "median_income"]
cat_attribs = ["ocean_proximity"]

cat_pipeline = make_pipeline(
    SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent"),
    OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore"))

preprocessing = ColumnTransformer([
    ("num", num_pipeline, num_attribs),
    ("cat", cat_pipeline, cat_attribs),
])

housing_prepared = preprocessing.fit_transform(housing)
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← Previous02.1 · Problem Frame Karo, Data Lao, Test Set Alag Rakho→ Next02.3 · Model Train Karo, Fine-Tune Karo, Launch Karo
02.3Chapter 2 · End-to-End Machine Learning Project

Model Train Karo, Fine-Tune Karo, Launch Karo

Problem frame ho gaya, data explore aur prepare ho gaya — ab model train karne ka time hai. Pehle simple model se baseline banao, phir behtar models try karo, cross-validation se honestly evaluate karo, hyperparameters tune karo, aur aakhir me launch karke monitor karo.

Pehle baseline — linear regression

Preprocessing pipeline ke saath LinearRegression train karo — ek line me: make_pipeline(preprocessing, LinearRegression()), phir fit(). Training set par RMSE nikla 68,688 — median house values zyada tar $120,000–$265,000 ke beech hain, to typical error $68,688 bilkul satisfying nahi hai. Yeh underfitting ka example hai: features kaafi information nahi de rahe, ya model kaafi powerful nahi hai.

Decision tree — training par perfect, asal me overfit

DecisionTreeRegressor try karo — yeh powerful model hai, complex nonlinear relationships dhoondh sakta hai. Training set par RMSE nikla 0.0 — bilkul zero error! Kya model sach me perfect hai? Bilkul nahi — yeh badly overfit hai. Sure kaise hon? Test set ko abhi chhoona nahi hai, to training set ka ek hissa validation ke liye use karo.

Cross-validation se honest evaluation

k-fold cross-validation: training set ko 10 non-overlapping folds me baanto, model ko 10 baar train karo — har baar ek alag fold evaluation ke liye, baaki 9 training ke liye. Scikit-Learn ka cross_val_score() yeh karta hai. Dhyaan rakho: Scikit-Learn ko utility function chahiye (greater is better), isliye scoring "neg_root_mean_squared_error" use hota hai — negative value, sign flip karke RMSE milta hai.

  • Decision tree: cross-validation RMSE lagbhag 66,868 (± 2,061) — linear model (69,858 ± 4,182) se bas thoda behtar. Training error zero aur validation error high = severe overfitting.
  • Random forest: cross-validation RMSE lagbhag 47,020 (± 1,034) — bahut behtar! Random forest kai decision trees ko features ke random subsets par train karke unki predictions average karta hai. Aise models ko ensembles kehte hain. Lekin training set par iska RMSE lagbhag 17,474 hai — abhi bhi kaafi overfitting hai.

Cross-validation ka faayda: sirf performance ka estimate nahi, uski precision (standard deviation) bhi milti hai. Cost: model kai baar train karna padta hai. Strategy: pehle kai alag categories ke models try karo bina zyada tuning ke, aur 2–5 promising models shortlist karo.

Fine-tuning — grid search aur randomized search

Hyperparameters haath se fiddle karna tedious hai. GridSearchCV aapke liye search karta hai: aap batate hain kaunse hyperparameters aur kaunsi values try karni hain, woh cross-validation se saare combinations evaluate karta hai. Pipeline me nested estimators ke hyperparameters double underscore se refer kiye jaate hain — jaise preprocessing__geo__n_clusters.

Is project me grid search ne 15 combinations × 3-fold CV = 45 rounds training karke best parameters dhoondhe: n_clusters=15, max_features=6 — mean test RMSE 44,042, jo default hyperparameters wale 47,019 se behtar hai. Tip: agar best value search range ke edge par ho (jaise 15 maximum tha), to aur badi values ke saath dobara search karo.

RandomizedSearchCV aksar behtar hota hai, khaas taur par jab search space bada ho: woh fixed number of combinations evaluate karta hai, har hyperparameter ke liye random values chun kar. Continuous hyperparameters ke liye yeh kai zyada values explore karta hai, aur bekaar hyperparameters search ko slow nahi karte. HalvingRandomSearchCV aur HalvingGridSearchCV pehle round me kam resources se kai candidates evaluate karke sirf best ko aage bhejte hain — isse time bachta hai.

GitHub: 02_end_to_end_machine_learning_project.ipynb

Code: <GridSearchCV se random forest fine-tune karo> — GitHub
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV

full_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ("preprocessing", preprocessing),
    ("random_forest", RandomForestRegressor(random_state=42)),
])
param_grid = [
    {'preprocessing__geo__n_clusters': [5, 8, 10],
     'random_forest__max_features': [4, 6, 8]},
    {'preprocessing__geo__n_clusters': [10, 15],
     'random_forest__max_features': [6, 8, 10]},
]
grid_search = GridSearchCV(full_pipeline, param_grid, cv=3,
                           scoring='neg_root_mean_squared_error')
grid_search.fit(housing, housing_labels)

grid_search.best_params_
# {'preprocessing__geo__n_clusters': 15, 'random_forest__max_features': 6}

Best models analyze karo — feature importances aur errors

Random forest har attribute ki relative importance bata sakta hai (feature_importances_). Sabse important nikla log__median_income (lagbhag 0.19), phir cat__ocean_proximity_INLAND (0.075), bedrooms__ratio (0.069), rooms_per_house__ratio aur people_per_house__ratio. Kam useful features ko drop karke try kar sakte ho — SelectFromModel transformer yeh automatically kar deta hai.

Specific errors ko bhi dekho: system kahan galti karta hai, kyun karta hai, kya fix kar sakta hai — extra features, uninformative features hatana, outliers clean karna. Aur yeh bhi check karo ki model har category par achha hai ya nahi — rural ya urban, rich ya poor, north ya south. Agar kisi category par model kharab hai, to use deploy nahi karna chahiye jab tak issue solve na ho — warna nuksaan ho sakta hai.

Ensemble methods ek aur fine-tuning tareeka hai: best models ko combine karo — group aksar best individual model se behtar perform karta hai, khaas taur par jab individual models alag-alag tarah ki errors karte hon.

Test set par final evaluation

Ab final model ko test set par evaluate karo — jise ab tak kabhi nahi dekha tha. Final RMSE nikla 41,424. Sirf point estimate kaafi na ho to 95% confidence interval nikalo — yahan 39,275 se 43,467. Dhyaan rakho: bahut hyperparameter tuning ke baad performance cross-validation se thodi kharab ho sakti hai, kyunki system validation data ke liye fine-tune ho jaata hai. Aise me test set par numbers achhe dikhane ke liye hyperparameters tweak karne ki temptation se bacho — woh improvements naye data par generalize nahi karenge.

Prelaunch phase: solution present karo — kya seekha, kya kaam kiya aur kya nahi, assumptions kya thi, limitations kya hain — sab kuch document karo, aur clear visualizations ke saath presentations banao (jaise "median income housing prices ka number one predictor hai").

Launch, monitor aur maintain karo

Model save karo (joblib.dump), production environment me transfer karo, aur load karke predictions lo. Custom classes aur functions ko bhi production me transfer karna padta hai, kyunki model un par depend karta hai.

Deployment ke tareeke: model ko web application ke andar use karna, ya ek dedicated web service me wrap karna jise REST API se query kiya jaaye — isse model upgrade karna aasan hota hai, scaling aasan hoti hai, aur web app kisi bhi language me likhi ja sakti hai. Cloud option bhi hai — jaise model ko cloud storage par upload karke ek managed web service banana jo load balancing aur scaling khud handle kare.

  • Monitoring: live performance ko regular intervals par check karo aur drop hone par alerts trigger karo. Performance tezi se bhi gir sakti hai (koi component break ho jaaye), ya dheere dheere — model rot ki wajah se. Human raters se bhi evaluation karwayi ja sakti hai — jaise model ki uncertain classifications ka sample experts ko bhejna.
  • Retraining automate karo: fresh data regularly collect karo aur label karo, training aur hyperparameter tuning ki script schedule karo, naye aur purane model ko updated test set par compare karo, aur performance na gire to hi deploy karo.
  • Input data quality monitor karo: agar missing features badh rahe hon, mean ya standard deviation drift kar raha ho, ya categorical feature me naye categories aa rahi hon, to alert trigger karo.
  • Backups rakho: har model aur har dataset version ka backup rakho, taaki kharab model se turant pehle wale par rollback kar sako, aur kisi bhi model ko kisi bhi purane dataset par evaluate kar sako.

ML me infrastructure ka kaam aksar model banane se zyada hota hai — is field ko MLOps kehte hain. Lekin ek baar infrastructure ban jaaye, to idea se production tak jaana bahut fast ho jaata hai.

GitHub: 02_end_to_end_machine_learning_project.ipynb

Code: <Final model ko test set par evaluate karo> — GitHub
X_test = strat_test_set.drop("median_house_value", axis=1)
y_test = strat_test_set["median_house_value"].copy()

final_predictions = final_model.predict(X_test)

final_rmse = mean_squared_error(y_test, final_predictions, squared=False)
print(final_rmse) # prints 41424.40026462184
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← Previous02.2 · Data Explore Karo aur ML ke Liye Prepare Karo→ Next03.1 · MNIST aur Binary Classifier: 5-Detector
03.1Chapter 3 · Classification

MNIST aur Binary Classifier: 5-Detector

Chapter 1 me regression aur classification do sabse common supervised tasks bataye gaye the. Chapter 2 me regression project kiya — housing prices predict karna. Ab classification ki baari hai, aur iske liye MNIST dataset perfect hai.

MNIST dataset — ML ka "hello world"

MNIST 70,000 chhoti images ka set hai — handwritten digits, high school students aur census bureau ke employees ke haath se likhe. Har image ko us digit se label kiya gaya hai jo woh represent karti hai. Yeh dataset itna study kiya gaya hai ki ise machine learning ka "hello world" kehte hain: jab bhi koi naya classification algorithm aata hai, log dekhna chahte hain ki MNIST par woh kaisa perform karta hai.

Scikit-Learn ka fetch_openml() function is dataset ko OpenML se download karta hai. Har image 28 × 28 pixels ki hai, aur har pixel ki intensity ek feature hai (0 white se 255 black tak) — matlab har image me 784 features hain. Data shape: X (70,000, 784), y (70,000,).

Ek digit dekhne ke liye feature vector ko 28 × 28 array me reshape karke Matplotlib ke imshow() se display karo. Pehla digit '5' hai — label bhi yahi kehta hai.

Pehle test set alag karo — hamesha

Data ko closely inspect karne se pehle hamesha test set banao aur side me rakh do. MNIST fetch_openml() se already split aata hai: pehle 60,000 images training set, aakhri 10,000 test set. Training set already shuffled hai — achha hai, kyunki isse saare cross-validation folds similar honge, aur kuch algorithms jo training instances ke order se sensitive hote hain, woh kharab perform nahi karenge.

Binary classifier — sirf 5 pehchanna

Problem simplify karte hain: sirf ek digit pehchanna — number 5. Yeh "5-detector" ek binary classifier hai, jo sirf do classes distinguish karta hai: 5 aur non-5. Target vectors banao: y_train_5 = (y_train == '5') — 5s ke liye True, baaki ke liye False.

Classifier chuno: SGDClassifier (stochastic gradient descent) — yeh bahut bade datasets efficiently handle kar sakta hai, kyunki SGD training instances ko ek-ek karke independently process karta hai, jo ise online learning ke liye bhi suitable banata hai. Train karo: sgd_clf.fit(X_train, y_train_5). Phir predict karo: sgd_clf.predict([some_digit]) — True aaya, matlab classifier ne sahi guess kiya.

GitHub: 03_classification.ipynb

Code: <MNIST load karo aur 5-detector train karo> — GitHub
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

mnist = fetch_openml('mnist_784', as_frame=False)
X, y = mnist.data, mnist.target

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = X[:60000], X[60000:], y[:60000], y[60000:]

y_train_5 = (y_train == '5')  # True for all 5s, False for all other digits
y_test_5 = (y_test == '5')

from sklearn.linear_model import SGDClassifier

sgd_clf = SGDClassifier(random_state=42)
sgd_clf.fit(X_train, y_train_5)
sgd_clf.predict([some_digit])  # array([ True])

Accuracy ka dhokha — 95% bhi kaafi nahi

Cross-validation (3 folds) se accuracy nikli: 95% se zyada har fold par! Amazing lagta hai, hai na? Lekin ruko — ek dummy classifier try karo jo har image ko sabse frequent class (non-5) me classify karta hai. Uski accuracy bhi 90% se zyada hai!

Kyun? Kyunki sirf lagbhag 10% images 5s hain — to hamesha "non-5" guess karne par bhi 90% baar sahi ho jaoge. Yahi dikhata hai ki accuracy generally classifiers ke liye preferred performance measure nahi hai, khaas taur par jab datasets skewed hon (kuch classes bahut zyada frequent hon). Behtar tareeka hai confusion matrix dekhna.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← Previous02.3 · Model Train Karo, Fine-Tune Karo, Launch Karo→ Next03.2 · Confusion Matrix, Precision-Recall aur ROC Curve
03.2Chapter 3 · Classification

Confusion Matrix, Precision-Recall aur ROC Curve

Classifier evaluate karna regressor evaluate karne se aksar tricky hota hai. Accuracy dhokha de sakti hai — isliye is chapter ka bada hissa performance measures par hai. Confusion matrix se shuru karte hain.

Confusion matrix — chaar numbers me poori kahani

Confusion matrix gin-ti hai ki class A ke instances ko kitni baar class B classify kiya gaya. Pehle cross_val_predict() se predictions lo — yeh k-fold cross-validation karta hai, lekin scores ki jagah har instance ke liye out-of-sample predictions return karta hai (model ne woh data training me kabhi nahi dekha).

5-detector ki confusion matrix:

  • True negatives (53,892): non-5 images jo sahi tareeke se non-5 classify hui.
  • False positives (687): non-5 images jo galti se 5 classify hui (type I errors).
  • False negatives (1,891): 5s ki images jo galti se non-5 classify hui (type II errors).
  • True positives (3,530): 5s ki images jo sahi tareeke se 5 classify hui.

Perfect classifier ki confusion matrix me nonzero values sirf main diagonal par hongi. Har row ek actual class hai, har column ek predicted class hai.

Precision aur recall — dono saath me dekho

  • Precision = TP / (TP + FP) — jab classifier kehta hai image 5 hai, to kitni baar woh sahi hota hai. Yahan 3,530 / (687 + 3,530) = 83.7%.
  • Recall (sensitivity ya true positive rate bhi kehte hain) = TP / (TP + FN) — saare 5s me se kitne percent detect hue. Yahan 3,530 / (1,891 + 3,530) = 65.1%.
  • F1 score = precision aur recall ka harmonic mean — 2 × precision × recall / (precision + recall). Yahan 0.73. Harmonic mean low values ko zyada weight deta hai, to F1 tabhi high hoga jab precision aur recall dono high hon.

Precision akele kaafi nahi: ek classifier jo sirf ek hi positive prediction kare (jis par use sabse zyada confidence ho) aur woh sahi ho, uski precision 100% hogi — lekin woh bekaar hai, kyunki usne baaki saare positives ignore kar diye. Isliye precision hamesha recall ke saath use hoti hai.

GitHub: 03_classification.ipynb

Code: <Confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1> — GitHub
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_predict
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, precision_score, recall_score, f1_score

y_train_pred = cross_val_predict(sgd_clf, X_train, y_train_5, cv=3)

cm = confusion_matrix(y_train_5, y_train_pred)
# array([[53892,   687],
#        [ 1891, 3530]])

precision_score(y_train_5, y_train_pred)  # 0.837
recall_score(y_train_5, y_train_pred)     # 0.651
f1_score(y_train_5, y_train_pred)         # 0.733

Precision/recall trade-off — threshold ka khel

SGDClassifier har instance ke liye ek decision score compute karta hai. Score threshold se zyada ho to positive class, warna negative. Threshold badhao to precision badhti hai (kam false positives) lekin recall girti hai (zyada false negatives). Threshold ghatao to ulta hota hai. Dono ek saath nahi badh sakte — yahi precision/recall trade-off hai.

Scikit-Learn threshold seedha set nahi karne deta, lekin decision_function() se scores mil jaate hain. precision_recall_curve() se saare possible thresholds ke liye precision aur recall nikaal kar plot karo. 90% precision chahiye to sabse chhota aisa threshold dhoondho: yahan threshold lagbhag 3,370 nikla — precision 90%, lekin recall sirf 48%! Isliye jab koi kahe "99% precision chahiye", to pehla sawaal hona chahiye: "kis recall par?"

Trade-off project par depend karta hai: bachchon ke liye safe videos detect karni hon to high precision chahiye (kuch achhi videos reject ho jaayein, chalega — lekin ek bhi kharab video na aaye). Surveillance images me shoplifters pakadne hon to 30% precision bhi chalegi agar recall 99% ho — security guards ko kuch false alerts milenge, lekin lagbhag saare shoplifters pakde jaayenge.

ROC curve aur AUC — classifier compare karna

ROC curve precision/recall curve jaisi hai, lekin yeh true positive rate (recall) ko false positive rate (FPR) ke against plot karti hai. FPR = galti se positive classify kiye gaye negative instances ka ratio = 1 − specificity (true negative rate). Random classifier ki ROC curve diagonal line hoti hai; achha classifier usse jitna door top-left corner ki taraf ho, utna behtar.

Classifiers compare karne ka ek tareeka hai area under the curve (AUC): perfect classifier ka ROC AUC 1 hota hai, purely random ka 0.5. SGD 5-detector ka ROC AUC 0.9605 nikla.

Kaunsi curve use karein? Rule of thumb: jab positive class rare ho, ya false positives false negatives se zyada matter karte hon, to PR curve prefer karo — warna ROC curve. ROC curve dekh kar classifier bahut achha lag sakta hai, jabki PR curve saaf dikhata hai ki improvement ki gunjaish hai.

Random forest vs SGD — comparison

RandomForestClassifier ka decision_function() nahi hota, lekin predict_proba() hota hai — positive class ki probability ko score ki tarah use karo. Uski PR curve SGD se bahut behtar hai — top-right corner ke zyada kareeb. Numbers: F1 score 0.924, ROC AUC 0.9983, precision lagbhag 99.1% aur recall lagbhag 86.6%. Bahut achha!

Ek warning: yeh estimated probabilities hain, actual probabilities nahi. Model overconfident ya underconfident ho sakta hai. sklearn.calibration package se estimated probabilities ko calibrate karke actual ke kareeb laaya ja sakta hai.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← Previous03.1 · MNIST aur Binary Classifier: 5-Detector→ Next03.3 · Multiclass, Multilabel aur Multioutput Classification
03.3Chapter 3 · Classification

Multiclass, Multilabel aur Multioutput Classification

Ab tak sirf do classes thi — 5 ya non-5. Ab saare 10 digits (0 se 9) classify karenge, phir woh cases dekhenge jahan ek instance ko multiple labels milte hain, ya output khud ek poori image hoti hai.

Multiclass classification — OvR vs OvO

Multiclass (multinomial) classifiers do se zyada classes distinguish karte hain. Kuch Scikit-Learn classifiers (jaise LogisticRegression, RandomForestClassifier) multiple classes natively handle karte hain. Doosre strictly binary hote hain (jaise SGDClassifier, SVC) — unke liye do strategies hain:

  • One-versus-the-rest (OvR / OvA): har digit ke liye ek binary classifier train karo — 10 digits ke liye 10 classifiers. Nayi image classify karni ho to har classifier ka decision score lo, aur jis class ka score sabse zyada ho, use chuno.
  • One-versus-one (OvO): har pair ke liye ek binary classifier — N classes ke liye N × (N − 1) / 2 classifiers. MNIST ke liye 45 classifiers! Image classify karni ho to saare 45 classifiers se guzaro, aur jo class sabse zyada duels jeete, use chuno. OvO ka faayda: har classifier sirf un do classes wale training data par train hota hai — jo algorithms training set size ke saath poorly scale karte hain (jaise SVM), unke liye OvO faster hota hai.

Scikit-Learn khud detect karta hai jab binary algorithm ko multiclass task par use kiya jaaye, aur algorithm ke hisaab se OvR ya OvO chunta hai. SVC (support vector machine classifier) pehle 2,000 images par train kiya gaya — 45 binary classifiers train hue, aur pehli image ko sahi '5' predict kiya. decision_function() se 10 scores milte hain — har class ko jeete hue duels ki count ke barabar score, plus ties todne ke liye chhota sa tweak. Sabse zyada score (9.3) class 5 ka tha.

Force karna ho to OneVsOneClassifier ya OneVsRestClassifier classes use karo — kisi bhi classifier ko wrap karke.

GitHub: 03_classification.ipynb

Code: <SVC se multiclass, OvO strategy> — GitHub
from sklearn.svm import SVC

svm_clf = SVC(random_state=42)
svm_clf.fit(X_train[:2000], y_train[:2000])  # y_train, not y_train_5

svm_clf.predict([some_digit])  # array(['5'], dtype=object)

some_digit_scores = svm_clf.decision_function([some_digit])
class_id = some_digit_scores.argmax()  # 5
svm_clf.classes_[class_id]  # '5'

SGD multiclass aur error analysis

SGDClassifier ko multiclass data par train karo to Scikit-Learn under the hood OvR use karta hai — 10 binary classifiers. Cross-validation accuracy lagbhag 87% (random classifier sirf 10% deta). Inputs ko scale karne se (StandardScaler) accuracy 89% se upar chali jaati hai.

Ab errors analyze karo: 10 classes ki confusion matrix bahut badi hoti hai, to ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_predictions() se colored diagram banao. Row se normalize karo (normalize="true") to har class ki sahi percentage dikhe: sirf 82% 5s sahi classify hue — sabse common error tha 5s ko 8s samajhna (10% 5s). Lekin confusion matrices generally symmetrical nahi hoti — sirf 2% 8s ko 5s samjha gaya.

Errors ko highlight karne ke liye correct predictions ko zero weight do (sample_weight) — tab column 8 bahut bright dikhta hai: lagbhag har class ki sabse common galti 8s banna hai. Percentages interpret karte waqt dhyaan rakho: errors-only diagram me row 7, column 9 ka 36% matlab yeh nahi ki 36% 7s ko 9s samjha gaya — matlab hai ki 7s par hui errors me se 36% 9s banna tha. Asliyat me sirf 3% 7s ko 9s samjha gaya.

Insights se improvements dhoondho: jo digits 8 jaise dikhte hain unka zyada training data jama karo, naye features engineer karo (jaise closed loops ginna — 8 me do hote hain, 6 me ek, 5 me zero), ya images preprocess karo. Individual errors dekhna bhi useful hai: 3s aur 5s ka confusion isliye hota hai kyunki SGDClassifier sirf ek linear model hai — har pixel ko har class ke liye ek weight deta hai, aur 3s aur 5s sirf kuch pixels se alag hote hain. Yeh classifier image shifting aur rotation ke prati sensitive hai. Simple fix hai data augmentation — training images ki shifted aur rotated copies add karna, taaki model aisi variations tolerate karna seekh le.

Multilabel classification — ek instance, multiple labels

Kabhi kabhi ek instance ko multiple classes milte hain. Jaise face-recognition classifier ek photo me kai log pehchan sakta hai — har pehchane gaye shakhs ke liye ek tag. Aise system ko multilabel classification kehte hain.

Simple example: har digit image ke liye do labels — digit bada hai ya nahi (7, 8, ya 9), aur digit odd hai ya nahi. KNeighborsClassifier multilabel support karta hai (saare classifiers nahi karte). Digit 5 ke liye prediction [False, True] aayi — bada nahi, odd hai — bilkul sahi!

Evaluate karne ka ek tareeka: har label ke liye F1 score nikaalo, phir average karo. Macro average (average="macro") se 0.976 aaya — saare labels equally important maane gaye. Agar ek label ke instances zyada hon, to average="weighted" se har label ko uske support (instances ki count) ke hisaab se weight diya jaata hai.

Jo classifier multilabel natively support nahi karta (jaise SVC), uske liye har label par ek model train kiya ja sakta hai — lekin isse labels ke beech dependencies capture nahi hoti. Jaise bada digit odd hone ki probability do guna zyada hai. Solution hai models ko chain me organize karna: har model input features ke saath-saath chain me pehle wale models ki predictions bhi use kare. Scikit-Learn ka ClassifierChain yahi karta hai.

GitHub: 03_classification.ipynb

Code: <KNN se multilabel classification> — GitHub
import numpy as np
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

y_train_large = (y_train >= '7')
y_train_odd = (y_train.astype('int8') % 2 == 1)
y_multilabel = np.c_[y_train_large, y_train_odd]

knn_clf = KNeighborsClassifier()
knn_clf.fit(X_train, y_multilabel)
knn_clf.predict([some_digit])  # array([[False, True]])

Multioutput classification — output bhi ek image

Aakhri type hai multioutput–multiclass classification: multilabel ka generalization, jahan har label multiclass ho sakta hai (do se zyada possible values). Example: images se noise hatana — input ek noisy digit image, output ek clean digit image (pixel intensities ka array). Har pixel ek label hai, aur har label ki values 0 se 255 tak ho sakti hain — to yeh multioutput system hai.

Training set banao: MNIST images me NumPy ke randint() se random noise (0–100) add karo; target images original images hain. Phir KNeighborsClassifier train karo aur noisy test image ko clean karo — result target ke bahut kareeb aata hai.

Note: classification aur regression ke beech line kabhi kabhi blurry hoti hai — pixel intensity predict karna arguably regression jaisa hai. Aur multioutput systems sirf classification tak limited nahi — ek system multiple labels output kar sakta hai, jinme class labels aur value labels dono hon.

Iske saath classification ka tour khatam hota hai: sahi metrics chunna, precision/recall trade-off set karna, classifiers compare karna, aur alag-alag tasks ke liye achhe classification systems banana — ab aap yeh sab jaante hain.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← Previous03.2 · Confusion Matrix, Precision-Recall aur ROC Curve→ Next04.1 · Linear Regression aur Normal Equation
04.1Chapter 4 · Training Models

Linear Regression aur Normal Equation

Linear regression sabse simple model hai — prediction sirf input features ka weighted sum hota hai, plus ek bias term. Is section mein samjhenge ki model ka matlab kya hai, cost function kaise measure karta hai ki model kitna achha fit hua, aur Normal Equation se best parameters seedha kaise nikaale jaate hain.

Linear model kya karta hai

Ek linear model prediction is tarah banata hai: har feature ko ek weight se multiply karo, sabko jod do, aur upar se bias term jod do. Formula hai: prediction = bias + weight1 × feature1 + weight2 × feature2 ... aur aise hi aage.

  • Bias term wo constant hai jo model ko upar-neeche shift karne deta hai, chahe saare features zero hon.
  • Weights batate hain ki har feature prediction ko kitna strongly aur kis direction mein affect karta hai.
  • Vector wali notation mein ye sirf do vectors ka dot product hai — parameters ka vector aur features ka vector.
  • Training ka matlab hai: wo weights aur bias dhoondhna jisse model training data par sabse achha fit ho.

Cost function: MSE

Fit ko measure karne ke liye sabse common tareeka hai Mean Squared Error (MSE) — har prediction ki galti ko square karke unka average. Training ka goal hai wo parameters dhoondhna jo MSE ko minimum kar dein.

  • RMSE ke bajay MSE minimize karna aasan hai, aur result same hi milta hai.
  • Ek important baat: training ke time jo loss optimize hota hai, wo final evaluation metric se alag ho sakta hai — loss aisa hona chahiye jo optimize karna aasan ho aur metric se closely juda ho.

Normal Equation: seedha jawab

Normal Equation ek closed-form solution hai — matlab ek seedha mathematical formula jo best parameters ek hi baar mein nikaal deta hai, bina iterative training ke. Ye MSE ko minimize karne wala parameter vector deta hai.

  • Scikit-Learn ka LinearRegression class iske liye SVD (singular value decomposition) par based pseudoinverse use karta hai.
  • Pseudoinverse wala tareeka Normal Equation se zyada efficient hai, aur edge cases bhi handle kar leta hai — jaise jab matrix invertible na ho, ya features redundant hon, ya instances se zyada features hon.
  • Scikit-Learn bias ko alag rakhta hai: intercept_ mein bias, aur coef_ mein feature weights.

Complexity: kab ye tareeka slow padta hai

Normal Equation mein ek matrix ko invert karna padta hai, jiska cost features ki ginti ke saath tezi se badhta hai — features double karo to time lagbhag 5 se 8 guna badh jaata hai. SVD wala tareeka lagbhag 4 guna badhta hai.

  • Dono tareeke training instances ki ginti ke saath linear hain — bada training set handle kar lete hain, bas memory mein fit hona chahiye.
  • Features bahut zyada hon (jaise 1,00,000) to dono hi bahut slow ho jaate hain — tab gradient descent behtar hai.
  • Ek baar model train ho jaaye to prediction bahut fast hoti hai — instances aur features dono ke saath linear.

GitHub: 04_training_linear_models.ipynb

Code: Normal Equation se theta nikaalna — GitHub
from sklearn.preprocessing import add_dummy_feature

X_b = add_dummy_feature(X)  # add x0 = 1 to each instance
theta_best = np.linalg.inv(X_b.T @ X_b) @ X_b.T @ y
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← Previous03.3 · Multiclass, Multilabel aur Multioutput Classification→ Next04.2 · Gradient Descent: Batch, Stochastic aur Mini-Batch
04.2Chapter 4 · Training Models

Gradient Descent: Batch, Stochastic aur Mini-Batch

Gradient descent ek generic optimization algorithm hai jo parameters ko dheere-dheere tweak karke cost function ko minimize karta hai. Iske teen versions hain — batch, stochastic aur mini-batch — aur inka farq samajhna neural networks ke liye bhi zaroori hai.

Gradient descent ka idea

Soch lo tum ghane kohre mein pahad par kho gaye ho aur sirf apne pairon ke neeche dhalaan mehsoos kar sakte ho. Neeche pahunchne ka best tareeka hai sabse tez dhalaan ki direction mein neeche chalna. Gradient descent bilkul yehi karta hai: cost function ka gradient measure karta hai aur uske opposite direction mein ek chhota step leta hai.

  • Parameters ko random values se start kiya jaata hai — isse random initialization kehte hain.
  • Har step mein cost function thoda kam hone ki koshish hoti hai, jab tak algorithm minimum par converge na kar jaaye.
  • Gradient zero ho jaaye to samjho minimum par pahunch gaye.

Learning rate: sabse important hyperparameter

Har step ka size learning rate se decide hota hai. Ye galat set ho to sab kharab ho sakta hai.

  • Learning rate bahut chhota ho to algorithm converge to karega, lekin bahut saare iterations lagenge — time waste hoga.
  • Learning rate bahut bada ho to algorithm valley ke doosri taraf jump kar jaayega, aur diverge karke solution se door bhaag sakta hai.
  • Achha learning rate dhoondhne ke liye grid search use kar sakte ho, lekin epochs ki limit rakhna taaki slow models jaldi eliminate ho jaayein.
  • Epochs ki ginti bhi matter karti hai: bahut kam ho to solution se door ruk jaoge, bahut zyada ho to time waste hoga jab parameters badal hi nahi rahe.

MSE convex hai — ye khushkhabri hai

Linear regression ka MSE cost function convex hota hai — matlab iska shape ek katora jaisa hai, jisme koi local minimum nahi, sirf ek global minimum hai. Isliye gradient descent (sahi learning rate ke saath) global minimum ke kareeb pahunchne ki guarantee deta hai.

  • Lekin agar features ke scales bahut alag hon to katora lamba-kheenchha (elongated) ho jaata hai aur convergence slow ho jaati hai.
  • Isliye gradient descent use karne se pehle saare features ka scale similar rakhna chahiye — jaise StandardScaler se.
  • Training ka matlab hi hai parameter space mein us combination ko dhoondhna jo cost function ko minimize kare.

Batch gradient descent

Batch gradient descent har step mein poore training set par gradients compute karta hai. Gradient vector mein har parameter ke liye partial derivative hoti hai — matlab wo parameter thoda badalne se cost kitna badlega.

  • Gradient uphill point karta hai, isliye usse ulta jaana hota hai: naya parameter = purana parameter − learning rate × gradient.
  • Poora training set har step mein use hota hai, isliye bahut bade dataset par ye bahut slow hai.
  • Lekin features ki ginti ke saath ye achha scale karta hai — lakhon features hon to bhi Normal Equation se fast hai.
  • Training set par ek poora pass ek epoch kehlata hai.

GitHub: 04_training_linear_models.ipynb

Code: Batch gradient descent — GitHub
eta = 0.1  # learning rate
n_epochs = 1000
m = len(X_b)  # number of instances

np.random.seed(42)
theta = np.random.randn(2, 1)  # randomly initialized model parameters

for epoch in range(n_epochs):
    gradients = 2 / m * X_b.T @ (X_b @ theta - y)
    theta = theta - eta * gradients

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD)

Batch GD ka main problem hai ki har step mein poora training set chahiye. Stochastic GD iske bilkul opposite hai: har step mein sirf ek random instance lekar usi par gradients compute karta hai.

  • Har step bahut fast hota hai aur ek time par sirf ek instance memory mein chahiye — isliye bahut bade dataset par bhi train kar sakte ho, jo memory mein fit bhi na ho.
  • Nuqsan ye hai ki cost function seedha neeche nahi jaata — upar-neeche bounce karta hai, sirf average mein kam hota hai.
  • Minimum ke kareeb pahunch kar bhi ye bounce karta rehta hai, kabhi settle nahi hota — final parameters achhe hote hain, lekin optimal nahi.
  • Randomness ka ek faayda bhi hai: irregular cost function mein ye local minimum se jump karke bahar nikal sakta hai.
  • Is dilemma ka hal hai learning schedule — learning rate ko dheere-dheere kam karna, taaki steps pehle bade hon (fast progress, local minima se escape) aur baad mein chhote (minimum par settle).
  • SGD ke liye training instances ka independent aur identically distributed (IID) hona zaroori hai, warna parameters global optimum ki taraf nahi kheenche jaayenge.

GitHub: 04_training_linear_models.ipynb

Code: Stochastic GD with learning schedule — GitHub
n_epochs = 50
t0, t1 = 5, 50  # learning schedule hyperparameters

def learning_schedule(t):
    return t0 / (t + t1)

np.random.seed(42)
theta = np.random.randn(2, 1)  # random initialization

for epoch in range(n_epochs):
    for iteration in range(m):
        random_index = np.random.randint(m)
        xi = X_b[random_index : random_index + 1]
        yi = y[random_index : random_index + 1]
        gradients = 2 * xi.T @ (xi @ theta - yi)  # for SGD, do not divide by m
        eta = learning_schedule(epoch * m + iteration)
        theta = theta - eta * gradients

Mini-batch gradient descent

Mini-batch GD beech ka rasta hai: har step mein poora training set nahi, sirf ek chhota random set (mini-batch) use hota hai.

  • Stochastic GD se iska faayda hai ki matrix operations ka hardware optimization milta hai, khaas taur par GPU par — performance boost milta hai.
  • Parameter space mein iski progress stochastic GD se kam erratic hoti hai, khaas taur par jab mini-batch kaafi bada ho.
  • Lekin local minima se bach nikalna iske liye thoda mushkil ho sakta hai, kyunki randomness kam hoti hai.
  • Teeno algorithms end mein lagbhag same model par pahunchte hain — farq sirf training ke tareeke aur speed ka hai.
  • Scikit-Learn mein SGDRegressor stochastic GD implement karta hai, aur partial_fit() se incremental learning kar sakte ho — ek ya kuch instances par ek round training.
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← Previous04.1 · Linear Regression aur Normal Equation→ Next04.3 · Polynomial Regression, Learning Curves aur Regularization
04.3Chapter 4 · Training Models

Polynomial Regression, Learning Curves aur Regularization

Seedhi line se complex data fit nahi hota — iske liye polynomial features add karte hain. Lekin zyada complex model overfit karne lagta hai. Is section mein seekhenge ki overfitting aur underfitting ko learning curves se kaise pehchana jaaye, aur ridge, lasso, elastic net aur early stopping se model ko kaise control kiya jaaye.

Polynomial regression: linear model se nonlinear fit

Polynomial regression mein har feature ki powers (square, cube, ...) ko naye features ki tarah add kar diya jaata hai, aur phir usi par linear model train hota hai. Model abhi bhi linear hi hai — bas features badh gaye hain.

  • Ek se zyada features hon to polynomial features unke combinations bhi add karta hai — jaise do features a aur b hon to ab, a²b aur ab² bhi banenge.
  • Savdhaan raho: features ki ginti combinatorial explosion se badhti hai — degree badhate hi features bahut zyada ho jaate hain.
  • Degree 300 jaisa bahut high polynomial training data ko bilkul chipak kar fit kar leta hai — wiggle kar karke har point ke paas se guzarta hai. Ye severe overfitting hai.

GitHub: 04_training_linear_models.ipynb

Code: Polynomial features aur linear fit — GitHub
from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures

poly_features = PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, include_bias=False)
X_poly = poly_features.fit_transform(X)

lin_reg = LinearRegression()
lin_reg.fit(X_poly, y)
lin_reg.intercept_, lin_reg.coef_

Learning curves: underfitting vs overfitting pehchano

Learning curves training error aur validation error ko training set ke size ke function ke roop mein plot karti hain. Inka shape bata deta hai ki model underfit kar raha hai ya overfit.

  • Underfitting wale model mein dono curves ek plateau par pahunch jaati hain — paas-paas aur kaafi upar. Aur training data add karne se kuch nahi hoga; behtar model ya behtar features chahiye.
  • Overfitting wale model mein training error bahut kam hoti hai, lekin curves ke beech gap hota hai — model training data par validation se behtar perform karta hai.
  • Overfitting ko kam karne ka ek tareeka hai aur training data dena, jab tak validation error training error ke kareeb na aa jaaye.
  • Scikit-Learn ka learning_curve() function cross-validation ke saath ye curves banane mein madad karta hai.

Bias/variance trade-off

Generalization error teen hisson se banta hai — bias, variance aur irreducible error.

  • Bias galat assumptions ki wajah se hota hai — jaise data ko linear maan lena jab wo asal mein quadratic ho. High-bias model underfit karta hai.
  • Variance model ki training data ke chhote changes ke prati sensitivity hai. Zyada degrees of freedom wala model (jaise high-degree polynomial) high variance rakhta hai aur overfit karta hai.
  • Irreducible error data ke noise ki wajah se hota hai — ise sirf data saaf karke kam kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Model ki complexity badhao to variance badhta hai aur bias kam hota hai — aur ulta bhi. Isi ko trade-off kehte hain.

Ridge regression

Ridge regression linear regression ka regularized version hai: MSE mein ek penalty add hoti hai jo weights ke square ke sum par based hoti hai. Isse learning algorithm ko sirf data fit nahi karna padta, weights ko chhota bhi rakhna padta hai.

  • Hyperparameter alpha control karta hai ki kitni regularization ho. Alpha zero ho to ye plain linear regression hai; bahut bada ho to saare weights zero ke kareeb aur prediction ek flat line ban jaati hai.
  • Bias term ko regularize nahi kiya jaata — sirf feature weights ko.
  • Alpha badhane se predictions flat aur reasonable hoti jaati hain — variance kam, bias zyada.
  • Regularized models se pehle data ko scale karna bahut zaroori hai, kyunki ye feature scales ke prati sensitive hote hain.
  • Ridge ko closed-form equation se bhi train kar sakte ho, ya gradient descent se bhi.

GitHub: 04_training_linear_models.ipynb

Code: Ridge regression — GitHub
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge

ridge_reg = Ridge(alpha=0.1, solver="cholesky")
ridge_reg.fit(X, y)
ridge_reg.predict([[1.5]])

from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso

lasso_reg = Lasso(alpha=0.1)
lasso_reg.fit(X, y)
lasso_reg.predict([[1.5]])

from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet

elastic_net = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, l1_ratio=0.5)
elastic_net.fit(X, y)
elastic_net.predict([[1.5]])

Lasso regression: feature selection free mein

Lasso bhi regularized linear regression hai, lekin ye weights ke square ke bajay unke absolute values ka sum penalty mein use karta hai.

  • Lasso ki sabse badi khaasiyat: ye kam important features ke weights ko bilkul zero kar deta hai — matlab automatic feature selection, aur ek sparse model milta hai.
  • Geometry ki wajah se ye hota hai: lasso ka penalty gradient ko axis ki taraf kheenchta hai, jahan ek weight zero ho jaata hai.
  • Ridge mein aisa nahi hota — weights zero ke kareeb aate hain, lekin kabhi poori tarah zero nahi hote.
  • Lasso ke saath gradient descent end mein optimum ke aas-paas bounce karta hai, isliye learning rate ko dheere-dheere kam karna padta hai.
  • Lasso ka cost function zero par differentiable nahi hota, lekin subgradient use karke gradient descent phir bhi kaam karta hai.

Elastic net: dono ka beech ka rasta

Elastic net ridge aur lasso ka mix hai — regularization term dono penalties ka weighted sum hota hai, aur mix ratio se control hota hai kaunsa kitna ho.

  • Mix ratio zero ho to ye ridge ke barabar hai, ek ho to lasso ke barabar.
  • Aam taur par thodi regularization hamesha behtar hoti hai — plain linear regression se bacho.
  • Ridge ek achha default hai, lekin agar lagta hai ki sirf kuch features kaam ke hain to lasso ya elastic net behtar hai.
  • Elastic net ko lasso se prefer kiya jaata hai jab features ki ginti training instances se zyada ho, ya kai features aapas mein strongly correlated hon — in cases mein lasso erratic behave kar sakta hai.

Early stopping: muft ki regularization

Early stopping ek bilkul alag tareeka hai: iterative training ko usi waqt rok do jab validation error minimum par pahunch jaaye. Uske baad training jaari rakho to model overfit karne lagta hai — validation error wapas upar jaane lagti hai.

  • Ye itni simple aur effective technique hai ki ise ek mashhoor researcher ne "beautiful free lunch" kaha tha.
  • Stochastic aur mini-batch GD mein curves smooth nahi hoti, isliye rukne ka faisla tab lo jab validation error kuch time se minimum se upar ho — phir parameters ko us point par wapas le aao jahan validation error minimum thi.
