09.2Chapter 9 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

DBSCAN aur Clustering ke Applications

k-means har cluster ko gol blob maanta hai. DBSCAN bilkul alag approach leta hai — wo high-density regions ko cluster maanta hai, isliye kisi bhi shape ke clusters dhoondh sakta hai aur outliers ko alag pehchan sakta hai.

DBSCAN kaise kaam karta hai

DBSCAN ka full form hai density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise. Ye clusters ko continuous high-density regions ke roop me define karta hai.

  • Har instance ke liye algorithm gin ta hai ki usse chhoti distance ε (epsilon) ke andar kitne instances hain — is region ko instance ka ε-neighbourhood kehte hain.
  • Agar kisi instance ke ε-neighbourhood me kam se kam min_samples instances hain (khud ko mila kar), to wo core instance hai — matlab wo dense region me hai.
  • Core instance ke neighbourhood ke saare instances usi cluster ke hote hain. Neighbourhood me dusre core instances bhi ho sakte hain, isliye neighbouring core instances ki lambi chain ek hi cluster ban jaati hai.
  • Jo instance core instance nahi hai aur uske neighbourhood me koi core instance bhi nahi hai, wo anomaly mana jaata hai.
  • Ye algorithm tab achha kaam karta hai jab saare clusters low-density regions se achhi tarah separated hon.

DBSCAN Scikit-Learn me

Moons dataset par DBSCAN chalao to eps ka value bahut matter karta hai.

  • eps=0.05 par bahut saare anomalies aur saat alag clusters mile — disappointing result.
  • eps ko 0.2 tak badhane par clustering perfect dikhi — do moons sahi se mile.
  • Anomalies ka cluster index −1 hota hai (labels_ me). Core instances ke indices core_sample_indices_ me aur core instances khud components_ me milte hain.
  • Important: DBSCAN class me predict() method nahi hai — sirf fit_predict() hai. Naye instance ka cluster predict karne ke liye khud ek classifier train karo, jaise KNeighborsClassifier ko core instances par train kar ke.
  • KNeighborsClassifier ki kneighbors() method se nearest neighbour ki distance bhi milti hai — maximum distance set karke door wale instances ko anomaly declare kar sakte ho.
  • DBSCAN simple lekin powerful hai — kisi bhi sankhya ke, kisi bhi shape ke clusters identify kar sakta hai, outliers ke prati robust hai, aur sirf do hyperparameters hain (eps aur min_samples).
  • Limitations: agar clusters ki density bahut alag-alag ho ya kisi cluster ke aas-paas low-density region na ho, to DBSCAN struggle karta hai. Computational complexity lagbhag O(m²n) hai, isliye bade datasets par achhe se scale nahi karta.

Clustering se image segmentation

Image segmentation ka matlab hai image ko multiple segments me baantna. Teen variants hain:

  • Color segmentation: similar color wale pixels ek hi segment me — jaise satellite images me forest area measure karna.
  • Semantic segmentation: same object type ke saare pixels ek segment me — jaise self-driving car me saare pedestrians ek segment me.
  • Instance segmentation: same individual object ke pixels ek segment me — har pedestrian ka alag segment.
  • Semantic ya instance segmentation ka state of the art aaj convolutional neural networks se milta hai, lekin color segmentation k-means se aasani se hoti hai.
  • Image ko pixels ki list me reshape karo (har pixel ek RGB vector hai), phir k-means se colors cluster karo — jaise 8 clusters. Har pixel ka color uske cluster ke mean color se replace kar do.
  • Clusters kam ho to chhote lekin flashy rang ko apna cluster nahi milta — jaise ladybug ka laal rang environment ke rangon me merge ho gaya, kyunki k-means similar sizes ke clusters prefer karta hai.

Clustering se semi-supervised learning

Jab labeled instances bahut kam aur unlabeled bahut zyada hon, to clustering bahut kaam aati hai. Digits dataset par experiment dekho — 1,797 grayscale 8 × 8 digit images.

  • Sirf 50 labeled instances par logistic regression train karo to test accuracy sirf 74.8% milti hai. Full training set par wahi model 90.7% deta hai.
  • Training set ko 50 clusters me baanto aur har cluster me centroid ke sabse kareeb image nikalo — inhe representative images kehte hain.
  • Sirf in 50 representative images ko manually label karke train karo to accuracy 84.9% ho jaati hai — random 50 instances ki jagah representative instances label karna bahut faydemand hai.
  • Label propagation: har cluster ke representative image ka label us cluster ke saare instances ko de do — accuracy 89.4% ho gayi.
  • Ek kadam aur: har cluster me centroid se sabse door 1% instances ko hata do (outliers eliminate) — accuracy 90.9% ho gayi, jo fully labeled dataset wale 90.7% se bhi thodi zyada hai!
  • Scikit-Learn me LabelSpreading aur LabelPropagation classes labels automatically propagate karti hain, aur SelfTrainingClassifier confident predictions se training set ko update karta rehta hai.
  • Active learning: human expert algorithm ke saath interact karke labels de — sabse common strategy uncertainty sampling hai: model jin instances par sabse uncertain ho, unhe expert ko label karne ke liye do, aur tab tak iterate karo jab tak fayda ho.

Dusre clustering algorithms

Scikit-Learn me aur bhi clustering algorithms hain — ek quick overview:

  • Agglomerative clustering: clusters ki hierarchy bottom-up banti hai — har iteration me nearest pair of clusters merge hote hain. Kisi bhi pairwise distance ke saath use ho sakta hai, aur cluster tree flexible aur informative hota hai.
  • BIRCH: bahut bade datasets ke liye design hua hai — batch k-means se tez ho sakta hai, similar results ke saath, jab features 20 se kam hon. Limited memory me huge datasets handle kar sakta hai.
  • Mean-shift: har instance par circle rakh kar use instances ke mean ki taraf shift karta hai, jab tak circles ruk na jaayein. Kisi bhi sankhya ke, kisi bhi shape ke clusters dhoondh sakta hai, lekin clusters ko tukdon me kaat deta hai jab unme internal density variations hon. Bade datasets ke liye suitable nahi hai.
  • Affinity propagation: instances ek dusre ko messages bhejte hain jab tak har instance ek representative (exemplar) elect na kar le. Clusters ki sankhya pehle se pick nahi karni padti — training ke dauraan decide hoti hai. Bade datasets par scale nahi karta.
  • Spectral clustering: instances ke beech similarity matrix se low-dimensional embedding banata hai, phir us space me dusra clustering algorithm (Scikit-Learn me k-means) chalata hai. Complex cluster structures capture kar sakta hai aur graphs ko cut karne ke liye use ho sakta hai.

GitHub: 09_unsupervised_learning.ipynb

Code: DBSCAN se moons dataset cluster karna — GitHub
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
from sklearn.datasets import make_moons

X, y = make_moons(n_samples=1000, noise=0.05, random_state=42)
dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=0.05, min_samples=5)
dbscan.fit(X)

09.3Chapter 9 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Gaussian Mixture Models aur Anomaly Detection

k-means gol clusters dhoondhta hai. Gaussian mixture model (GMM) ellipsoidal clusters dhoondhta hai — har cluster ka apna shape, size, density aur orientation ho sakta hai. Ye clustering ke saath-saath density estimation aur anomaly detection bhi karta hai.

Gaussian mixture model kya hai?

GMM ek probabilistic model hai jo assume karta hai ki instances kai Gaussian distributions ke mixture se generate hue hain, jinke parameters unknown hain.

  • Ek hi Gaussian distribution se generate hue saare instances ek cluster banate hain jo aam taur par ellipsoid jaisa dikhta hai.
  • Har cluster ka alag ellipsoidal shape, size, density aur orientation ho sakta hai — bilkul waise hi jaise k-means fail hua tha wale ellipsoidal blobs me.
  • Model me har instance ke liye pehle k clusters me se ek cluster randomly pick hota hai (cluster ka weight uski pick hone ki probability hai), phir instance us cluster ki Gaussian distribution se sample hota hai.
  • GaussianMixture class me tumhe pehle se clusters ki sankhya k batani hoti hai.

EM algorithm: expectation aur maximization

GaussianMixture class expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm par rely karti hai — iski k-means se bahut similarities hain.

  • Ye bhi cluster parameters ko randomly initialize karta hai, phir convergence tak do steps repeat karta hai.
  • Expectation step: har instance ko clusters assign karo — lekin hard assignment ki jagah soft assignment: har instance ke liye estimate karo ki wo har cluster se belong karne ki kitni probability rakhta hai.
  • Maximization step: har cluster ko dataset ke saare instances se update karo, har instance ko us probability se weight karke jo us cluster ke liye estimate hui thi. In probabilities ko clusters ki responsibilities kehte hain.
  • EM ko k-means ka generalization samjho — ye sirf cluster centers hi nahi dhoondhta, balki unki size, shape, orientation aur relative weights bhi dhoondhta hai.
  • k-means ki tarah EM bhi kharab solutions par converge kar sakta hai, isliye ise kai baar chalana chahiye aur sirf best solution rakhna chahiye — isliye n_init=10 set kiya gaya tha (default sirf 1 hai).
  • converged_ batata hai ki algorithm converge hua ya nahi, aur n_iter_ batata hai ki kitne iterations lage.

GMM se kya-kya kar sakte ho?

Ek baar cluster ke weights, means aur covariance matrices estimate ho jaayein, to model bahut kuch kar sakta hai.

  • Hard clustering: predict() se har instance ko sabse likely cluster assign karo. Soft clustering: predict_proba() se har cluster ki probability estimate karo.
  • Naye instances generate karna: GMM ek generative model hai — sample() method se naye instances sample kar sakte ho.
  • Density estimation: score_samples() method har instance ke liye us location par log probability density function (PDF) estimate karta hai — score zyada matlab density zyada.
  • Covariance constraints: covariance_type se clusters ke shapes limit kar sakte ho — "spherical" (saare clusters gol, alag diameters), "diag" (ellipsoidal lekin axes coordinate axes ke parallel), "tied" (saare clusters ka same shape, size aur orientation), aur default "full" (har cluster ka apna unconstrained covariance matrix).
  • Zyada dimensions, zyada clusters ya kam instances par EM ko optimal solution dhoondhne me struggle hota hai — covariance constraints se parameters kam karke task aasan kiya ja sakta hai.

GMM se anomaly detection

GMM se anomaly detection bahut simple hai — jo instance low-density region me ho, use anomaly mano.

  • Density threshold define karna hota hai. Example: defective products ka ratio 2% hai, to threshold aisi value set karo jisse 2% instances us threshold se neeche density me hon.
  • Zyada false positives hon to threshold kam karo; zyada false negatives hon to threshold badhao — ye usual precision/recall trade-off hai.
  • Novelty detection anomaly detection se alag hai — isme algorithm ko "clean" dataset par train kiya jaata hai jo outliers se contaminated nahi hai, jabki anomaly detection me ye assumption nahi hoti. Outlier detection aksar dataset clean up karne ke liye use hota hai.
  • Warning: GMM outliers samet saare data ko fit karne ki koshish karta hai — agar outliers bahut zyada hon to model ka "normality" ka view bias ho sakta hai. Solution: model ko ek baar fit karke sabse extreme outliers hatao, phir cleaned dataset par dobara fit karo.

Clusters ki sankhya kaise chune? BIC, AIC aur Bayesian GMM

k-means me inertia ya silhouette score use hota tha, lekin Gaussian mixtures me ye metrics reliable nahi hain kyunki clusters spherical nahi hote ya alag sizes ke hote hain.

  • BIC (Bayesian information criterion) aur AIC (Akaike information criterion): dono aise models ko penalize karte hain jinke parameters zyada hon (jaise zyada clusters) aur aise models ko reward karte hain jo data ko achhe se fit karein. Dono aksar same model select karte hain; jab differ karein to BIC simpler model select karta hai.
  • bic() aur aic() methods se values nikal sakte ho — example me dono k=3 par sabse kam the, isliye wahi best choice thi.
  • Likelihood vs probability: probability batati hai ki future outcome kitna plausible hai (parameters pata hon to), jabki likelihood batati hai ki parameters ki values kitni plausible hain (outcome pata ho to). Likelihood ko maximize karna hi log likelihood maximize karne ke barabar hai, aur log likelihood maximize karna aasan hota hai kyunki products sums me badal jaate hain.
  • BayesianGaussianMixture: optimal clusters ki sankhya manually dhoondhne ki jagah, ye class unnecessary clusters ko khud zero (ya zero ke kareeb) weight de deti hai. n_components ko optimal se bada value set karo (jaise 10), aur algorithm khud detect karega ki sirf 3 clusters chahiye — weights [0.4, 0.21, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] mile.
  • Limitation: GMM ellipsoidal shapes par great kaam karta hai, lekin bahut alag shapes wale clusters par nahi — moons dataset par Bayesian GMM ne do moons ki jagah aath clusters dhoondhe, kyunki wo ellipsoids dhoondh raha tha.

Anomaly aur novelty detection ke dusre algorithms

Scikit-Learn me anomaly ya novelty detection ke liye aur bhi algorithms hain:

  • EllipticEnvelope (Fast-MCD): outlier detection ke liye useful, khaas taur par dataset clean up karne ke liye. Assume karta hai ki normal instances ek hi Gaussian distribution se aaye hain, aur Gaussian ke parameters estimate karte waqt outliers ko ignore karta hai.
  • Isolation forest: high-dimensional datasets me outlier detection ke liye efficient hai. Random forest banata hai jisme har tree randomly grow hota hai — anomalies dusre instances se door hote hain, isliye average me wo kam steps me isolate ho jaate hain.
  • Local outlier factor (LOF): kisi instance ke aas-paas ki density ko uske neighbours ke aas-paas ki density se compare karta hai — anomaly aksar apne k-nearest neighbours se zyada isolated hota hai.
  • One-class SVM: novelty detection ke liye behtar hai. High-dimensional space me instances ko origin se separate karne ki koshish karta hai — original space me ye ek chhota region banata hai jo saare instances ko cover kare. Jo naya instance is region me na aaye, wo anomaly hai. High-dimensional datasets par great kaam karta hai, lekin bade datasets par scale nahi karta.
  • PCA reconstruction error: normal instance ka reconstruction error anomaly ke comparison me aam taur par bahut kam hota hai — ye simple aur aksar kaafi efficient anomaly detection approach hai.

GitHub: 09_unsupervised_learning.ipynb

Code: Gaussian mixture model train karna — GitHub
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture

gm = GaussianMixture(n_components=3, n_init=10, random_state=42)
gm.fit(X)
Code: Bayesian GMM, clusters khud chunna — GitHub
from sklearn.mixture import BayesianGaussianMixture

bgm = BayesianGaussianMixture(n_components=10, n_init=10, random_state=42)
bgm.fit(X)
bgm.weights_.round(2)

10.1Chapter 10 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks with Keras

Perceptron aur TLU — Neural Network ki Shuruaat

Neural network ka idea dimaag se inspired hai — lekin aaj ke neural network biological dimaag ki copy nahi hain, ye apne aap mein ek powerful machine learning tool ban chuke hain. Is section mein hum sabse pehle aur sabse simple artificial neuron se shuru karte hain: perceptron.

Biological neuron se artificial neuron tak

Biological neuron mein dendrites se signal aata hai, cell body usko process karta hai, aur axon se signal aage jaata hai. Artificial neuron iska simplified version hai: ye inputs ka weighted sum nikaalta hai, usme bias jodta hai, aur phir ek activation function lagata hai.

  • Weighted sum: har input xi ko ek weight wi se multiply kiya jaata hai, phir sabko jodkar bias b add karte hain: z = w1x1 + w2x2 + ... + wnxn + b.
  • Activation function: is sum par ek function lagaya jaata hai jo final output decide karta hai. Perceptron mein ye ek step function hoti hai.
  • TLU: is artificial neuron ko threshold logic unit (TLU) kehte hain. Ye sirf 0 ya 1 (ya -1 ya +1) output karta hai — threshold cross hua to positive class, nahi to negative class.

Perceptron kya karta hai?

Ek perceptron ek ya zyada TLUs ki single layer hoti hai, jisme har TLU har input se connected hota hai. Aisi layer ko fully connected layer ya dense layer kehte hain.

  • Ek TLU: simple linear binary classification kar sakta hai — jaise iris flowers ko petal length aur width ke basis par alag karna.
  • Multiple TLUs: ek hi perceptron ek saath kai binary classes mein classify kar sakta hai — ye multilabel classifier bhi ban sakta hai, aur multiclass classification ke liye bhi use ho sakta hai.
  • Matrix form: poori layer ka output ek hi equation se nikalta hai: h(X) = activation(XW + b). Yahan X input matrix hai, W weight matrix hai, b bias vector hai.
  • Broadcasting: matrix mein vector add karna matlab har row mein wahi vector add karna — har neuron ka apna bias har instance par lagta hai.

Perceptron kaise seekhta hai?

Perceptron ek training instance ko ek baar mein dekhta hai, prediction karta hai, aur jahan galti hoti hai wahan weights ko correct karta hai. Jo connections sahi prediction mein help karte, unko mazboot kiya jaata hai; jo galat prediction ki taraf le jaate, unko kamzor kiya jaata hai.

  • Weight update rule: wi,j = wi,j + learning_rate × (target − prediction) × xi. Matlab galti jitni badi, update utna bada.
  • Convergence: agar training data linearly separable hai — matlab ek seedhi line (ya hyperplane) se classes alag ho sakti hain — to ye algorithm ek solution par converge karega.
  • Scikit-Learn mein: Perceptron class available hai, jo andar se SGDClassifier ke barabar hai (loss="perceptron", constant learning rate, koi regularization nahi).

Perceptron ki limit kya hai?

Har output neuron ki decision boundary linear hoti hai, isliye perceptron complex patterns nahi seekh sakta — jaise logistic regression nahi seekh sakta.

  • XOR problem: exclusive OR ek bahut simple problem hai jise koi bhi linear model solve nahi kar sakta — perceptron bhi nahi.
  • Probabilities nahi: perceptron class probability nahi deta, sirf hard 0/1 decision deta hai — is wajah se aksar logistic regression ko prefer kiya jaata hai.
  • Regularization nahi: by default koi regularization nahi hoti, aur training usi waqt ruk jaati hai jab training set par koi galti nahi bachti — isliye generalization aksar logistic regression ya linear SVM se kamzor hoti hai.
  • Solution: kai perceptrons ko stack karke multilayer perceptron (MLP) banao — MLP XOR problem solve kar sakta hai. Yehi agle section ka topic hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 10
← Previous09.3 · Gaussian Mixture Models aur Anomaly Detection→ Next10.2 · MLP, Backpropagation aur Activation Functions
10.2Chapter 10 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks with Keras

MLP, Backpropagation aur Activation Functions

Ek layer se kaam nahi chala, to layers ko stack kar diya — yahi multilayer perceptron (MLP) hai. Lekin itne saare weights ko train kaise karein? Iska jawab hai backpropagation, jo aaj deep learning ki sabse important training technique hai.

MLP ki architecture

MLP mein ek input layer, ek ya zyada hidden layers, aur ek output layer hoti hai. Input ke paas wali layers ko lower layers aur output ke paas wali ko upper layers kehte hain.

  • Feedforward network: signal sirf ek direction mein behta hai — input se output ki taraf. Isliye MLP ek feedforward neural network hai.
  • Deep neural network (DNN): jab hidden layers ka deep stack ho, to use DNN kehte hain. Deep learning isi ka study hai.
  • Hidden layers: ye network ko complex patterns seekhne ki taakat deti hain — har layer pichhli layer ke patterns par aur complex patterns banati hai.

Backpropagation kaise kaam karta hai?

Backpropagation do cheezon ka combination hai: reverse-mode autodiff (gradients ko efficiently compute karna) aur gradient descent (weights ko update karna). Ye ek mini-batch par ek baar mein kaam karta hai, aur poora training set kai baar dekha jaata hai — har poora pass ek epoch kehlata hai.

  1. Forward pass: mini-batch input layer se daalo, har layer ka output compute karo aur aage bhejo, jab tak output layer ka output na mil jaaye. Beech ke saare intermediate results save rakho — backward pass mein chahiye honge.
  2. Error measure karo: loss function se dekho desired output aur actual output mein kitna farak hai.
  3. Backward pass: chain rule use karke peeche ki taraf jaao — pehle output layer ke connections ka error contribution nikaalo, phir usse neeche wali layer ka, aur aise hi input layer tak.
  4. Gradient descent step: jo gradients mile, unse saare weights aur biases ko tweak karo taaki error kam ho.

Random initialization zaroori hai: agar saare weights zero se initialize kar doge, to ek layer ke saare neurons bilkul identical rahenge, aur backpropagation unko hamesha ek jaisa hi update karega — poora layer ek hi neuron jaisa behave karega. Random weights se symmetry toot-ti hai aur har neuron alag cheez seekh pata hai.

Activation function kyun zaroori hai?

Agar layers ke beech koi nonlinearity na ho, to kitni bhi deep stack ek hi linear transformation ke barabar hoti hai — jaise f(x) = 2x + 3 aur g(x) = 5x − 1 ko chain karo to phir bhi ek linear function milta hai. Nonlinear activation ke bina deep network koi complex problem solve nahi kar sakta. Lekin nonlinear activations ke saath ek kaafi bada DNN theoretically kisi bhi continuous function ko approximate kar sakta hai.

  • Sigmoid: S-shaped, output 0 se 1 ke beech. Iska derivative har jagah nonzero hota hai, isliye gradient descent har step par progress kar sakta hai — step function mein ye possible nahi tha, kyunki flat segments par gradient zero hota hai.
  • Tanh: sigmoid jaisi, lekin output -1 se 1 ke beech. Output zero ke aas-paas centered rehta hai, jo training ke shuru mein convergence ko speed up karta hai.
  • ReLU: max(0, z) — negative ko zero kar do, positive ko waise hi rehne do. Compute karne mein bahut fast hai, aur iska koi maximum output nahi hota, jo gradient problems ko kam karta hai. Aaj ye default choice hai. Ek kami: z = 0 par differentiable nahi hai, aur z < 0 par derivative zero hota hai.

Regression MLPs

Regression ke liye output layer mein activation function nahi lagate — output neuron koi bhi value de sakta hai. Ek value predict karni ho to ek output neuron, multiple values ho to har dimension ke liye ek neuron.

  • Typical setup: 1 se 5 hidden layers, har layer mein 10 se 100 neurons, hidden activation ReLU, loss MSE (outliers zyada ho to robust loss).
  • Positive outputs chahiye? Output layer mein ReLU ya softplus use karo. Bounded range chahiye to sigmoid (0 se 1) ya tanh (-1 se 1) use karke targets ko us range mein scale karo.
  • Feature scaling zaroori: neural networks gradient descent se train hote hain, aur alag-alag scales wale features par gradient descent achhe se converge nahi karta — isliye inputs ko standardize karna bahut important hai.
  • Scikit-Learn mein: MLPRegressor class hai, lekin isme output activation aur robust loss jaise options nahi milte — isliye asli kaam ke liye Keras use karte hain.

Classification MLPs

Classification mein output layer aur loss function task ke hisaab se chunte hain.

  • Binary classification: ek output neuron, sigmoid activation, loss binary cross-entropy.
  • Multilabel binary: har label ke liye ek output neuron, sab par sigmoid, loss binary cross-entropy — ek hi email ko spam bhi aur urgent bhi classify kar sakte ho.
  • Multiclass (ek hi class): har class ke liye ek output neuron, softmax activation — saari probabilities ka sum 1 hota hai. Loss cross-entropy.
  • Loss ka rule: probabilities predict kar rahe ho to cross-entropy use karo — yehi classification ke liye standard hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 10
← Previous10.1 · Perceptron aur TLU — Neural Network ki Shuruaat→ Next10.3 · Keras Sequential API — Fashion MNIST Image Classifier
10.3Chapter 10 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks with Keras

Keras Sequential API — Fashion MNIST Image Classifier

Keras TensorFlow ka high-level deep learning API hai — isse neural network banana, train karna, evaluate karna aur chalana bahut simple ho jaata hai. Simple dikhne par bhi ye expressive aur flexible hai: zyada tar use cases ke liye yehi kaafi hai. Is section mein hum Fashion MNIST par ek image classifier banate hain.

Dataset load karna

Fashion MNIST MNIST ka hi format hai — 70,000 grayscale images, 28 × 28 pixels, 10 classes — lekin images handwritten digits ki jagah fashion items ki hain, isliye problem kaafi zyada challenging hai. Simple linear model MNIST par lagbhag 92% accuracy deta hai, lekin Fashion MNIST par sirf lagbhag 83%.

  • Split: 60,000 training images aur 10,000 test images; training mein se aakhri 5,000 images validation ke liye alag rakho.
  • Shape ka farak: Keras mein har image 28 × 28 array hoti hai (Scikit-Learn jaisi 784-size 1D array nahi), aur pixel values 0 se 255 tak integers hote hain.
  • Scaling: pixel values ko 255 se divide karke 0–1 range mein le aao — neural network ko chhoti values par train karna aasan hota hai.
  • Import style: TensorFlow ko aam taur par tf ke naam se import karte hain, aur Keras API tf.keras se milti hai.

Sequential model banana

Sequential model layers ka ek simple stack hota hai — har layer ka output agle layer ka input. Fashion MNIST classifier mein do hidden layers hain.

  • Input layer: input shape batata hai — batch size nahi, sirf har instance ki shape, yahan [28, 28]. Isse Keras ko pehli hidden layer ke weight matrix ki shape pata chalti hai.
  • Flatten layer: har 28 × 28 image ko 784-size 1D array mein badal deta hai. Iske koi parameters nahi hote — ye sirf reshaping karta hai.
  • Dense hidden layers: pehli mein 300 neurons, doosri mein 100 neurons, dono mein ReLU activation. Har Dense layer apna weight matrix aur bias vector khud manage karta hai.
  • Output layer: 10 neurons (har class ke liye ek), softmax activation kyunki classes exclusive hain — ek image sirf ek hi class ki ho sakti hai.
  • Parameters: model.summary() se pata chalta hai ki total 266,610 trainable parameters hain — pehli hidden layer mein hi 784 × 300 weights + 300 biases = 235,500 parameters! Itni flexibility overfitting ka risk bhi laati hai.
  • Weights dekhna: layer.get_weights() se weights aur biases nikaal sakte ho. Weights randomly initialize hote hain (symmetry todne ke liye), biases zero se.

GitHub: 10_neural_nets_with_keras.ipynb

Code: Sequential Fashion MNIST model — GitHub
tf.random.set_seed(42)
model = tf.keras.Sequential()
model.add(tf.keras.layers.InputLayer(input_shape=[28, 28]))
model.add(tf.keras.layers.Flatten())
model.add(tf.keras.layers.Dense(300, activation="relu"))
model.add(tf.keras.layers.Dense(100, activation="relu"))
model.add(tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax"))

Compile karna — loss, optimizer, metrics

Model banane ke baad compile() call karna zaroori hai — isme loss function, optimizer aur extra metrics batate hain.

  • sparse_categorical_crossentropy: jab labels sparse ho — har instance ke liye sirf ek class index (0 se 9) — aur classes exclusive ho. One-hot labels ho to categorical_crossentropy use karo; binary ya multilabel ho to output mein sigmoid + binary_crossentropy.
  • Optimizer "sgd": stochastic gradient descent — matlab backpropagation (reverse-mode autodiff + gradient descent). Default learning rate 0.01 hoti hai; tune karna ho to SGD(learning_rate=...) object banao.
  • Metrics: classifier ke liye accuracy measure karna useful hota hai, isliye metrics=["accuracy"].

Train, evaluate aur predict karna

Training sirf model.fit() call karne se hoti hai. Har epoch mein Keras mini-batches process karta hai (default batch size 32), aur loss aur accuracy dikhata hai.

  • fit(): X_train, y_train, epochs (default sirf 1 hota hai — kaafi nahi!), aur validation_data pass karo. Validation loss aur accuracy har epoch ke end mein measure hoti hai.
  • Overfitting ka signal: training accuracy validation accuracy se bahut zyada ho jaaye to model overfit kar raha hai, ya data mein mismatch hai.
  • History object: fit() ek History object deta hai — history.history mein har epoch ki training aur validation loss/metrics hoti hain, jinse learning curves plot kar sakte ho.
  • Class imbalance: kuch classes zyada ho to fit() mein class_weight do, aur per-instance weights ke liye sample_weight.
  • evaluate(): test set par final performance check karo — validation par tune kiye hue hyperparameters ko test set par dobara tweak mat karo, nahi to generalization error ka estimate bahut optimistic ho jaayega.
  • predict(): har instance ke liye har class ki probability deta hai. Sabse zyada probability wali class ke liye argmax() use karo.
  • Continue training: model poori tarah converge na hua ho to fit() dobara call kar sakte ho — Keras wahi se training continue karta hai jahan ruka tha.

GitHub: 10_neural_nets_with_keras.ipynb

Code: Compile aur train karna — GitHub
model.compile(loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
              optimizer="sgd",
              metrics=["accuracy"])

history = model.fit(X_train, y_train, epochs=30,
                    validation_data=(X_valid, y_valid))

Hyperparameters tune karne ka order

Performance pasand na aaye to pehle learning rate check karo. Phir optimizer badlo (aur har baar learning rate dobara tune karo). Phir model hyperparameters — layers ki sankhya, har layer mein neurons, activation functions — aur batch size bhi try karo. Chapter ke end mein hyperparameter search ke tools bhi hain, lekin manual tuning ki intuition sabse pehle aani chahiye.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 10
← Previous10.2 · MLP, Backpropagation aur Activation Functions→ Next10.4 · Functional API, Subclassing API, Saving aur Callbacks
10.4Chapter 10 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks with Keras

Functional API, Subclassing API, Saving aur Callbacks

Sequential API sirf seedhe stack wale models ke liye hai. Jaise hi model mein multiple inputs, multiple outputs, ya skip connections aati hain, functional API chahiye hoti hai. Aur jab model mein loops ya conditional branching ho, to subclassing API kaam aati hai.

Functional API — Wide & Deep network

Wide & Deep network mein inputs ka ek hissa seedha output layer se judta hai (wide path — simple rules seekhne ke liye) aur ek hissa deep layers se hokar jaata hai (deep path — complex patterns ke liye). Regular MLP mein saara data poori stack se guzarta hai, jisse simple patterns distort ho sakte hain.

  • Layers ko function ki tarah use karo: pehle saari layers banao, phir unko Input object par call karo — jaise normalized = normalization_layer(input_). Abhi koi asli data process nahi ho raha, ye sirf symbolic connection hai.
  • Concatenate: wide path aur deep path ke outputs ko Concatenate layer se jodo, phir output layer mein bhejo.
  • Model banao: tf.keras.Model(inputs=[...], outputs=[...]) se model banta hai. Uske baad compile, fit, evaluate, predict — sab Sequential jaisa hi hai.
  • Multiple inputs: alag-alag features ko alag paths se bhejna ho to do Input objects banao. fit() mein phir ek ki jagah do matrices ka tuple (ya naam wala dictionary) pass karna padta hai.
  • Multiple outputs: jaise ek hi picture mein object ko locate bhi karna hai aur classify bhi — har output ke liye alag loss function do, aur loss_weights se batao kis output ko kitni importance deni hai. Auxiliary output ko chhota weight dekar regularization ke liye bhi use kar sakte ho.

GitHub: 10_neural_nets_with_keras.ipynb

Code: Wide & Deep — Functional API — GitHub
normalization_layer = tf.keras.layers.Normalization()
hidden_layer1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(30, activation="relu")
hidden_layer2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(30, activation="relu")
concat_layer = tf.keras.layers.Concatenate()
output_layer = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)

input_ = tf.keras.layers.Input(shape=X_train.shape[1:])
normalized = normalization_layer(input_)
hidden1 = hidden_layer1(normalized)
hidden2 = hidden_layer2(hidden1)
concat = concat_layer([normalized, hidden2])
output = output_layer(concat)

model = tf.keras.Model(inputs=[input_], outputs=[output])

Subclassing API — dynamic models

Sequential aur functional API declarative hain — pehle structure declare karo, phir data do. Iske fayde hain: model aasani se save, clone aur share hota hai, structure display aur analyze ho sakta hai, aur shapes/types ki checking pehle se ho jaati hai. Lekin ye static hain.

  • Kab use karein: jab model mein loops, alag-alag shapes, ya conditional branching ho — ya tumhe imperative style pasand ho.
  • Kaise: Model class ko subclass karo, constructor mein layers banao, aur call() method mein computation likho — for loops, if statements, low-level TensorFlow ops, sab allowed hai.
  • Keemat: architecture call() method ke andar chhupi hoti hai, isliye Keras use inspect nahi kar sakta — clone_model() kaam nahi karta, summary() mein connections nahi dikhte, aur shape/type ki checking pehle se nahi hoti. Galti karna aasan ho jaata hai.
  • Rule of thumb: jab tak extra flexibility ki sach mein zaroorat na ho, sequential ya functional API par hi raho.

GitHub: 10_neural_nets_with_keras.ipynb

Code: Wide & Deep — Subclassing API — GitHub
class WideAndDeepModel(tf.keras.Model):
    def __init__(self, units=30, activation="relu", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)  # needed to support naming the model
        self.norm_layer_wide = tf.keras.layers.Normalization()
        self.norm_layer_deep = tf.keras.layers.Normalization()
        self.hidden1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units, activation=activation)
        self.hidden2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units, activation=activation)
        self.main_output = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)
        self.aux_output = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)

    def call(self, inputs):
        input_wide, input_deep = inputs
        norm_wide = self.norm_layer_wide(input_wide)
        norm_deep = self.norm_layer_deep(input_deep)
        hidden1 = self.hidden1(norm_deep)
        hidden2 = self.hidden2(hidden1)
        concat = tf.keras.layers.concatenate([norm_wide, hidden2])
        output = self.main_output(concat)
        aux_output = self.aux_output(hidden2)
        return output, aux_output

tf.random.set_seed(42)  # extra code – just for reproducibility
model = WideAndDeepModel(30, activation="relu", name="my_cool_model")

Model save aur restore karna

Trained model ko save karna ek line ka kaam hai, aur load karna bhi utna hi aasan hai.

  • Poora model: model.save() se architecture, weights, aur optimizer state — sab save hota hai. Load karne ke baad training wahi se continue kar sakte ho.
  • Sirf weights: save_weights() / load_weights() sirf parameter values save karte hain — fast hai aur kam disk lagti hai, isliye training ke dauraan checkpoints ke liye perfect hai.
  • Custom components: Chapter 12 mein aayega — custom loss ya layer wale model ko load karte waqt custom_objects dictionary dena padta hai.

Callbacks — checkpoints, early stopping, TensorBoard

fit() ka callbacks argument Keras ko batata hai ki training se pehle/baad, har epoch se pehle/baad, aur har batch se pehle/baad kya karna hai.

  • ModelCheckpoint: har epoch ke end mein model (ya sirf weights) save karta hai. save_best_only=True ke saath sirf tab save karta hai jab validation performance ab tak ki best ho.
  • EarlyStopping: validation par patience epochs tak koi progress na ho to training rok deta hai. restore_best_weights=True se training ke end mein best wale weights wapas mil jaate hain. Dono callbacks ko combine karna best practice hai — bade models ghanton ya dinon train hote hain, crash se bachne ke liye checkpoints zaroori hain.
  • Custom callback: Callback class ko subclass karke on_epoch_end() jaise methods implement karo — jaise har epoch mein val/train loss ratio print karna, jisse overfitting detect ho.
  • TensorBoard: learning curves live dekhne, multiple runs compare karne, computation graph visualize karne aur profiling ke liye interactive tool hai. TensorBoard callback log directory mein event files likhta hai, aur server unko monitor karke visualizations update karta hai. Har run ke liye alag subdirectory banao taaki runs compare kar sako.

GitHub: 10_neural_nets_with_keras.ipynb

Code: Checkpoints aur early stopping — GitHub
checkpoint_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint("my_checkpoints.weights.h5",
                                                   save_weights_only=True)
history = model.fit(
    (X_train_wide, X_train_deep), (y_train, y_train), epochs=10,
    validation_data=((X_valid_wide, X_valid_deep), (y_valid, y_valid)),
    callbacks=[checkpoint_cb])

early_stopping_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(patience=10,
                                                     restore_best_weights=True)
history = model.fit(
    (X_train_wide, X_train_deep), (y_train, y_train), epochs=100,
    validation_data=((X_valid_wide, X_valid_deep), (y_valid, y_valid)),
    callbacks=[checkpoint_cb, early_stopping_cb])

Hyperparameter tuning

Manual tuning ke baad automated search bhi hai: random search, Hyperband (jo bekaar trials ko jaldi band karke achhe trials ko zyada resources deta hai), aur Bayesian optimization. KerasTuner library in sab ko Keras models ke saath integrate karti hai. Rule yaad rakho: pehle learning rate, phir optimizer, phir architecture — aur har change ke baad learning rate dobara tune karo.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 10
← Previous10.3 · Keras Sequential API — Fashion MNIST Image Classifier→ Next11.1 · Vanishing / Exploding Gradients aur Weight Initialization
11.1Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Vanishing / Exploding Gradients aur Weight Initialization

Uthle (shallow) network train karna aasan tha. Lekin jaise hi network gehra hota hai — 10 layers ya zyada, har layer mein sainkadon neurons — training mein chaar badi problems aati hain: gradients ka unstable hona, labeled data ki kami, slow training, aur overfitting. Is chapter mein hum ek-ek karke in sab ka solution dekhte hain.

Vanishing aur exploding gradients problem

Backpropagation output layer se input layer ki taraf error gradient propagate karta hai. Lekin gradients aksar neeche jaate-jaate chhote hote jaate hain — lower layers ke weights lagbhag badalte hi nahi, aur training kabhi achhe solution par converge nahi karti. Ye vanishing gradients problem hai.

  • Vanishing: gradients chhote hote-hote lagbhag zero ho jaate hain — neeche wali layers kuch seekh hi nahi paati.
  • Exploding: ulta bhi ho sakta hai — gradients badhte-badhte itne bade ho jaate hain ki weights ko bahut bada update milta hai aur algorithm diverge kar jaata hai. Ye recurrent networks mein zyada hota hai.
  • Unstable gradients: aam taur par alag-alag layers alag-alag speeds par seekhti hain — kuch layers tez, kuch bahut slow.
  • Wajah: sigmoid activation function aur us waqt ki popular weight initialization (mean 0, standard deviation 1 wala normal distribution) ka combination — har layer ke baad outputs ka variance badhta jaata hai, jab tak top layers mein activation saturate na ho jaaye. Sigmoid ka mean 0.5 hota hai (0 nahi), jo problem ko aur badhata hai.

Weight initialization — variance ko stable rakho

Solution ka core idea simple hai: har layer ke outputs ka variance inputs ke variance ke barabar rehna chahiye — na badhe, na ghate. Iske liye weights ko sahi scale par initialize karna padta hai, activation function ke hisaab se.

  • variance-scaling initialization: sigmoid aur tanh jaise saturating activations ke liye — weights ka variance fan-in aur fan-out ke average par based hota hai. Keras mein ye default initialization hai (uniform distribution ke saath).
  • ReLU variance-scaling initialization: ReLU aur uske variants ke liye — variance 2 / fan-in. ReLU negative values ko zero kar deta hai, isliye variance ko double karna padta hai taaki signal aage badhte hue kamzor na pade.
  • self-normalizing initialization: SELU activation ke liye — variance 1 / fan-in. Ye self-normalizing networks ka hissa hai (agle section mein).
  • fan-in / fan-out: fan-in matlab layer ke inputs ki sankhya, fan-out matlab outputs ki sankhya. VarianceScaling initializer se scale, mode (fan-in, fan-out ya average) aur distribution (uniform ya normal) khud choose kar sakte ho.
  • Biases: biases ko zero se initialize karna bilkul theek hai — problem sirf weights mein hoti hai, kyunki saare weights ek jaise hone se symmetry banti hai.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: He initialization — GitHub
dense = tf.keras.layers.Dense(50, activation="relu",
                              kernel_initializer="he_normal")

Initialization se aage

Sahi initialization training ke shuru mein vanishing/exploding gradients ko bahut kam kar deti hai, lekin ye guarantee nahi deti ki training ke dauraan problem wapas nahi aayegi. Isliye activation functions aur batch normalization bhi chahiye — jo agle section mein hain.

SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 11
← Previous10.4 · Functional API, Subclassing API, Saving aur Callbacks→ Next11.2 · Behtar Activations, Batch Normalization aur Gradient Clipping
11.2Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Behtar Activations, Batch Normalization aur Gradient Clipping

Sigmoid ko isliye chuna gaya tha kyunki biological neurons lagbhag waisa hi karte hain — lekin deep networks mein dusre activation functions bahut behtar behave karte hain. Aur jahan activation badalne se kaam na bane, wahan batch normalization gradients ko stable rakhta hai.

ReLU ki problem — dying ReLUs

ReLU positive values ke liye saturate nahi hota aur compute karne mein fast hai, isliye ye deep networks mein bahut achha hai. Lekin isme ek problem hai: training ke dauraan kuch neurons "mar" jaate hain — matlab wo sirf 0 output karte hain.

  • Neuron kab marta hai: jab weights aise tweak ho jaayein ki ReLU ka input training set ke saare instances ke liye negative ho jaaye. Phir gradient zero hota hai, aur gradient descent us neuron ko kabhi fix nahi kar pata.
  • Kitna bura: bada learning rate use karo to aadhe tak neurons dead ho sakte hain.

Leaky ReLU aur PReLU

Leaky ReLU negative values ke liye bhi ek chhoti slope rakhta hai: max(alpha × z, z). Slope hone se neurons kabhi poori tarah marte nahi — lambe coma mein ja sakte hain, lekin wapas jaag sakte hain.

  • Alpha: leak ki matra batata hai — 0.2 jaisi badi leak aksar 0.01 jaisi chhoti leak se behtar perform karti hai.
  • PReLU: parametric leaky ReLU — alpha hyperparameter nahi, trainable parameter hota hai, jo backpropagation se seekha jaata hai. Bade image datasets par bahut achha, chhote datasets par overfitting ka risk.
  • Keras mein: LeakyReLU aur PReLU layers ke roop mein milte hain — activation argument mein bhi de sakte ho, ya alag layer ki tarah bhi. Inke saath bhi ReLU variance-scaling initialization use karo.

ELU aur SELU — smooth options

ReLU, leaky ReLU aur PReLU smooth nahi hain — z = 0 par unka derivative achanak badalta hai, jisse gradient descent optimum ke aas-paas bounce kar sakta hai. ELU iska smooth jawab hai.

  • ELU: z < 0 par negative values leta hai (alpha × (exp(z) − 1)), jisse average output zero ke kareeb rehta hai aur vanishing gradients kam hote hain. z < 0 par gradient nonzero hota hai, to dead neurons nahi hote. Alpha = 1 ho to function har jagah smooth hota hai. Kami: exponential ki wajah se ReLU se slow hai.
  • SELU: ELU ka scaled version. Agar network sirf dense layers ka stack hai, saari hidden layers SELU use karti hain, inputs standardized hain, aur weights variance-scaling normal se initialize hain — to network self-normalize karta hai: har layer ka output mean 0 aur standard deviation 1 ke aas-paas rehta hai, aur vanishing/exploding gradients problem solve ho jaati hai.
  • SELU ki shartein: sirf plain MLPs par guarantee hai; L1/L2 regularization, max-norm, batch norm ya regular dropout use nahi kar sakte (ye self-normalization tod dete hain). Isliye SELU zyada popular nahi hua.

GELU, Swish aur Mish

Ye teeno ReLU ke smooth, non-convex, non-monotonic variants hain — aur practical tests mein aksar sabse behtar perform karte hain.

  • GELU: z × (standard normal CDF). ReLU jaisi dikhti hai, lekin har point par curvature hota hai — complex patterns fit karna aasan ho sakta hai. Approximate form z × sigmoid(1.702z) fast compute hoti hai.
  • Swish: z × sigmoid(beta × z) — beta tune kar sakte ho, ya trainable bhi bana sakte ho. Complex tasks ke liye ye shayad best default hai.
  • Mish: GELU aur Swish se thoda sa behtar, lekin thoda zyada compute mangta hai.
  • Kya chunein: simple tasks ke liye ReLU (fast, aur aksar utna hi achha); complex tasks ke liye Swish; deep MLPs ke liye SELU try karo; latency bahut important ho to leaky ReLU.

Batch Normalization (BN)

Batch normalization har hidden layer ke activation se pehle ya baad mein ek operation jodta hai: pehle inputs ko zero-center aur normalize karo (mini-batch ka mean aur standard deviation use karke), phir do naye parameter vectors se unko scale aur shift karo — model khud seekhta hai ki har layer ke inputs ka optimal scale aur mean kya hona chahiye.

  • Training mein: mean aur standard deviation current mini-batch se nikalte hain. Test time par batch statistics nahi milte, isliye training ke dauraan moving average se final statistics estimate kiye jaate hain.
  • Chaar parameters: har BN layer mein scale (gamma) aur shift (beta) backpropagation se seekhe jaate hain; moving mean aur moving variance exponential moving average se estimate hote hain — ye backpropagation se update nahi hote, isliye Keras unko "non-trainable" kehta hai.
  • Fayde: vanishing gradients bahut kam, saturating activations (tanh, sigmoid bhi) use kar sakte ho, weight initialization ke prati kam sensitive, bade learning rates use kar sakte ho, aur BN ek regularizer ki tarah bhi kaam karta hai.
  • Keemat: model complex hota hai, predictions thode slow hote hain — lekin training ke baad BN layer ko pichhli layer mein fuse kar sakte ho (weights aur biases update karke), jisse runtime penalty khatam ho jaati hai.
  • Position: BN ko activation se pehle lagana hai ya baad mein — is par debate hai, task par depend karta hai, dono try karo. Activation se pehle lagana ho to activation ko alag layer banao aur pichhli layer ka bias hata do (use_bias=False), kyunki BN mein khud offset parameter hota hai.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Batch Normalization — GitHub
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=[28, 28]),
    tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(300, activation="relu",
                          kernel_initializer="he_normal"),
    tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(100, activation="relu",
                          kernel_initializer="he_normal"),
    tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")
])

Gradient Clipping

Exploding gradients ko rokne ka ek aur tareeka: backpropagation ke dauraan gradients ko ek threshold se zyada badhne hi mat do. Ye recurrent networks mein khaas taur par useful hai, jahan batch normalization use karna mushkil hota hai.

  • clipvalue: gradient ke har component ko -threshold se +threshold ke beech clip karo. Ye gradient ki direction badal sakta hai.
  • clipnorm: poore gradient vector ko uske L2 norm ke hisaab se clip karo — direction same rehti hai, sirf magnitude kam hoti hai.
  • Keras mein: optimizer banate waqt clipvalue ya clipnorm argument do. Threshold ek hyperparameter hai — validation set par alag-alag values try karo.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Gradient clipping — GitHub
optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.SGD(clipvalue=1.0)
model.compile(loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", optimizer=optimizer)
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 11
← Previous11.1 · Vanishing / Exploding Gradients aur Weight Initialization→ Next11.3 · Transfer Learning aur Pretraining — Kam Data se Deep Network
11.3Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Transfer Learning aur Pretraining — Kam Data se Deep Network

Bada deep network scratch se train karna achha idea nahi hai — khaas taur par jab labeled data kam ho ya labeling mehenga ho. Agar koi existing neural network tumhare jaisa hi task solve kar chuka hai, to uski layers ko reuse karo. Ye technique transfer learning kehlati hai.

Transfer learning kaise kaam karta hai?

Maan lo ek network 100 alag categories ki pictures classify karna seekh chuka hai — animals, plants, vehicles, roz ki cheezein. Ab tumhe sirf specific types ki vehicles classify karni hain. Dono tasks bahut similar hain, to pehle network ke neeche wale layers reuse karo — sirf top layers ko apne task ke liye dobara train karo.

  • Kyun kaam karta hai: neeche wali layers general features seekhti hain — edges, textures, shapes — jo har image task mein kaam aate hain. Upar wali layers task-specific hoti hain.
  • Steps: pehle reused layers ko freeze karo (trainable = False), sirf top layers train karo. Phir reused layers ko unfreeze karo aur poore network ko chhote learning rate se thoda aur train karo (fine-tuning).
  • Fayda: training bahut fast ho jaati hai, aur bahut kam labeled data chahiye hota hai.
  • Model kahan se laayein: model garden aur hub se pretrained architectures milte hain — Chapter 14 mein is par detail hogi.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Reused layers freeze karke train karna — GitHub
for layer in model_B_on_A.layers[:-1]:
    layer.trainable = False

optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.SGD(learning_rate=0.001)
model_B_on_A.compile(loss="binary_crossentropy", optimizer=optimizer,
                     metrics=["accuracy"])

Unsupervised pretraining

Agar similar task ka pretrained model na mile, lekin tumhare paas bahut saara unlabeled data hai, to unsupervised pretraining kaam aata hai.

  • Idea: pehle network ko bina labels ke train karo — jaise autoencoders se (Chapter 17) — taaki wo data ki useful structure seekh le. Phir usko apne labeled task par fine-tune karo.
  • Kab useful: jab labeled data kam ho lekin unlabeled data bahut ho.

Auxiliary task par pretraining

Teesra option: kisi similar task ke liye labeled data bahut ho to pehle us task par train karo, phir apne asli task par fine-tune karo.

  • Example: chehre pehchanne wala system banana hai — pehle network ko face-related auxiliary task par train karo, phir asli task par le aao.
  • Common pattern: teeno techniques ka goal ek hi hai — scratch se shuru karne ki jagah pehle se seekhi hui knowledge se shuru karo.
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 11
← Previous11.2 · Behtar Activations, Batch Normalization aur Gradient Clipping→ Next11.4 · Faster Optimizers, Learning Rate Scheduling aur Regularization
11.4Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Faster Optimizers, Learning Rate Scheduling aur Regularization

Deep network ko train karna slow bhi ho sakta hai aur overfit bhi kar sakta hai. Is section mein teen cheezein hain: training ko tez karne wale optimizers, learning rate ko schedule karna, aur overfitting se bachne wale regularization techniques.

Momentum aur aage-dekhne-wala (look-ahead) gradient

Plain gradient descent ek lambe, patle valley mein dheere chalta hai — pehle steep slope se neeche aata hai, phir valley ke bottom tak bahut dheere badhta hai. Momentum isme madad karta hai.

  • Momentum optimization: gradient ka exponentially decaying average rakho — jaise bhaari ball neeche roll kar rahi ho. Ye oscillations ko kam karta hai aur convergence tez karta hai. Momentum 0.9 aam taur par achha kaam karta hai.
  • look-ahead accelerated gradient: gradient ko current position par nahi, momentum ki direction mein thoda aage jaakar measure karo. Ye chhota tweak aksar momentum se bhi tez hota hai, aur valley ke across oscillations ko kam karta hai.
  • Keras mein: SGD optimizer mein momentum=0.9 aur nesterov=True set karo.

Adaptive learning rate optimizers — AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam

Ye optimizers har parameter ke liye alag learning rate rakhte hain — jo dimensions steep hain unka step chhota, jo gentle hain unka step bada.

  • AdaGrad: gradients ke squares ko accumulate karta hai aur learning rate ko usse scale down karta hai — steep dimensions jaldi slow ho jaati hain, direction optimum ki taraf correct hoti hai. Lekin deep networks mein ye bahut jaldi ruk jaata hai — learning rate itna chhota ho jaata hai ki training optimum tak pahunche bina hi tham jaati hai. Isliye deep nets ke liye use mat karo.
  • RMSProp: AdaGrad ka fix — saare past gradients ki jagah sirf recent gradients ka exponential decay average rakhta hai (decay rate aam taur par 0.9). AdaGrad se lagbhag hamesha behtar hai.
  • Adam: momentum + RMSProp ka combination — past gradients ka average (first moment) aur past squared gradients ka average (second moment) dono rakhta hai. Default learning rate 0.001 aksar bina tune kiye kaam kar jaata hai, isliye ye use karne mein sabse aasan hai.
  • Variants: AdaMax (max norm use karta hai, zyada stable ho sakta hai), Nadam (Adam + look-ahead trick, aksar Adam se thoda tez), AdamW (Adam + sahi weight decay — Adam ke saath L2 regularization use karne ki jagah AdamW use karo, kyunki Adam mein L2 aur weight decay ek jaise nahi hote).
  • Warning: adaptive optimizers tez converge karte hain, lekin kuch datasets par inka solution generalize kam achha karta hai. Agar performance nirash kare, to look-ahead momentum try karo.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Adam optimizer — GitHub
optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=0.001, beta_1=0.9,
                                     beta_2=0.999)

Learning rate scheduling

Constant learning rate se behtar hai: bade learning rate se shuru karo, phir training aage badhte hue use kam karo. Bahut bada rate diverge kar dega, bahut chhota rate bahut slow hoga, thoda bada rate optimum ke aas-paas dance karta rahega.

  • Power scheduling: learning rate iteration ke saath kam hota hai — pehle tez, phir dheere-dheere slow. Optimizer mein decay hyperparameter set karke implement hota hai.
  • Exponential scheduling: har s steps mein learning rate 10 guna kam ho jaata hai. Implement karne mein aasan aur tune karne mein simple.
  • Piecewise constant: kuch epochs tak ek rate, phir chhota rate — achha kaam karta hai lekin sahi sequence dhoondhne mein fiddling chahiye.
  • Performance scheduling: validation error N steps tak improve na ho to learning rate ko factor se multiply karke kam kar do — ReduceLROnPlateau callback se hota hai.
  • 1cycle: pehle learning rate ko badhao (aadhi training tak), phir ghatao — aksar training ko kaafi tez karta hai aur behtar performance deta hai. Keras mein built-in nahi hai, custom callback se implement hota hai.
  • Learning rate dhoondhna: model ko kuch sau iterations tak train karo, learning rate ko exponentially badhate hue, phir curve dekho — jis rate par loss wapas upar shoot karne lage, usse thoda kam rate chuno.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Exponential learning rate schedule — GitHub
def exponential_decay_fn(epoch):
    return 0.01 * 0.1 ** (epoch / 20)

L1 aur L2 regularization

Deep networks mein hazaaron ya laakhon parameters hote hain — ye flexibility overfitting laati hai. Regularization isko rokta hai.

  • L2: weights ko chhota rakhne ke liye penalty — kernel_regularizer ke through har layer par lagao. SGD, momentum aur look-ahead ke saath theek hai, lekin Adam ke saath L2 ki jagah AdamW use karo.
  • L1: sparse model chahiye (bahut saare weights zero) to L1 use karo. Dono chahiye to l1_l2() use karo.
  • Tip: har layer mein wahi regularizer, activation aur initialization repeat karna ho to functools.partial() se ek wrapper banao — code chhota aur galti-kam hota hai.

Dropout aur MC Dropout

Dropout deep networks ki sabse popular regularization techniques mein se hai. Har training step par har neuron (output neurons ko chhodkar) ko probability p ke saath temporarily "drop" kar do — us step mein wo neuron bilkul ignore hota hai, agle step mein wapas aa sakta hai.

  • Kyun kaam karta hai: neurons apne neighbours par co-adapt nahi kar sakte — har neuron ko khud useful hona padta hai, aur kisi ek input par zyada depend nahi kar sakte. Network zyada robust banta hai aur behtar generalize karta hai.
  • Ensemble view: har step par ek alag network sample hota hai — 10,000 steps matlab 10,000 alag networks, jo weights share karte hain. Final network in sab ka averaging ensemble jaisa hota hai.
  • Dropout rate: aam taur par 10% se 50% — recurrent nets mein 20%–30%, convolutional nets mein 40%–50%. Sirf top 1–3 layers par lagana bhi aksar kaafi hota hai.
  • Technical detail: training mein sirf (1 − p) neurons active hote hain, isliye training ke dauraan baaki inputs ko keep probability se divide kiya jaata hai — taaki test time par scale same rahe.
  • MC Dropout: trained dropout model ko bina retrain kiye behtar banao — prediction ke waqt dropout ko on rakhkar 100 baar predict karo aur average lo. Isse probability estimates zyada reliable hote hain (model confident hokar galat kam hota hai) aur uncertainty ka estimate bhi milta hai — risk-sensitive systems ke liye bahut useful hai.
  • SELU networks ke liye: regular dropout self-normalization tod deta hai — iski jagah alpha dropout use karo, jo inputs ka mean aur standard deviation preserve karta hai.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Dropout aur MC Dropout — GitHub
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=[28, 28]),
    tf.keras.layers.Dropout(rate=0.2),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(100, activation="relu",
                          kernel_initializer="he_normal"),
    tf.keras.layers.Dropout(rate=0.2),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(100, activation="relu",
                          kernel_initializer="he_normal"),
    tf.keras.layers.Dropout(rate=0.2),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")
])

y_probas = np.stack([model(X_test, training=True)
                     for sample in range(100)])
y_proba = y_probas.mean(axis=0)

Max-norm regularization aur practical defaults

Max-norm har neuron ke incoming weights ko constrain karta hai ki unka L2 norm ek limit r se zyada na ho — har training step ke baad zaroorat ho to weights ko rescale kar diya jaata hai. Ye loss mein term add nahi karta. r kam karo to regularization zyada. Keras mein kernel_constraint=max_norm(1.) se lagta hai.

  • Default DNN setup: ReLU variance-scaling initialization, ReLU (shallow) ya Swish (deep), deep nets mein batch norm, early stopping + zaroorat ho to weight decay, optimizer look-ahead ya AdamW, learning rate schedule performance scheduling ya 1cycle.
  • Self-normalizing net setup: self-normalizing initialization, SELU activation, koi normalization nahi, alpha dropout agar chahiye, optimizer look-ahead.
  • Input features normalize karna mat bhoolo: aur agar ho sake to pretrained network ke parts reuse karo, ya unsupervised pretraining use karo.

GitHub: 11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb

Code: Max-norm constraint — GitHub
dense = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
    100, activation="relu", kernel_initializer="he_normal",
    kernel_constraint=tf.keras.constraints.max_norm(1.))
