12.1Chapter 12 · Custom Models and Training with TensorFlow

TensorFlow ki Duniya — Tensors, Operations aur Variables

Ab tak humne sirf Keras ka high-level API use kiya — aur wo 95% use cases ke liye kaafi hai. Lekin jab custom loss, custom layer ya apna training loop chahiye hota hai, to TensorFlow ke low-level API ko samajhna padta hai. Is section mein hum uski buniyaad dekhte hain.

TensorFlow kya hai?

TensorFlow numerical computation ki powerful library hai, khaas taur par large-scale machine learning ke liye fine-tuned. Iska core NumPy jaisa hai, lekin GPU support ke saath.

  • Distributed computing: multiple devices aur servers par kaam kar sakta hai.
  • JIT compiler: Python function se computation graph nikaal kar use optimize karta hai — unused nodes prune karta hai, independent operations ko parallel chalata hai.
  • Portable graphs: computation graph ko portable format mein export kar sakte ho — ek environment mein train karo, dusre mein chalao (jaise Python/Linux par train, Android par run).
  • Autodiff aur optimizers: reverse-mode autodiff aur RMSProp, Nadam jaise excellent optimizers built-in hain.
  • Ecosystem: Keras ke alawa tf.data (data loading), TensorBoard (visualization), TFX (production), Hub (pretrained models) aur model garden bhi hain.
  • Har jagah chalta hai: Windows, Linux, macOS, mobile (TensorFlow Lite), aur browser mein bhi (TensorFlow.js).

Tensors aur operations — NumPy jaisa, lekin alag

TensorFlow ka API tensors ke aas-paas ghumta hai. Tensor NumPy ke ndarray jaisa hi hota hai — multidimensional array, ya scalar bhi ho sakta hai.

  • Banao: tf.constant([[1., 2., 3.], [4., 5., 6.]]) se 2 × 3 matrix banti hai. Har tensor ki shape aur dtype hoti hai.
  • Indexing: NumPy jaisi — t[:, 1:], t[..., 1, tf.newaxis] sab chalta hai.
  • Operations: t + 10, tf.square(t), t @ tf.transpose(t) (matrix multiplication) — operators ke peeche tf.add() jaise functions hain. @ operator tf.matmul() ke barabar hai.
  • Naam ka farak: tf.reduce_mean(), tf.reduce_sum(), tf.reduce_max() NumPy ke mean/sum/max ke barabar hain. Reduce naam isliye kyunki GPU kernel elements ko kisi bhi order mein add kar sakta hai — 32-bit floats ki wajah se result halka sa alag aa sakta hai.
  • NumPy ke saath: tensors NumPy ke saath achhe se khelte hain — NumPy array se tensor banao (tf.constant(a)), tensor se array (t.numpy()), TensorFlow ops NumPy arrays par aur NumPy ops tensors par chala sakte ho.
  • Precision warning: NumPy by default 64-bit use karta hai, TensorFlow 32-bit — neural networks ke liye 32-bit kaafi hoti hai, fast hai aur kam RAM leti hai. NumPy array se tensor banate waqt dtype=tf.float32 set karo.
  • Type conversions: TensorFlow automatic type conversion nahi karta — float aur int tensor ko add karne par exception aata hai. Zaroorat ho to tf.cast() use karo.

Variables — trainable weights ke liye

Regular tensors immutable hote hain — unko modify nahi kar sakte. Neural network ke weights ko backpropagation se tweak karna hota hai, isliye tf.Variable chahiye hota hai.

  • Modify karna: assign(), assign_add(), assign_sub() se poori variable badlo; v[0, 1].assign(42) se ek cell; scatter_nd_update() se multiple cells ek saath.
  • Direct assignment nahi: v[1] = [7., 8., 9.] kaam nahi karta — TypeError aata hai.
  • Practical note: aam taur par variables manually banane nahi padte — Keras ka add_weight() method ye kaam karta hai, aur optimizers parameters ko khud update karte hain.

Aur data structures

Regular tensors ke alawa TensorFlow mein aur bhi structures hain — har ek kisi khaas kaam ke liye:

  • Sparse tensors: mostly zeros wale tensors ko efficiently represent karte hain.
  • Tensor arrays: tensors ki list — fixed length, ya extensible bhi ho sakti hai.
  • Ragged tensors: alag-alag sizes wale tensors ki list — jaise alag lengths wale sentences.
  • String tensors: byte strings hold karte hain (Unicode strings UTF-8 mein encode hoti hain). tf.strings package mein inke operations hain.
  • Sets aur queues: sets ko regular tensors se represent karte hain; queues steps ke across tensors store karti hain (FIFO, priority, shuffle, padding wali).
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 12
← Previous11.4 · Faster Optimizers, Learning Rate Scheduling aur Regularization→ Next12.2 · Custom Loss, Metrics, Layers aur Models
12.2Chapter 12 · Custom Models and Training with TensorFlow

Custom Loss, Metrics, Layers aur Models

Keras ke almost har component ko customize kar sakte ho — loss, metric, activation, initializer, regularizer, constraint, layer, aur poora model bhi. Pattern har jagah ek hi hai: simple function likho, ya hyperparameters save karne ho to class subclass karo.

Custom loss function — robust loss

Noisy regression dataset ho to MSE outliers ko bahut zyada penalize karta hai, aur MAE slow converge karta hai. robust loss dono ka combination hai: chhoti error par quadratic, badi error par linear.

  • Function se: ek function likho jo labels aur predictions lekar har sample ka loss return kare — sirf TensorFlow operations use karo, aur vectorized implementation rakho taaki graph optimization ka fayda mile.
  • Mean mat return karo: per-sample losses return karo, nahi to class weights ya sample weights use nahi kar paoge.
  • Threshold configurable: create_huber(threshold) jaisi factory function se configured loss banao — lekin save karte waqt threshold save nahi hota, load karte waqt dobara dena padta hai.
  • Class se: Loss class ko subclass karo aur get_config() implement karo — phir threshold model ke saath save hota hai, aur load karte waqt sirf class ka naam map karna padta hai (custom_objects dictionary mein, ya register decorator se automatic).

GitHub: 12_custom_models_and_training_with_tensorflow.ipynb

Code: robust loss — function aur class — GitHub
def huber_fn(y_true, y_pred):
    error = y_true - y_pred
    is_small_error = tf.abs(error) < 1
    squared_loss = tf.square(error) / 2
    linear_loss  = tf.abs(error) - 0.5
    return tf.where(is_small_error, squared_loss, linear_loss)

class HuberLoss(tf.keras.losses.Loss):
    def __init__(self, threshold=1.0, **kwargs):
        self.threshold = threshold
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def call(self, y_true, y_pred):
        error = y_true - y_pred
        is_small_error = tf.abs(error) < self.threshold
        squared_loss = tf.square(error) / 2
        linear_loss  = self.threshold * tf.abs(error) - self.threshold**2 / 2
        return tf.where(is_small_error, squared_loss, linear_loss)

    def get_config(self):
        base_config = super().get_config()
        return {**base_config, "threshold": self.threshold}

Custom activation, initializer, regularizer, constraint

Ye sab bhi wahi pattern follow karte hain — bas arguments alag hote hain.

  • Activation function: ek function jo tensor lekar transformed tensor de — jaise softplus: log(1 + exp(z)).
  • Initializer: shape aur dtype lekar random weights de — jaise variance-scaling initializer: standard deviation sqrt(2 / (fan_in + fan_out)) wala normal distribution.
  • Regularizer: weights lekar regularization loss de — jaise L1: sum of absolute values × factor.
  • Constraint: weights lekar constrained weights de — jaise saare weights positive rakhna (negative ko zero kar do).
  • Hyperparameters save karne ho: sahi class ko subclass karo (Regularizer, Constraint, Initializer) aur get_config() implement karo. Losses, layers aur models ke liye call() implement karte hain; regularizers, initializers aur constraints ke liye __call__().

Custom metrics — streaming metrics kyun chahiye

Loss aur metric ek jaise nahi hote: loss gradient descent ke liye hoti hai (differentiable honi chahiye), metric evaluation ke liye hoti hai (interpretable honi chahiye, differentiable hona zaroori nahi).

  • Simple function kaafi hai: zyada tar metrics ko loss function ki tarah hi define kar sakte ho — Keras har batch par call karta hai aur epoch ka mean rakhta hai.
  • Precision jaisi metrics: batch-wise precision ka mean lena galat hota hai — do batches mein 80% aur 0% precision ka mean 40% hota hai, lekin overall precision 50% ho sakti hai (4 true positives / 8 positive predictions). Iske liye streaming metric chahiye jo counts ko accumulate kare.
  • Streaming metric banao: Metric class subclass karo — add_weight() se state variables banao (jaise total aur count), update_state() mein har batch par update karo, result() mein final value compute karo, aur get_config() se hyperparameters save karo.
  • Built-in example: Precision class aisa hi karti hai — true positives aur false positives ko track karti hai, result() overall precision deti hai, reset_states() se dono zero ho jaate hain.

Custom layers — Lambda se MyDense tak

Kabhi aisa layer chahiye hota hai jo TensorFlow mein built-in nahi hai, ya ek block baar-baar repeat hota hai aur use ek layer ki tarah treat karna hai.

  • Bina weights wala layer: simple function ko Lambda layer mein wrap karo — jaise exponential function lagana.
  • Weights wala layer: Layer class subclass karo. Constructor mein hyperparameters save karo; build() mein add_weight() se weights banao (input shape tab pata chalti hai jab layer pehli baar use hoti hai); call() mein computation likho; get_config() mein hyperparameters save karo.
  • Multiple inputs/outputs: call() mein tuple lo aur list return karo — lekin ye sirf functional aur subclassing API mein chalta hai, sequential mein nahi.
  • Training vs testing: agar layer training mein alag behave karti hai (Dropout ya BatchNormalization jaisi), to call() mein training argument lo aur us hisaab se decide karo — jaise training mein Gaussian noise add karo, testing mein kuch mat karo.

GitHub: 12_custom_models_and_training_with_tensorflow.ipynb

Code: Custom Dense layer — GitHub
class MyDense(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, units, activation=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.units = units
        self.activation = tf.keras.activations.get(activation)

    def build(self, batch_input_shape):
        self.kernel = self.add_weight(
            name="kernel", shape=[batch_input_shape[-1], self.units],
            initializer="he_normal")
        self.bias = self.add_weight(
            name="bias", shape=[self.units], initializer="zeros")

    def call(self, X):
        return self.activation(X @ self.kernel + self.bias)

    def get_config(self):
        base_config = super().get_config()
        return {**base_config, "units": self.units,
                "activation": tf.keras.activations.serialize(self.activation)}

Custom models aur model internals par loss/metric

Model class ko subclass karke koi bhi architecture bana sakte ho — constructor mein layers banao, call() mein computation likho. Example: ResidualBlock layer (do dense layers + skip connection: output = input + block output) aur use chaar baar repeat karne wala ResidualRegressor model.

  • Nested layers: ek layer ke andar dusri layers rakh sakte ho — Keras unke variables ko automatically track karta hai.
  • Save karna: save()/load_model() ke liye custom layer aur model dono mein get_config() implement karo — ya sirf save_weights()/load_weights() use karo.
  • Internals par loss: add_loss() se model ke kisi bhi hisse par based loss jodo — jaise reconstruction loss: hidden layers se inputs ko reconstruct karo, reconstruction aur original inputs ka mean squared difference loss mein add karo (chhote weight ke saath, taaki main loss dominate kare). Ye regularization ki tarah kaam karta hai.
  • Internals par metric: add_metric() se aise metric jodo — jaise training ke dauraan reconstruction error display karna.
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 12
← Previous12.1 · TensorFlow ki Duniya — Tensors, Operations aur Variables→ Next12.3 · Autodiff, Custom Training Loops aur TF Functions
12.3Chapter 12 · Custom Models and Training with TensorFlow

Autodiff, Custom Training Loops aur TF Functions

Custom models ke baad aakhri step hai training par poora control: gradients khud compute karna, apna training loop likhna, aur TensorFlow ke graph feature se code ko tez aur portable banana.

GradientTape se autodiff

Neural network mein hazaaron parameters hote hain — har ek ka partial derivative haath se nikaalna impossible hai. Numerical approximation (parameter ko thoda tweak karke dekho) bhi kaam nahi karta, kyunki har parameter ke liye function ko kam se kam ek baar call karna padta hai. Reverse-mode autodiff ek forward aur ek reverse pass mein saare gradients nikaal leta hai.

  • Basic use: tf.GradientTape() context mein computation karo, phir tape.gradient(result, [variables]) se gradients maango — ek hi reverse pass mein sab mil jaate hain, accurate aur fast.
  • Tape ek baar use hoti hai: gradient() call karne ke baad tape erase ho jaati hai — dobara call karne par error aata hai. Multiple baar gradients chahiye to persistent=True use karo aur kaam khatam hone par tape delete karo.
  • Sirf variables track hote hain: constants ke gradients None aate hain. Kisi tensor ke gradients chahiye to tape.watch() se use track karwao — jaise inputs ke respect mein activations ka gradient (regularization loss ke liye).
  • Vector ka gradient: vector diya to TensorFlow uske sum ka gradient nikaalta hai. Har loss ka alag gradient chahiye to jacobian() use karo. Second-order derivatives (Hessians) bhi possible hain, lekin practical mein rarely chahiye hote hain.
  • Gradients rokna: tf.stop_gradient() forward pass mein input ko waise hi pass karta hai, lekin backpropagation mein gradients ko aage nahi jaane deta — jaise constant ho.
  • Numerical stability: square root bahut chhoti values par infinite gradient de sakta hai — x mein chhoti value add karo. Exponential explode ho sakta hai — softplus ko stable form mein likho: log(1 + exp(−|z|)) + max(z, 0). Agar stable function ke gradients bhi unstable ho, to @tf.custom_gradient decorator se khud gradient function likho.

GitHub: 12_custom_models_and_training_with_tensorflow.ipynb

Code: GradientTape — GitHub
w1, w2 = tf.Variable(5.), tf.Variable(3.)
with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
    z = f(w1, w2)

gradients = tape.gradient(z, [w1, w2])

Custom training loop

fit() method kabhi-kabhi kaafi flexible nahi hota — jaise ek model mein wide path aur deep path ke liye do alag optimizers chahiye ho. Tab apna loop likhna padta hai. Yaad rakho: custom loop code ko lamba, galti-prone aur maintain karna mushkil banata hai — seekhne ya sach mein zaroorat ho tab hi likho, warna fit() prefer karo.

  1. Model banao: compile karne ki zaroorat nahi — training loop khud handle karega.
  2. Batch sample karo: har step par training set se random batch lo (asli projects mein tf.data API use hoti hai — Chapter 13).
  3. GradientTape mein forward pass: model ko training=True ke saath call karo, main loss compute karo, aur model.losses (jaise regularization losses) ko add karo.
  4. Gradients aur update: tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables) se gradients lo, phir optimizer.apply_gradients() se gradient descent step lagao. Gradient clipping chahiye to optimizer mein clipnorm/clipvalue set karo; gradients par aur transformation chahiye to apply_gradients() se pehle karo; weight constraints ho to apply ke baad har variable par constraint lagao.
  5. Metrics update karo: mean loss aur metrics ko har step par update karo, aur har epoch ke end mein reset karo.
  6. training=True mat bhoolo: model call karte waqt training=True dena zaroori hai, khaas taur par jab model mein BatchNormalization ya Dropout ho — nahi to wo testing mode mein chalenge.

GitHub: 12_custom_models_and_training_with_tensorflow.ipynb

Code: Custom training loop — GitHub
for epoch in range(1, n_epochs + 1):
    print(f"Epoch {epoch}/{n_epochs}")
    for step in range(1, n_steps + 1):
        X_batch, y_batch = random_batch(X_train_scaled, y_train)
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            y_pred = model(X_batch, training=True)
            main_loss = tf.reduce_mean(loss_fn(y_batch, y_pred))
            loss = tf.add_n([main_loss] + model.losses)

        gradients = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables)
        optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(gradients, model.trainable_variables))

        # extra code – if your model has variable constraints
        for variable in model.variables:
            if variable.constraint is not None:
                variable.assign(variable.constraint(variable))

        mean_loss(loss)
        for metric in metrics:
            metric(y_batch, y_pred)

        print_status_bar(step, n_steps, mean_loss, metrics)

    for metric in [mean_loss] + metrics:
        metric.reset_state()

TF Functions aur graphs — code ko tez banao

TensorFlow 2 mein graphs peeche rehte hain, lekin ab bhi use hote hain — aur inka use bahut simple hai. tf.function() ek Python function ko TensorFlow function mein badal deta hai: pehle AutoGraph source code ko analyze karke control flow (for loops, if statements) ko TensorFlow operations mein badalta hai, phir tracing mein symbolic tensor ke saath function ko run karke computation graph banata hai.

  • Speed: TensorFlow graph ko optimize karta hai — unused nodes prune karta hai, expressions simplify karta hai, independent operations ko parallel chalata hai. Complex computations par TF function aam taur par Python function se bahut tez chalti hai.
  • XLA: jit_compile=True se accelerated linear algebra use hota hai — multiple operations ek hi kernel mein fuse ho jaate hain, jo tez bhi hai aur kam RAM bhi leta hai.
  • Automatic hai: custom loss, metric ya layer ko Keras model mein use karte ho to Keras khud use TF function mein convert kar deta hai — tumhe kuch karne ki zaroorat nahi. XLA chahiye to compile() mein jit_compile=True do.
  • Polymorphism: har unique input shapes aur dtypes ke set ke liye ek graph banta hai aur cache hota hai. Tensor arguments par same graph reuse hota hai, lekin Python numbers (jaise 10 aur 20) par alag-alag graphs banenge — isliye Python values sirf hyperparameters jaise kam-unique-values wale arguments ke liye rakho.

TF Function ke rules

Zyada tar functions ko @tf.function se decorate karna hi kaafi hota hai, lekin kuch rules yaad rakho:

  • External libraries graph mein nahi aati: NumPy ya standard library ki calls sirf tracing ke waqt chalti hain, graph ka hissa nahi banti. tf.reduce_sum() use karo, np.sum() nahi. Random number chahiye to tf.random.uniform() use karo — np.random.rand() har call par wahi number dega jo tracing mein bana tha.
  • Side effects: logging ya Python counter update jaise side effects sirf tracing mein honge, har call par nahi.
  • Variables: TF function ke andar variable banana ho to sirf pehli call par banao — behtar hai variables bahar banao (jaise custom layer ke build() mein). Value badalni ho to assign() use karo, = operator nahi.
  • Source code available hona chahiye: TensorFlow ko function ka source code chahiye hota hai — Python shell mein define kiya function ya sirf compiled .pyc files deploy ki ho to graph generation fail ho sakti hai.
  • Loops: sirf tensor ya dataset par iterate karne wale for loops capture hote hain — for i in tf.range(x) likho, for i in range(x) nahi (wo tracing mein chalega, graph mein nahi).
  • Vectorize karo: performance ke liye jahan ho sake loops ki jagah vectorized implementation use karo.

GitHub: 12_custom_models_and_training_with_tensorflow.ipynb

Code: tf.function — GitHub
def cube(x):
    return x ** 3

tf_cube = tf.function(cube)

@tf.function
def tf_cube(x):
    return x ** 3
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 12
← Previous12.2 · Custom Loss, Metrics, Layers aur Models→ Next13.1 · tf.data API — bade datasets ko fast load karna
13.1Chapter 13 · Loading and Preprocessing Data with TensorFlow

tf.data API — bade datasets ko fast load karna

Jab dataset chhota ho to Pandas aur Scikit-Learn se kaam chal jaata hai, lekin jab dataset bada ho aur memory me fit na ho, to TensorFlow ka apna tf.data API kaam aata hai. Ye API data ko disk se parallel me padhta hai, on the fly preprocess karta hai, aur GPU ko busy rakhte hue agla batch pehle se taiyaar rakhta hai.

Dataset kya hota hai?

tf.data API ka centre point hai tf.data.Dataset — ye data items ki ek sequence hoti hai. Simple example me tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices() ek tensor ko lekar uske slices ka dataset bana deta hai. Dataset par iterate karna bilkul list par iterate karne jaisa hai, lekin ye ek streaming API hai — isme indexing ya slicing nahi hoti, sirf aage badhkar items padhe jaate hain.

  • Dataset me tuples, dictionaries, ya nested structures bhi ho sakti hain — slicing sirf andar ke tensors par hoti hai, structure waise ka waisa rehta hai.
  • tf.data.Dataset.range(10) seedha 0 se 9 tak ka dataset bana deta hai.
  • Dataset ke items ko dekhne ke liye take() method se pehle kuch items liye ja sakte hain.

Transformations ko chain karna

Har transformation method ek naya dataset return karta hai, purana dataset change nahi hota. Isliye methods ko chain kiya ja sakta hai — jaise dataset.repeat(3).batch(7). Repeat karne se data memory me teen guna copy nahi hota, sirf dobara padha jaata hai. Bina argument ke repeat() dataset ko hamesha ke liye repeat karta hai.

  • map() — har item par ek preprocessing function lagata hai. Heavy kaam ke liye num_parallel_calls ko threads ki sankhya ya tf.data.AUTOTUNE par set karo.
  • filter() — sirf wahi items rakhta hai jo condition pass karein.
  • batch() — items ko batches me group karta hai. Aakhri chhota batch hatane ke liye drop_remainder=True use karo.
  • take() — sirf pehle kuch items lene ke liye, dekhne aur debug karne me useful.

Shuffle karna kyun zaroori hai?

Gradient descent tab best kaam karta hai jab training instances independent aur identically distributed hon. shuffle() method ek buffer bharta hai, phir usme se randomly item nikaalta hai aur nayi item se replace karta hai. Buffer size kaafi bada hona chahiye, warna shuffling effective nahi hogi — lekin RAM se zyada bada bhi nahi.

  • Bade dataset ke liye sirf buffer kaafi nahi hota — source data ko pehle se shuffle karna, ya data ko kai files me baantkar unhe random order me padhna bhi zaroori hota hai.
  • list_files() filepaths ka dataset banata hai aur by default unhe shuffle karta hai.
  • interleave() ek saath kai files ko padhkar unki lines ko aapas me mila deta hai — jaise 5 files se ek-ek line baari-baari padhna. num_parallel_calls se files parallel me padhi ja sakti hain.

CSV lines ko parse aur scale karna

TextLineDataset se har line ek byte string ke roop me milti hai. tf.io.decode_csv() us line ko parse karke har column ka scalar tensor deta hai, aur tf.stack() se features ka 1D tensor banaya jaata hai. Uske baad features ko (x - mean) / std se scale kiya jaata hai — mean aur std pehle se training data par compute kiye jaate hain.

Prefetch aur cache — GPU ko khaali mat baithne do

prefetch(1) dataset ko hamesha ek batch aage rehne deta hai — jab GPU ek batch par train kar raha hota hai, tab CPU agla batch taiyaar kar raha hota hai. Agar loading aur preprocessing multithreaded ho, to GPU lagbhag 100% utilized rehta hai.

  • Chhota dataset memory me fit ho to cache() se use RAM me cache karo — load aur preprocess sirf ek baar hoga, har epoch me nahi.
  • cache() ko load aur preprocess ke baad, lekin shuffle, repeat, batch aur prefetch se pehle lagana chahiye, taaki har epoch me order alag rahe.
  • Aur bhi methods hain — concatenate(), zip(), window(), shard(), flat_map(), unbatch(), padded_batch() — details ke liye API docs dekho.

Keras ke saath dataset use karna

Dataset ko model.fit() me seedha pass kiya ja sakta hai — train_set ki jagah X_train, y_train dene ki zaroorat nahi. fit() har epoch me dataset ko repeat karta hai, har baar naye random order ke saath. evaluate() aur predict() me bhi dataset pass ho sakta hai. Custom training loop me dataset par seedha iterate kiya ja sakta hai, aur poora epoch bhi ek TF function ke andar chalaya ja sakta hai.

GitHub: 13_loading_and_preprocessing_data.ipynb

Code: CSV files se efficient dataset — GitHub
def csv_reader_dataset(filepaths, n_readers=5, n_read_threads=None,
                       n_parse_threads=5, shuffle_buffer_size=10_000, seed=42,
                       batch_size=32):
    dataset = tf.data.Dataset.list_files(filepaths, seed=seed)
    dataset = dataset.interleave(
        lambda filepath: tf.data.TextLineDataset(filepath).skip(1),
        cycle_length=n_readers, num_parallel_calls=n_read_threads)
    dataset = dataset.map(preprocess, num_parallel_calls=n_parse_threads)
    dataset = dataset.shuffle(shuffle_buffer_size, seed=seed)
    return dataset.batch(batch_size).prefetch(1)
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 13
← Previous12.3 · Autodiff, Custom Training Loops aur TF Functions→ Next13.2 · TFRecord aur Protocol Buffers — data ko binary format me store karna
13.2Chapter 13 · Loading and Preprocessing Data with TensorFlow

TFRecord aur Protocol Buffers — data ko binary format me store karna

CSV files simple aur convenient hoti hain, lekin bade ya complex data — jaise images ya audio — ke liye efficient nahi hoti. Iske liye TensorFlow ka preferred format hai TFRecord — ek simple binary format jisme varying size ke records ki sequence hoti hai.

TFRecord file likhna aur padhna

Har record me length, length ka checksum, actual data, aur data ka checksum hota hai. tf.io.TFRecordWriter se file likhi jaati hai aur tf.data.TFRecordDataset se padhi jaati hai. Files ko GZIP se compress bhi kiya ja sakta hai — khaas taur par jab data network se load karna ho. Lekin agar CSV se kaam chal raha ho to TFRecord par jaane ki zaroorat nahi — jo cheez tooti nahi hai, use fix mat karo.

  • TFRecordDataset ko filepaths ki list aur num_parallel_reads dekar kai files parallel me padhi ja sakti hain.
  • Har record me koi bhi binary data ho sakta hai — sirf protocol buffers hi nahi.

Protocol Buffers (protobuf) kya hain?

Protobuf ek portable, extensible aur efficient binary format hai. Ek .proto file me message define kiya jaata hai — jaise ek shakhs ka naam, id, aur emails ki list — aur har field ka ek number hota hai jo binary representation me use hota hai. Object ko SerializeToString() se byte string me badla jaata hai aur ParseFromString() se wapas parse kiya jaata hai. TensorFlow me use hone wale protobuf definitions pehle se compile hokar library ka hissa hote hain, isliye alag se compiler chalane ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Example protobuf — ek instance ko represent karna

TFRecord me sabse common protobuf hai Example — ye dataset ki ek instance ko represent karta hai. Isme named features ki list hoti hai, aur har feature ya to byte strings ki list, ya floats ki list, ya integers ki list ho sakti hai.

  • BytesList, FloatList aur Int64List — teen tarah ki value lists.
  • Feature — inme se ek list ko hold karta hai.
  • Features — feature naam se Feature tak ka map.
  • Example — sirf ek Features object hold karta hai, taaki aage naye fields add kiye ja sakein bina purana format tode.

Examples ko parse karna

Padhne ke liye tf.io.parse_single_example() use hota hai — use serialized data aur ek feature description dictionary chahiye hoti hai. Fixed-length features ke liye FixedLenFeature (shape, type, default value) aur variable-length features ke liye VarLenFeature (sirf type) use hota hai. Variable-length features sparse tensor ke roop me parse hoti hain, jinhe tf.sparse.to_dense() se dense banaya ja sakta hai.

  • Batch me parse karne ke liye tf.io.parse_example() use karo — pehle batch() lagao, phir map(parse).
  • BytesList me image bhi store ho sakti hai — tf.io.encode_jpeg() se encode karke, aur padhte waqt tf.io.decode_jpeg() ya tf.io.decode_image() se decode karke.
  • Koi bhi tensor tf.io.serialize_tensor() se serialize karke BytesList me rakha ja sakta hai, aur tf.io.parse_tensor() se wapas parse kiya ja sakta hai.

SequenceExample — lists of lists ke liye

Agar data lists of lists ho — jaise ek document me sentences ki list, aur har sentence me words ki list — to SequenceExample kaam aata hai. Isme context ke liye ek Features object hota hai aur feature lists ke liye ek FeatureLists object. Parse karne ke liye tf.io.parse_single_sequence_example() ya batch ke liye tf.io.parse_sequence_example() use hota hai, aur varying-length sequences ko tf.RaggedTensor.from_sparse() se ragged tensor banaya ja sakta hai.

GitHub: 13_loading_and_preprocessing_data.ipynb

Code: Example protobuf banana aur parse karna — GitHub
from tensorflow.train import BytesList, FloatList, Int64List
from tensorflow.train import Feature, Features, Example

person_example = Example(
    features=Features(
        feature={
            "name": Feature(bytes_list=BytesList(value=[b"[Name]"])),
            "id": Feature(int64_list=Int64List(value=[123])),
            "emails": Feature(bytes_list=BytesList(value=[b"a@b.com",
                                                          b"c@d.com"]))
        }))

with tf.io.TFRecordWriter("my_contacts.tfrecord") as f:
    for _ in range(5):
        f.write(person_example.SerializeToString())

feature_description = {
    "name": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string, default_value=""),
    "id": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64, default_value=0),
    "emails": tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.string),
}

def parse(serialized_example):
    return tf.io.parse_single_example(serialized_example, feature_description)

dataset = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(["my_contacts.tfrecord"]).map(parse)
for parsed_example in dataset:
    print(parsed_example)
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 13
← Previous13.1 · tf.data API — bade datasets ko fast load karna→ Next13.3 · Keras preprocessing layers — model ke andar hi preprocessing
13.3Chapter 13 · Loading and Preprocessing Data with TensorFlow

Keras preprocessing layers — model ke andar hi preprocessing

Data ko preprocess karne ke teen tareeke hain — files likhte waqt pehle se kar lo, tf.data pipeline me on the fly kar lo, ya preprocessing layers ko model ke andar hi daal do. Teesra tareeka sabse safe hai, kyunki training aur production me bilkul wahi preprocessing chalti hai — training/serving skew ka risk khatm ho jaata hai.

Normalization layer

Normalization layer features ko standardize karti hai. Mean aur variance khud specify kiye ja sakte hain, ya adapt() method ko training set dekar layer khud measure kar leti hai. adapt() ke liye poora training set dene ki zaroorat nahi — kuch sau randomly sampled instances kaafi hote hain.

  • Layer ko model ke andar daalo to deployment par model khud raw data ko normalize kar lega.
  • Training fast karni ho to layer ko standalone use karke data ko ek baar scale kar lo, phir bina layer ke model train karo — aur deployment ke liye adapted layer aur trained model ko wrap karke ek final model bana lo.
  • Preprocessing layer ko tf.data dataset par bhi map() se lagaya ja sakta hai, aur adapt() ko dataset bhi pass kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Apni khud ki layer bhi likhi ja sakti hai — jaise ek custom layer jisme adapt() mean aur std compute kare aur call() me (inputs - mean) / (std + eps) return kare.

Discretization layer — numbers ko categories me badalna

Discretization layer numerical feature ko bins me baantkar categorical feature bana deti hai. Ye tab useful hota hai jab feature ka distribution multimodal ho ya target ke saath relation highly non-linear ho. Bin boundaries khud di ja sakti hain, ya num_bins dekar adapt() ko percentiles se boundaries dhoondhne di ja sakti hain — jaise 3 bins ke liye boundaries 33rd aur 66th percentile ke paas hongi.

CategoryEncoding layer — one-hot aur multi-hot encoding

Category IDs ko seedha neural network me nahi dena chahiye, kyunki unki values ka aapas me koi meaningful comparison nahi hota. CategoryEncoding layer one-hot encoding karti hai. Ek se zyada categorical features ek saath encode karo to by default multi-hot encoding hoti hai — output me har category ke liye 1 hota hai jo kisi bhi input feature me present ho.

  • output_mode="count" se har category kitni baar aayi, ye count milta hai.
  • Multi-hot aur count encoding me ye pata nahi chalta ki kaunsi category kis feature se aayi — isse bachne ke liye har feature ko alag se one-hot encode karke outputs ko concatenate karo.

StringLookup aur Hashing layers

StringLookup layer text categories ko integers me badalti hai — adapt() se vocabulary seekhti hai, categories frequency ke order me number hoti hain (sabse frequent ko 1), aur unknown categories ko 0 milta hai. output_mode="one_hot" se seedha one-hot vectors milte hain. IntegerLookup layer bilkul waisi hi hoti hai, bas integers input leti hai.

  • Bada training set ho to adapt() sirf ek subset par chalaya ja sakta hai — lekin rare categories miss ho sakti hain. num_oov_indices ko 1 se zyada rakhne se unknown categories hash se alag-alag out-of-vocabulary buckets me jaati hain.
  • Hashing collisions ho sakti hain — do alag categories ek hi bucket me aa jaayein. Buckets badhane se collision ka risk kam hota hai, lekin categories aur parameters badh jaate hain.
  • Hashing layer ko adapt() ki bilkul zaroorat nahi — ye hash modulo num_bins se category ko bucket deti hai. Ye out-of-core setting me useful hai, lekin collision ki wajah se aam taur par StringLookup behtar rehti hai.

Embeddings — categories ko dense vectors me badalna

Jab categories bahut zyada hon — jaise 50,000 — to one-hot encoding 50,000-dimensional sparse vector banati hai. Embedding usi category ko ek chhota dense vector deti hai, jaise 100 dimensions ka. Embeddings randomly initialize hokar gradient descent se baaki parameters ke saath train hoti hain, aur training ke dauraan similar categories ke embeddings paas aa jaate hain — ye representation learning kehlata hai.

  • Embedding layer ek matrix ko wrap karti hai — har category ke liye ek row. Category ID dene par wahi row return hoti hai.
  • Word embeddings me ye aur bhi interesting hota hai — similar words paas hote hain, aur embedding space ki axes meaningful concepts encode karti hain. Lekin embeddings me biases bhi aa sakte hain, isliye fairness par dhyaan dena zaroori hai.
  • Embedding dimensions ka rule of thumb hai 10 se 300, task aur vocabulary size par depend karta hai.
  • One-hot encoding ke baad bina activation wala Dense layer, Embedding layer ke barabar hota hai — lekin Embedding layer zero se multiply karne ka kaam bachakar bahut kam computation karti hai.
  • Categorical text feature ke liye StringLookup aur Embedding layers ko chain karo — embedding matrix ki rows vocabulary_size() ke barabar honi chahiye.

GitHub: 13_loading_and_preprocessing_data.ipynb

Code: Normalization layer standalone use — GitHub
norm_layer = tf.keras.layers.Normalization()
norm_layer.adapt(X_train)
X_train_scaled = norm_layer(X_train)
X_valid_scaled = norm_layer(X_valid)
Code: Numerical + categorical inputs, embedding ke saath model — GitHub
num_input = tf.keras.layers.Input(shape=[8], name="num")
cat_input = tf.keras.layers.Input(shape=[], dtype=tf.string, name="cat")
cat_embeddings = lookup_and_embed(cat_input)
encoded_inputs = tf.keras.layers.concatenate([num_input, cat_embeddings])
outputs = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)(encoded_inputs)
model = tf.keras.models.Model(inputs=[num_input, cat_input], outputs=[outputs])
model.compile(loss="mse", optimizer="sgd")
history = model.fit((X_train_num, X_train_cat), y_train, epochs=5,
                    validation_data=((X_valid_num, X_valid_cat), y_valid))
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 13
← Previous13.2 · TFRecord aur Protocol Buffers — data ko binary format me store karna→ Next13.4 · Text preprocessing, TF Hub aur TensorFlow Datasets
13.4Chapter 13 · Loading and Preprocessing Data with TensorFlow

Text preprocessing, TF Hub aur TensorFlow Datasets

Numerical aur categorical features ke baad baari aati hai text ki — aur phir data load karne ke do aur aasan tareeke: pretrained model components aur TensorFlow Datasets.

TextVectorization layer

TextVectorization layer basic text preprocessing karti hai. adapt() se vocabulary seekhti hai — pehle text ko lowercase karke punctuation hatati hai, phir whitespace par split karke words ko descending frequency me sort karti hai. Unknown words ko 1 encode kiya jaata hai aur chhoti sentences ko 0 se pad kiya jaata hai.

  • standardize=None se case aur punctuation preserve kiye ja sakte hain, ya apna standardization function diya ja sakta hai.
  • output_sequence_length se saari sequences ko ek hi length par crop ya pad kiya ja sakta hai, ya ragged=True se ragged tensor liya ja sakta hai.
  • output_mode="multi_hot" ya "count" se word counts milte hain, lekin aam words jaise "the" bahut frequent hote hain aur kuch khaas batate nahi.
  • output_mode="tf_idf" behtar hota hai — term-frequency ko inverse-document-frequency se multiply kiya jaata hai, taaki frequent words downweight hon aur rare words upweight hon.

Text encoding ki limitations

TF-IDF simple tasks ke liye kaafi achha hai, lekin iski limits hain — ye sirf space-separated languages me kaam karta hai, homonyms ko alag nahi kar sakta, related words ke beech ka connection nahi samajhta, aur multi-hot/count/TF-IDF me words ka order kho jaata hai. Advanced text preprocessing ke liye TensorFlow Text library me subword tokenizers hote hain, jo words se chhote tokens me split karte hain.

Pretrained language model components — TensorFlow Hub

TensorFlow Hub se pretrained model components — modules — ko seedha Keras layer ke roop me model me daala ja sakta hai. Module me preprocessing code aur pretrained weights dono hote hain, aur aam taur par use extra training ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Example ke liye ek sentence encoder module raw text lekar 50-dimensional sentence embeddings deta hai — andar wo har word ko pretrained embedding matrix se embed karke unka mean nikaalta hai. Isi tarah Hugging Face ki Transformers library se bhi powerful language model components milte hain.

Image preprocessing layers

Keras me teen image preprocessing layers hain — Resizing (image ko desired size par laata hai, crop_to_aspect_ratio=True se distortion se bacha ja sakta hai), Rescaling (pixel values ko scale karta hai, jaise 0–255 se -1–1), aur CenterCrop (beech ka patch kaat-ta hai). Data augmentation ke liye RandomCrop, RandomFlip, RandomTranslation, RandomRotation, RandomZoom, RandomHeight, RandomWidth aur RandomContrast layers hain — ye sirf training ke dauraan active rehti hain aur training set ko artificially bada karke overfitting kam karti hain.

TensorFlow Datasets (TFDS)

TFDS se common datasets — MNIST, Fashion MNIST, ImageNet jaise bade datasets, image, text, audio, video, time series datasets — ek hi function call se load hote hain. tfds.load() data download karke datasets ka dictionary return karta hai, aam taur par train aur test ke liye.

  • Har item ek dictionary hota hai jisme features aur labels hote hain — as_supervised=True se seedha (features, labels) tuples milte hain, jo Keras ko chahiye hote hain.
  • split argument se data split kiya ja sakta hai — jaise split=["train[:90%]", "train[90%:]", "test"] se 90% training, 10% validation aur poora test set milta hai.
  • load() ke baad shuffle, batch aur prefetch lagakar model train karne ke liye taiyaar hai.

GitHub: 13_loading_and_preprocessing_data.ipynb

Code: TFDS se MNIST load karke model train karna — GitHub
train_set, valid_set, test_set = tfds.load(
    name="mnist",
    split=["train[:90%]", "train[90%:]", "test"],
    as_supervised=True
)
train_set = train_set.shuffle(10_000, seed=42).batch(32).prefetch(1)
valid_set = valid_set.batch(32).cache()
test_set = test_set.batch(32).cache()
tf.random.set_seed(42)
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")
])
model.compile(loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", optimizer="nadam",
              metrics=["accuracy"])
history = model.fit(train_set, validation_data=valid_set, epochs=5)
test_loss, test_accuracy = model.evaluate(test_set)
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 13
← Previous13.3 · Keras preprocessing layers — model ke andar hi preprocessing→ Next14.1 · Convolutional layers aur pooling — CNN ke building blocks
14.1Chapter 14 · Deep Computer Vision Using Convolutional Neural Networks

Convolutional layers aur pooling — CNN ke building blocks

Fully connected network chhoti images par to chal jaata hai, lekin badi images par parameters ki sankhya itni badh jaati hai ki training mushkil ho jaati hai — jaise 100x100 image aur pehli layer me 1,000 neurons ka matlab hai 10 million connections, sirf pehli layer me. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) ye problem partially connected layers aur weight sharing se solve karte hain.

Idea kahan se aayi?

CNNs ki inspiration brain ke visual cortex se aayi — wahan kai neurons ka ek chhota local receptive field hota hai, matlab wo sirf visual field ke ek limited region par react karte hain. Kuch neurons sirf horizontal lines par react karte hain, kuch alag orientations par. Upar ki layers me neurons ke receptive fields bade hote hain aur wo neeche ki layers ke patterns ko combine karke complex patterns detect karte hain.

Convolutional layer kaise kaam karti hai?

Convolutional layer me neuron sirf apne receptive field ke pixels se connected hota hai — poori image se nahi. Pehli layer chhoti low-level features par focus karti hai, agle layers unhe jodkar bade high-level features banate hain. Ye hierarchical structure real-world images me naturally hoti hai, isiliye CNNs image recognition me itne achhe hain.

  • Receptive field ki height aur width fh aur fw hoti hain. Layer ki height-width pehle jaisi rakhni ho to inputs ke aas-paas zeros add kiye jaate hain — ye zero padding kehlata hai.
  • Stride wo step size hai jisse receptive fields aage badhte hain. Stride 2 ka matlab hai output ki height aur width aadhi ho jaati hain, aur computation bahut kam ho jaata hai.
  • Ek feature map ke saare neurons same parameters (kernel aur bias) share karte hain — ek baar pattern kahin seekh liya to use kahin bhi pehchan sakte hain.

Filters aur feature maps

Neuron ke weights ko receptive field ke size ki ek chhoti image ke roop me dekha ja sakta hai — ise filter ya convolution kernel kehte hain. Ek layer me kai filters hote hain aur har filter se ek feature map banta hai — jo image ke un areas ko highlight karta hai jahan filter sabse zyada activate hota hai. Filters manually define nahi karne padte — training ke dauraan layer khud sabse useful filters seekh leti hai.

  • Input images me bhi multiple channels hote hain — aam taur par red, green, blue (RGB). Grayscale me ek channel hota hai, satellite images me aur bhi zyada ho sakte hain.
  • Neuron ka receptive field pehli layer ke saare feature maps tak extend hota hai.
  • Parameters ki sankhya image size par depend nahi karti — sirf kernel size, input channels aur filters par. Isliye ek hi layer kisi bhi size ki image par chal sakti hai, bas channels sahi hone chahiye.

Keras me Conv2D

Keras me Conv2D layer (alias Convolution2D) 4D inputs leti hai — batch size, height, width, channels. filters se feature maps ki sankhya, kernel_size se filter ka size, padding se "valid" (koi padding nahi) ya "same" (output size input ke barabar) decide hota hai. Strides se output aur chhota ho jaata hai.

  • padding="valid" ka matlab hai koi zero-padding nahi — naam confusing hai, lekin ye standard terminology hai.
  • Kernel ki shape hoti hai [kernel_height, kernel_width, input_channels, output_channels] aur biases ki shape [output_channels].
  • Conv2D ke saath activation function (jaise ReLU) aur sahi initializer (jaise ReLU variance-scaling initialization) dena zaroori hai — warna stacked convolutional layers ek hi layer ke barabar ho jaayengi.
  • 5x5 kernel ki jagah do 3x3 kernels wali layers stack karna behtar hota hai — kam parameters, kam computation, aur aam taur par behtar performance.

Memory ki zaroorat

Convolutional layers ke parameters kam hote hain, lekin RAM ki zaroorat bahut zyada hoti hai — khaas taur par training me, kyunki backpropagation ke reverse pass ke liye forward pass ke saare intermediate values save rakhne padte hain. Example ke liye 200 filters wali layer 100 instances ke batch par 1.2 GB RAM le sakti hai.

  • Inference me sirf do consecutive layers jitni RAM chahiye hoti hai, kyunki purani layer ka output release ho jaata hai.
  • Out-of-memory error aaye to mini-batch size kam karo, stride se dimensionality kam karo, kuch layers hatao, 16-bit floats use karo, ya model ko multiple devices par distribute karo.

Pooling layers

Pooling layer ka kaam input image ko subsample karke chhota karna hai — computation, memory aur parameters kam hote hain aur overfitting ka risk bhi kam hota hai. Pooling neuron ke koi weights nahi hote — wo sirf inputs ko aggregate karta hai, jaise max ya mean se.

  • Max pooling sabse common hai — 2x2 kernel aur stride 2 se output ki height aur width aadhi ho jaati hain, aur 75% input values drop ho jaati hain.
  • Max pooling se chhoti translations ke prati invariance milti hai — image thodi shift ho to bhi output wahi rehta hai. Thodi rotation aur scale invariance bhi milti hai.
  • Average pooling bhi hoti hai, lekin max pooling aam taur par behtar perform karti hai — ye sirf strongest features rakhti hai, isliye agli layers ko cleaner signal milta hai.
  • Global average pooling har feature map ka mean nikaalti hai — ek feature map se ek number. Ye output layer se pehle bahut useful hoti hai.
  • Pooling depth dimension par bhi ki ja sakti hai — jaise alag rotations detect karne wale filters ke outputs ka max lekar rotation invariance seekhna.
  • Invariance har jagah nahi chahiye — semantic segmentation me output ko input ke saath shift hona chahiye, isliye wahan equivariance chahiye, invariance nahi.

GitHub: 14_deep_computer_vision_with_cnns.ipynb

Code: Conv2D layer banana aur max pooling — GitHub
conv_layer = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(filters=32, kernel_size=7)
fmaps = conv_layer(images)

conv_layer = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(filters=32, kernel_size=7,
                                    padding="same")
fmaps = conv_layer(images)

kernels, biases = conv_layer.get_weights()

max_pool = tf.keras.layers.MaxPool2D(pool_size=2)
output = max_pool(images)

global_avg_pool = tf.keras.layers.GlobalAvgPool2D()

← Previous13.4 · Text preprocessing, TF Hub aur TensorFlow Datasets→ Next14.2 · Classic CNN architectures — LeNet se EfficientNet tak
14.2Chapter 14 · Deep Computer Vision Using Convolutional Neural Networks

Classic CNN architectures — LeNet se EfficientNet tak

Typical CNN architecture me kuch convolutional layers (+ReLU), phir pooling layer, phir wahi pattern dobara — image chhoti hoti jaati hai aur feature maps gehare hote jaate hain. Upar ek regular feedforward network hota hai jo prediction deta hai. Is basic pattern se saalon me kai famous architectures bani hain.

LeNet-5 (1998)

LeNet-5 handwritten digits pehchanne ke liye banayi gayi thi aur banks me checks par digits padhne ke liye widely use hui. Isme convolutional layers aur pooling layers ka stack hai, phir dense network. Aaj ke hisaab se main farq activation functions ka hai — aaj tanh ki jagah ReLU aur RBF ki jagah softmax use karte hain.

AlexNet (2012)

AlexNet ne image classification competition me top-five error rate 17% tak gira diya, jabki dusre best competitor ka 26% tha. Ye LeNet-5 jaisi hai, lekin bahut badi aur gehri — aur isne pehli baar convolutional layers ko seedha ek ke upar ek stack kiya, har layer ke upar pooling layer daale bina.

  • Overfitting kam karne ke liye dropout (50%) aur data augmentation use kiya gaya — images ko shift karna, horizontally flip karna, lighting badalna.
  • Data augmentation training set ko artificially bada karta hai — generated instances itne realistic hone chahiye ki insaan bata na sake ki wo augmented hain. Sirf white noise add karne se kuch nahi hota.
  • Local response normalization (LRN) se strongly activated neurons paas ke feature maps ke neurons ko inhibit karte hain, jisse alag feature maps alag features seekhte hain.

GoogLeNet aur inception modules (2014)

GoogLeNet ne top-five error rate 7% se neeche la diya. Iska raaz hai inception module — ek subnetwork jisme input chaar parallel layers ko jaata hai: 1x1, 3x3 aur 5x5 kernels wali convolutional layers aur ek max pooling layer. Saari outputs ko depth dimension par concatenate kar diya jaata hai.

  • 1x1 convolutional layers spatial patterns nahi dekh sakti, lekin depth (channels) ke patterns capture karti hain, aur bottleneck ki tarah dimensionality kam karti hain.
  • 1x1 + 3x3 ya 1x1 + 5x5 ka pair ek powerful convolutional layer ki tarah kaam karta hai.
  • GoogLeNet me AlexNet se 10 guna kam parameters the — lagbhag 6 million, 60 million ke mukable.
  • Network ke end me global average pooling layer hoti hai, isliye kai fully connected layers ki zaroorat nahi padti — parameters aur overfitting dono kam hote hain.

VGGNet (2014)

VGGNet bahut simple aur classical architecture hai — 2 ya 3 convolutional layers, phir pooling, aur ye pattern kul 16 ya 19 convolutional layers tak repeat hota hai, phir dense network. Isme chhote 3x3 filters use hote hain, lekin bahut saare.

ResNet aur skip connections (2015)

ResNet ne top-five error rate 3.6% se neeche la diya, 152 layers ke saath. Iska raaz hai skip connections — layer ka input usse upar wali layer ke output me add kar diya jaata hai. Network ko target function h(x) ki jagah residual f(x) = h(x) - x seekhna hota hai.

  • Shuruaat me weights zero ke paas hote hain, to skip connection wali network identity function model karti hai — agar target uske paas ho to training bahut fast hoti hai.
  • Kai layers ne abhi seekhna shuru bhi na kiya ho, tab bhi signal skip connections se poori network me aasani se beh sakta hai.
  • Har residual unit me do 3x3 convolutional layers hoti hain, batch normalization aur ReLU ke saath, stride 1 aur "same" padding.
  • Jab feature maps double hote hain aur size aadha hota hai, to skip connection me 1x1 convolutional layer (stride 2) se shapes match ki jaati hain.
  • Gehri ResNets me bottleneck residual units hote hain — 1x1 layer se depth kam karo, 3x3 layer chalao, phir 1x1 se depth wapas badhao.

Xception, SENet aur baaki architectures

  • Xception — inception modules ki jagah depthwise separable convolutions use karta hai. Pehle har input feature map par ek spatial filter lagta hai, phir 1x1 filters sirf cross-channel patterns dekhte hain. Kam parameters, kam memory, kam computation — aur aam taur par behtar performance. Keras me SeparableConv2D, Conv2D ki drop-in replacement hai.
  • SENet (2017) — har inception module ya residual unit me ek chhota SE block add karta hai, jo feature maps ko recalibrate karta hai. SE block global average pooling, phir ek chhoti ReLU dense layer (squeeze), phir sigmoid dense layer se bana hota hai. Isse top-five error rate 2.25% tak gaya.
  • ResNeXt — residual units me kai parallel stacks hote hain, jinke outputs add hote hain.
  • DenseNet — har layer ka output usi block ki baad wali saari layers ko input milta hai.
  • MobileNet — lightweight aur fast models, mobile aur web apps ke liye, depthwise separable convolutions par based.
  • EfficientNet — depth, width aur resolution ko ek saath principled tareeke se scale karta hai (compound scaling). Baseline se B1 se B7 tak bade versions banaye gaye, aur ye aaj bhi best models me se hain.

Sahi architecture kaise chuno?

Choice is par depend karti hai ki kya important hai — accuracy, model size, CPU par inference speed, ya GPU par speed. Bade models aam taur par zyada accurate hote hain, lekin hamesha nahi — jaise EfficientNetB2, InceptionV3 se chhota bhi hai aur accurate bhi. MobileNetV2 sirf 14 MB ka hai, EfficientNetB7 256 MB ka hai aur sabse accurate hai.

GitHub: 14_deep_computer_vision_with_cnns.ipynb

Code: Fashion MNIST ke liye basic CNN — GitHub
from functools import partial

DefaultConv2D = partial(tf.keras.layers.Conv2D, kernel_size=3, padding="same",
                        activation="relu", kernel_initializer="he_normal")
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    DefaultConv2D(filters=64, kernel_size=7, input_shape=[28, 28, 1]),
    tf.keras.layers.MaxPool2D(),
    DefaultConv2D(filters=128),
    DefaultConv2D(filters=128),
    tf.keras.layers.MaxPool2D(),
    DefaultConv2D(filters=256),
    DefaultConv2D(filters=256),
    tf.keras.layers.MaxPool2D(),
    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=128, activation="relu",
                          kernel_initializer="he_normal"),
    tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.5),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=64, activation="relu",
                          kernel_initializer="he_normal"),
    tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.5),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=10, activation="softmax")
])

← Previous14.1 · Convolutional layers aur pooling — CNN ke building blocks→ Next14.3 · Pretrained models, transfer learning, detection aur segmentation
14.3Chapter 14 · Deep Computer Vision Using Convolutional Neural Networks

Pretrained models, transfer learning, detection aur segmentation

Standard architectures ko haath se implement karne ki zaroorat aam taur par nahi padti — Keras me pretrained networks ek line me mil jaate hain. Aur sirf classification hi nahi, CNNs objects ko locate bhi kar sakte hain, kai objects detect kar sakte hain, aur har pixel ko classify bhi kar sakte hain.

ResNet-34 ko Keras me implement karna

ResNet-34 lagbhag 40 lines me ban jaata hai. Pehle ek ResidualUnit custom layer banao — main layers (do convolutional layers + batch normalization + activation) aur skip layers (sirf jab stride 1 se zyada ho, tab 1x1 convolution). Phir Sequential model me pehle 7x7 convolution, batch normalization, ReLU aur max pooling daalo, phir loop se 3 units 64 filters ke, 4 units 128 ke, 6 units 256 ke aur 3 units 512 filters ke add karo. Aakhir me global average pooling, flatten aur dense output layer.

Pretrained models use karna

tf.keras.applications se ResNet-50 jaise models ek line me load hote hain — model = tf.keras.applications.ResNet50(weights="imagenet"). Images ko sahi size par resize karna hota hai (ResNet-50 ke liye 224x224) aur har model ka apna preprocess_input() function hota hai jo pixel values ko us model ki expectation ke hisaab se taiyaar karta hai.

  • Predictions ke liye decode_predictions() top K predictions deta hai — class id, naam aur confidence score ke saath.
  • tf.keras.applications me MobileNet, EfficientNet, InceptionV3, ResNetV2 jaise kai models hain — lightweight aur fast se lekar bade aur accurate tak.

Transfer learning — apni classes par train karna

Agar aapki classes ImageNet me nahi hain, to bhi pretrained model ka fayda uthaya ja sakta hai. Flowers dataset ka example dekho — sirf 3,670 images hain, 5 classes ke. Pehle dataset ko TFDS se load karke train/validation/test me split karo, images ko 224x224 par resize karo aur Xception ke preprocess_input() se preprocess karo.

  • Data augmentation model me daalo — RandomFlip, RandomRotation, RandomContrast — ye training ke dauraan randomly transform karte hain.
  • Xception base model ko include_top=False ke saath load karo, phir GlobalAveragePooling2D aur apni classes ke liye softmax Dense layer add karo.
  • Pehle base model ki layers ko freeze karke sirf top layers train karo — validation accuracy 80% se upar jaani chahiye.
  • Phir base model ki upar wali layers ko unfreeze karke bahut kam learning rate se dobara train karo — test accuracy lagbhag 92% tak ja sakti hai, aur tuning se 95-97% tak.
  • Freeze/unfreeze ke baad model ko dobara compile karna mat bhoolo.

Classification aur localization

Object ko locate karna ek regression task hai — bounding box ke centre ke coordinates aur uski height-width predict karni hoti hain. Model me ek aur dense output layer add karo jisme 4 units hon, MSE loss se train karo. Bounding boxes ko 0 se 1 ke beech normalize karna chahiye, aur height-width ki jagah unka square root predict karna behtar hota hai — taaki bade box me 10-pixel error chhote box jitna penalize na ho.

  • Bounding boxes ke liye annotation tools use hote hain, ya crowdsourcing platforms — lekin ye project ka sabse mehenga aur mushkil hissa ho sakta hai.
  • Bounding box evaluate karne ka standard metric hai IoU (intersection over union) — predicted aur target box ke overlap ka area, unke union ke area se divide karke.

Object detection — kai objects ek image me

Object detection me kai objects ko classify aur locate karna hota hai. Purana tareeka tha CNN ko image par slide karna — har region me class probabilities, bounding box aur ek objectness score predict karna (object ke centre me hone ki probability). Ek hi object kai baar detect ho sakta hai, isliye non-max suppression se extra boxes hataye jaate hain.

  • Non-max suppression — pehle low objectness wale boxes hatao, phir sabse zyada score wale box se bahut overlap karne wale boxes hatao, aur ye repeat karo.
  • Fully convolutional network (FCN) me dense layers ko convolutional layers se replace kar diya jaata hai — isse network kisi bhi size ki image par ek hi baar me chal sakta hai aur grid of predictions deta hai.
  • YOLO (You Only Look Once) bahut fast aur accurate hai — real-time video par bhi chal sakta hai. Har grid cell me objects ke bounding boxes predict karta hai, har cell ke liye do bounding boxes aur class probabilities ke saath. Baad ke versions me anchor priors aur skip connections se accuracy aur badhi.
  • mAP (mean average precision) object detection ka common metric hai — har class ki average precision ka mean, IoU threshold ke saath.
  • TensorFlow Hub par YOLO, SSD, Faster R-CNN aur EfficientDet jaise pretrained detection models milte hain.

Object tracking aur semantic segmentation

Video me objects ko sirf detect nahi, track bhi karna hota hai. DeepSORT naam ka system Kalman filters (constant speed assume karke position predict karna), deep learning resemblance measure, aur Hungarian algorithm (detections ko tracked objects se map karna) ko combine karta hai.

Semantic segmentation me har pixel ko us object ki class se classify kiya jaata hai — jaise road, car, pedestrian, building. Mushkil ye hai ki CNN se guzarte hue image ki spatial resolution kho jaati hai. Solution hai transposed convolutional layers se upsampling karna, aur neeche wali layers se skip connections jodkar khoyi hui resolution wapas laana.

  • Transposed convolutional layer pehle image ko zeros daalkar stretch karti hai, phir regular convolution karti hai. Keras me Conv2DTranspose use hota hai.
  • Instance segmentation semantic segmentation jaisi hai, lekin ek hi class ke alag-alag objects ko bhi alag pehchanti hai — jaise Mask R-CNN har bounding box ke liye pixel mask bhi deta hai.
  • 2020 ke baad se transformers bhi computer vision me aane lage hain, lekin lagbhag saari architectures ab bhi CNNs par based hain.

GitHub: 14_deep_computer_vision_with_cnns.ipynb

Code: ResNet-34 — ResidualUnit aur model — GitHub
DefaultConv2D = partial(tf.keras.layers.Conv2D, kernel_size=3, strides=1,
                        padding="same", kernel_initializer="he_normal",
                        use_bias=False)

class ResidualUnit(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, filters, strides=1, activation="relu", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.activation = tf.keras.activations.get(activation)
        self.main_layers = [
            DefaultConv2D(filters, strides=strides),
            tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
            self.activation,
            DefaultConv2D(filters),
            tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization()
        ]
        self.skip_layers = []
        if strides > 1:
            self.skip_layers = [
                DefaultConv2D(filters, kernel_size=1, strides=strides),
                tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization()
            ]

    def call(self, inputs):
        Z = inputs
        for layer in self.main_layers:
            Z = layer(Z)
        skip_Z = inputs
        for layer in self.skip_layers:
            skip_Z = layer(skip_Z)
        return self.activation(Z + skip_Z)

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    DefaultConv2D(64, kernel_size=7, strides=2, input_shape=[224, 224, 3]),
    tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
    tf.keras.layers.Activation("relu"),
    tf.keras.layers.MaxPool2D(pool_size=3, strides=2, padding="same"),
])
prev_filters = 64
for filters in [64] * 3 + [128] * 4 + [256] * 6 + [512] * 3:
    strides = 1 if filters == prev_filters else 2
    model.add(ResidualUnit(filters, strides=strides))
    prev_filters = filters

model.add(tf.keras.layers.GlobalAvgPool2D())
model.add(tf.keras.layers.Flatten())
model.add(tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax"))
Code: Data augmentation layers — GitHub
data_augmentation = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.RandomFlip(mode="horizontal", seed=42),
    tf.keras.layers.RandomRotation(factor=0.05, seed=42),
    tf.keras.layers.RandomContrast(factor=0.2, seed=42)
])
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow, O'Reilly, Chapter 14

15.1Chapter 15 · Processing Sequences Using RNNs and CNNs

Recurrent neurons aur memory cells — sequences ko samajhna

Bhavishya predict karna hum roz karte hain — dost ka sentence poora karna, ya subah coffee ki khushboo ka andaza lagana. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) yehi kaam data par karte hain — time series analyze karke aage ka forecast karte hain, aur sentences, documents ya audio jaise arbitrary length ke sequences par kaam karte hain.

Recurrent neuron kya hota hai?

Feedforward network me activations sirf ek direction me behti hain — input se output tak. RNN me backward connections bhi hote hain. Sabse simple RNN me ek neuron hota hai jo inputs leta hai, output deta hai, aur apna output wapas khud ko bhejta hai. Har time step t par neuron ko current input x(t) aur pichhle time step ka output milta hai. Pehle time step par previous output nahi hota, isliye use 0 maan liya jaata hai.

  • Network ko time axis par dikhana unrolling kehlata hai — wahi neuron har time step par ek baar dikhaya jaata hai.
  • Har recurrent neuron ke do sets of weights hote hain — ek current inputs ke liye (Wx) aur ek pichhle outputs ke liye (Wy). Poori layer ke liye ye do weight matrices hoti hain.
  • Output ek function hota hai current inputs aur pichhle output ka — aur pichhla output usse pichhle inputs ka function hota hai. Isliye time step t ka output, time 0 se lekar t tak ke saare inputs ka function hota hai.

Memory cells

Neural network ka wo hissa jo time steps ke across kuch state preserve karta hai, memory cell (ya sirf cell) kehlata hai. Ek recurrent neuron ya recurrent neurons ki layer ek bahut basic cell hai — ye sirf chhote patterns seekh sakti hai, aam taur par lagbhag 10 steps tak ke. Cell ki state h(t) current inputs aur pichhli state ka function hoti hai. Basic cells me output state ke barabar hota hai, lekin complex cells me dono alag ho sakte hain.

Input aur output sequences ke chaar patterns

  • Sequence-to-sequence — sequence input, sequence output. Jaise pichhle N dinon ka data dekar agle dinon ka power consumption forecast karna.
  • Sequence-to-vector — sequence input, sirf aakhri output use hoti hai. Jaise movie review ke words dekar sentiment score nikaalna.
  • Vector-to-sequence — ek hi input vector har time step par dekar sequence output karna. Jaise image dekar uska caption generate karna.
  • Encoder-decoder — pehle sequence-to-vector encoder sentence ko ek vector me badalta hai, phir vector-to-sequence decoder use doosri language me sentence me badalta hai. Ye translation ke liye single RNN se behtar kaam karta hai, kyunki poora sentence dekhe bina translate karna mushkil hota hai.

Training — backpropagation through time (BPTT)

RNN ko train karne ke liye use time ke through unroll karke regular backpropagation lagayi jaati hai — yehi BPTT hai. Pehle unrolled network se forward pass hota hai, phir loss function se output sequence evaluate hoti hai. Loss sirf kuch outputs par bhi depend kar sakti hai — jaise sequence-to-vector me sirf aakhri output par. Phir gradients unrolled network se backward propagate hote hain. Kyunki wahi parameters W aur b har time step par use hote hain, unke gradients backprop me kai baar tweak hote hain. Keras ye saari complexity khud handle karta hai.

GitHub: 15_processing_sequences_using_rnns_and_cnns.ipynb

Code: Time series se training windows banana — GitHub
seq_length = 56
train_ds = tf.keras.utils.timeseries_dataset_from_array(
    rail_train.to_numpy(),
    targets=rail_train[seq_length:],
    sequence_length=seq_length,
    batch_size=32,
    shuffle=True,
    seed=42
)
valid_ds = tf.keras.utils.timeseries_dataset_from_array(
    rail_valid.to_numpy(),
    targets=rail_valid[seq_length:],
    sequence_length=seq_length,
    batch_size=32

← Previous14.3 · Pretrained models, transfer learning, detection aur segmentation→ Next15.2 · Time series forecasting — baselines se RNN tak
15.2Chapter 15 · Processing Sequences Using RNNs and CNNs

Time series forecasting — baselines se RNN tak

Ek practical example se samjho — daily ridership data se agle din kitne log bus aur train me safar karenge, ye forecast karna. Pehle data ko samjho, phir simple baselines banao, aur phir machine learning models se unhe beat karne ki koshish karo.

Time series ko samajhna

Time series wo data hai jisme values alag-alag time steps par hoti hain, aam taur par regular intervals par. Ek value per time step ho to univariate, kai values hon to multivariate time series kehlati hai. Ridership data me weekly seasonality bahut strong hai — har hafte wahi pattern repeat hota hai. Yearly seasonality bhi hai, aur long-term trends bhi.

  • Naive forecasting — pichhle hafte ki value ko copy karke forecast karna. Ye ek bahut achha baseline hai, aur kabhi-kabhi ise beat karna mushkil hota hai.
  • Differencing — value me se 7 din pehle ki value ghata dena. Isse seasonality aur trend hat jaate hain, aur series stationary ho jaati hai — matlab uski statistical properties time ke saath constant rehti hain.
  • Naive forecast ka MAE lagbhag 43,916 (bus) aur 42,143 (rail) tha, aur MAPE lagbhag 8.3% aur 9.0%.
  • MAE, MAPE aur MSE forecasting ke sabse common metrics hain — kaunsa metric chuno, ye task par depend karta hai.

ARMA family — classical statistical models

ARMA model apna forecast past values ke weighted sum se banata hai (autoregressive component), aur pichhli forecast errors ke weighted sum se use correct karta hai (moving average component). Time series stationary honi chahiye — nahi ho to differencing madad karti hai. Ek round differencing linear trend ko khatm karta hai, do rounds quadratic trend ko.

  • ARIMA model pehle d rounds differencing karta hai, phir ARMA lagata hai, aur forecast karte waqt subtracted terms ko wapas add kar deta hai.
  • SARIMA isme seasonal component bhi model karta hai — kul 7 hyperparameters: p, d, q aur seasonal P, D, Q, plus seasonal period s (yahan weekly seasonality ke liye s = 7).
  • statsmodels library se SARIMA fit kiya gaya — order=(1, 0, 0), seasonal_order=(0, 1, 1, 7). March–May 2019 par iska MAE lagbhag 32,041 tha — naive forecasting se bahut behtar.
  • Hyperparameters chunne ka sabse simple tareeka hai grid search — har combination try karo, sabse kam MAE wala model jeetta hai.

Machine learning ke liye data taiyaar karna

Goal hai pichhle 56 dinon ke data se agle din ki ridership forecast karna. Training data banane ki trick hai — past ki har 56-din ki window ek training sample hoti hai, aur uska target uske turant baad wali value hoti hai. tf.keras.utils.timeseries_dataset_from_array() ye windows aur targets wala tf.data.Dataset bana deta hai. tf.data ka window() method bhi wahi kaam karta hai, zyada control ke saath — flat_map() se nested dataset ko flat dataset me badla jaata hai.

  • Time series ko time ke hisaab se split karo — training 2016–2018, validation Jan–May 2019, test June 2019 se aage.
  • Values ko 1e6 se divide karke 0–1 range me laaya gaya, taaki default weight initialization aur learning rate achhe se kaam karein.
  • Training windows ko shuffle karna zaroori hai, kyunki gradient descent ko instances independent aur identically distributed chahiye hote hain.

Linear model se SimpleRNN tak — results kya aaye?

Basic linear model (Dense(1), robust loss, early stopping) ka validation MAE lagbhag 37,866 tha — naive se behtar, SARIMA se kharab. Phir SimpleRNN try kiya gaya. Recurrent layers ko 3D inputs chahiye hote hain — [batch size, time steps, dimensionality]. input_shape=[None, 1] ka matlab hai kisi bhi length ki univariate sequences.

  • Sirf ek neuron wala SimpleRNN bilkul fail hua — validation MAE 100,000 se zyada. Do wajah — memory sirf ek number thi, aur tanh activation -1 se +1 ke beech hi output de sakta hai, jabki values 1.4 tak jaati hain.
  • 32 neurons wala SimpleRNN aur upar ek Dense(1) output layer — validation MAE 27,703. SARIMA ko beat kar diya.
  • Deep RNN — teen SimpleRNN layers stack karke (pehli do me return_sequences=True) — MAE lagbhag 31,211. Behtar to hai, lekin shallow RNN se kharab — model task ke liye thoda bada tha.
  • Multivariate RNN — bus aur rail dono + agle din ka day type (one-hot encoded) input me — validation MAE 22,062. Badi progress!
  • Multitask model — bus aur rail dono forecast karna — rail MAE 25,330 aur bus MAE 26,369. Dedicated models se thoda kharab, lekin phir bhi kaafi achha.

Kai steps aage forecast karna

Agli 14 values forecast karne ke do tareeke hain. Pehla — ek step predict karo, use input me add karo, phir dobara predict karo — lekin errors accumulate hote hain, isliye ye sirf kuch steps ke liye achha hai. Dusra — model ko ek saath 14 values predict karne ke liye train karo (Dense(14) output layer) — isme errors accumulate nahi hote.

  • Sequence-to-sequence model har time step par agle 14 values forecast karta hai — loss me har time step ka term hota hai, isliye gradients zyada stable hote hain aur training fast hoti hai.
  • Seq2seq model ka t+1 par validation MAE 25,519 tha, t+2 par 26,274, aur t+14 par 34,322 — jitna aage forecast karo, utni accuracy girti hai.
  • Dono approaches combine bhi ki ja sakti hain — 14 din forecast karo, use input me add karo, phir agle 14 din forecast karo.

GitHub: 15_processing_sequences_using_rnns_and_cnns.ipynb

Code: SimpleRNN aur deep RNN models — GitHub
univar_model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.SimpleRNN(32, input_shape=[None, 1]),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)
])

deep_model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.SimpleRNN(32, return_sequences=True, input_shape=[None, 1]),
    tf.keras.layers.SimpleRNN(32, return_sequences=True),
    tf.keras.layers.SimpleRNN(32),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)
])
Code: Sequence-to-sequence dataset aur model — GitHub
def to_seq2seq_dataset(series, seq_length=56, ahead=14, target_col=1,
                       batch_size=32, shuffle=False, seed=None):
    ds = to_windows(tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(series), ahead + 1)
    ds = to_windows(ds, seq_length).map(
        lambda S: (S[:, 0], S[:, 1:, target_col]))
    if shuffle:
        ds = ds.shuffle(8 * batch_size, seed=seed)
    return ds.batch(batch_size)

seq2seq_model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.SimpleRNN(32, return_sequences=True, input_shape=[None, 5]),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(14)
])

← Previous15.1 · Recurrent neurons aur memory cells — sequences ko samajhna→ Next15.3 · LSTM, GRU aur WaveNet — lambi sequences ko handle karna
15.3Chapter 15 · Processing Sequences Using RNNs and CNNs

LSTM, GRU aur WaveNet — lambi sequences ko handle karna

Simple RNNs time series forecasting me kaafi achhe hain, lekin lambi sequences par do badi problems aati hain — unstable gradients aur bahut limited short-term memory. Is section me dono ka solution hai.

Unstable gradients se ladna

Lambi sequence par RNN ko train karne ke liye use kai time steps tak chalana padta hai, to unrolled network bahut deep ho jaata hai — aur deep networks ki tarah unstable gradients ki problem aati hai. ReLU jaise nonsaturating activations yahan utni madad nahi karte — balki outputs explode kar sakte hain, kyunki wahi weights har time step par use hote hain.

  • Chhota learning rate use karo, ya tanh jaise saturating activation use karo — isiliye tanh RNNs me default hai.
  • Gradients explode hon to gradient clipping use karo, aur gradients ka size monitor karo.
  • Batch normalization RNNs me utni efficiently kaam nahi karti — time steps ke beech nahi, sirf recurrent layers ke beech lagayi ja sakti hai.
  • Layer normalization RNNs ke saath behtar kaam karti hai — ye batch dimension ki jagah features dimension par normalize karti hai, har time step par on the fly statistics compute karti hai, aur training aur testing me ek jaise behave karti hai.
  • Dropout ke liye recurrent layers me dropout aur recurrent_dropout hyperparameters hote hain — inputs aur hidden states par alag-alag dropout rates.
  • Custom cell bhi banayi ja sakti hai — jaise ek cell jo SimpleRNNCell ke baad layer normalization aur activation lagaye. Use tf.keras.layers.RNN layer me wrap karke model me daalo.
  • MC dropout se error bars bhi mil sakte hain — inference par dropout on rakhkar kai baar forecast karo, phir mean aur standard deviation nikaalo.

LSTM cells — long-term memory

LSTM cell ki state do vectors me split hoti hai — short-term state h(t) aur long-term state c(t). Network seekh sakta hai ki long-term state me kya store karna hai, kya discard karna hai, aur kya padhna hai. Keras me LSTM layer use karna SimpleRNN ko replace karne jitna aasan hai — aur GPU par optimized implementation milti hai.

  • Forget gate (f(t)) control karta hai ki long-term state ka kaunsa hissa erase karna hai.
  • Input gate (i(t)) control karta hai ki nayi memory g(t) ka kaunsa hissa long-term state me add karna hai.
  • Output gate (o(t)) control karta hai ki long-term state ka kaunsa hissa padhkar output karna hai.
  • Gate controllers logistic activation use karte hain — output 0 se 1 ke beech hota hai, 0 ka matlab gate band, 1 ka matlab gate khula.
  • Long-term state seedha aage badhti hai bina transformation ke — kuch memories drop hoti hain, kuch add hoti hain. Isi wajah se LSTM lambi patterns capture kar sakta hai.
  • Forget gate ka bias 1 se initialize hota hai, taaki training ki shuruaat me sab kuch bhool na jaaye.

GRU cells — LSTM ka simplified version

GRU cell LSTM ka simplified version hai aur lagbhag utna hi achha perform karta hai. Dono state vectors ek hi vector h(t) me merge ho jaate hain. Ek hi gate controller z(t) forget aur input gate dono ko control karta hai — jab memory store karni ho, to pehle us jagah ko erase kiya jaata hai. Output gate nahi hota — poora state vector har time step par output hota hai — lekin ek naya gate controller r(t) control karta hai ki pichhli state ka kaunsa hissa main layer ko dikhaya jaaye. Keras me GRU layer use karna bas SimpleRNN ya LSTM ko replace karne jitna hai.

1D convolutional layers se sequences chhoti karo

LSTM aur GRU 100 se zyada time steps wali sequences par bhi struggle karte hain. Ek solution hai input sequences ko 1D convolutional layers se chhota karna. 1D convolutional layer kai kernels ko sequence par slide karke har kernel ke liye ek 1D feature map banati hai — har kernel ek bahut chhota sequential pattern detect karna seekhta hai.

  • Stride 2 aur kernel size 4 wali Conv1D layer sequence ko aadha kar deti hai, aur kernel stride se bada ho to saare inputs use hote hain — model useful information preserve karna seekh sakta hai.
  • Sequence chhoti karne ke baad GRU layers lambi patterns detect kar sakti hain — aur input sequence length double ki ja sakti hai, jaise 56 se 112 din.
  • Targets ko bhi adjust karna padta hai — kernel size ki wajah se pehle kuch time steps crop karo aur stride ki wajah se targets ko downsample karo.
  • Sirf 1D convolutional layers use karke recurrent layers ko poori tarah hatana bhi possible hai.

WaveNet — dilated convolutions se bahut lambi sequences

WaveNet me 1D convolutional layers stack ki jaati hain, har layer par dilation rate double karke — 1, 2, 4, 8, aur aage. Pehli layer sirf 2 time steps dekhti hai, agle layers 4, 8, 16 time steps — neeche wali layers short-term patterns aur upar wali layers long-term patterns seekhti hain. Dilation rate double karne se network bahut badi sequences ko efficiently process kar sakta hai.

  • Original architecture me 10 layers ke 3 groups the — dilation rates 1, 2, 4, 8, ..., 256, 512 — jo 1,024 size ke kernel wali layer ki tarah kaam karta hai, lekin bahut fast aur kam parameters ke saath.
  • Causal padding ka matlab hai zeros sirf sequence ki shuruaat me add hote hain — taaki convolutional layer future me jhaank na sake.
  • Simplified WaveNet me dilation rates (1, 2, 4, 8) do baar repeat hote hain, aur aakhir me kernel size 1 wali convolutional layer hoti hai jo Dense layer ke barabar hoti hai.
  • WaveNet audio tasks me state-of-the-art raha — ek second ke audio me tens of thousands time steps hote hain, jo LSTM aur GRU handle nahi kar sakte.
  • Ek warning — agar best models ko 2020 se shuru hone wale test period par evaluate karo to performance bahut kharab milti hai, kyunki us dauraan ek badi global health crisis ne public transport ko bahut affect kiya tha. Models sirf tab achha kaam karte hain jab past patterns future me bhi continue karein — isliye production me deploy karne se pehle recent data par verify karo aur baad me performance monitor karte raho.

GitHub: 15_processing_sequences_using_rnns_and_cnns.ipynb

Code: Layer normalization wali custom RNN cell — GitHub
class LNSimpleRNNCell(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, units, activation="tanh", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.state_size = units
        self.output_size = units
        self.simple_rnn_cell = tf.keras.layers.SimpleRNNCell(units,
                                                             activation=None)
        self.layer_norm = tf.keras.layers.LayerNormalization()
        self.activation = tf.keras.activations.get(activation)

    def call(self, inputs, states):
        outputs, new_states = self.simple_rnn_cell(inputs, states)
        norm_outputs = self.activation(self.layer_norm(outputs))
        return norm_outputs, [norm_outputs]
Code: Conv1D + GRU model — GitHub
conv_rnn_model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Conv1D(filters=32, kernel_size=4, strides=2,
                           activation="relu", input_shape=[None, 5]),
    tf.keras.layers.GRU(32, return_sequences=True),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(14)
])
Code: Simplified WaveNet — GitHub
wavenet_model = tf.keras.Sequential()
wavenet_model.add(tf.keras.layers.InputLayer(input_shape=[None, 5]))
for rate in (1, 2, 4, 8) * 2:
    wavenet_model.add(tf.keras.layers.Conv1D(
        filters=32, kernel_size=2, padding="causal", activation="relu",
        dilation_rate=rate))
wavenet_model.add(tf.keras.layers.Conv1D(filters=14, kernel_size=1))
