F1End Matter · Interview FAQs

Interview FAQs

ML interviews (current era) ke liye — fundamentals se lekar deep learning aur deployment tak, 36 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.

Q01 Supervised, unsupervised aur reinforcement learning me kya farak hai?

Supervised learning me model ko labelled data milta hai — har example ke saath sahi answer (label) hota hai, jaise spam ya not-spam. Unsupervised learning me labels nahi hote; model khud data me pattern dhoondhta hai, jaise customers ko groups me baantna (clustering).

Reinforcement learning me koi fixed dataset nahi hota — ek agent environment me actions leta hai aur reward ya penalty se seekhta hai, jaise game khelna ya robot ko chalna sikhana.

  • Supervised: classification aur regression — label chahiye.
  • Unsupervised: clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection.
  • Reinforcement: trial-and-error se seekhna, reward maximize karna.

Interview me example ke saath farak batana sabse strong jawab hota hai.

Q02 Model-based learning aur instance-based learning me kya antar hai, aur generalization kya hoti hai?

Instance-based learning training examples ko yaad rakhta hai aur naye example ke liye sabse kareebi (nearest) examples se jawab nikaalta hai — jaise k-nearest neighbors. Model-based learning data se ek model banata hai (jaise linear regression ki line) aur phir us model se prediction karta hai.

Generalization matlab hai model unseen data par bhi achha perform kare, sirf training data ko ratna nahi. Agar model sirf training data yaad kar le, to wo overfit karta hai aur naye data par fail hota hai.

  • Instance-based: training fast, prediction slow, memory zyada.
  • Model-based: training slow ho sakti hai, prediction fast hoti hai.
  • Generalization ko test set par measure karte hain, training set par nahi.
Q03 Ek end-to-end machine learning project ke main steps kya hote hain?

End-to-end project ek pipeline hota hai, sirf model train karna nahi. Pehle problem ko frame karo — business goal kya hai, aur ML se kya solve hoga. Phir data lo, explore karo aur visualize karo, kyunki data ki quality hi model ki quality tay karti hai.

  • Data preparation: missing values bharna, outliers handle karna, features banana aur scale karna.
  • Model selection: pehle simple models try karo, phir unhe cross-validation se compare karo.
  • Fine-tuning: hyperparameters tune karo, phir best model ko test set par evaluate karo.
  • Deployment: model ko production me launch karo aur monitor karo — performance waqt ke saath girti hai.

Interview me California housing jaisa example dekar steps batana bahut achha lagta hai.

Q04 Data leakage kya hai aur train-test split karte waqt kya galtiyan avoid karni chahiye?

Data leakage tab hota hai jab test data ki information training me ghus jaati hai — jaise poore dataset par scaler fit karna aur phir split karna. Aisa model test par bahut achha dikhta hai, lekin real life me fail hota hai.

  • Sahi tareeka: pehle train-test split karo, phir sirf training data par preprocessing (scaling, imputation) fit karo.
  • Stratified split: classification me har class ka proportion train aur test dono me same rakhna chahiye.
  • Random split ka dhyaan: time-based data me random split galat hota hai — purana data train, naya data test hona chahiye.

Pipeline use karna best practice hai, kyunki preprocessing aur model ek saath fit hote hain aur leakage ka chance kam ho jaata hai.

Q05 Precision aur recall kya hain, aur inke beech tradeoff kaise handle karte hain?

Precision matlab hai: model ne jinhe positive bola, unme se kitne asal me positive the. Recall matlab hai: asal positive cases me se model ne kitne pakde. Dono ek saath badhana mushkil hota hai — threshold badhao to precision badhti hai, recall girta hai.

  • Spam filter: precision important hai — achha email spam me nahi jaana chahiye.
  • Cancer ya fraud detection: recall important hai — ek bhi case miss nahi hona chahiye.
  • F1 score: precision aur recall ka harmonic mean hai, jab dono ka balance chahiye ho.

Threshold ko tune karke business need ke hisaab se balance set karte hain, aur precision-recall curve se decision lete hain.

Q06 Imbalanced data par accuracy kyun misleading hoti hai? ROC-AUC kya batata hai?

Agar 95% data ek hi class ka ho, to sabko wahi class bolne wala bekaar model bhi 95% accuracy de dega. Isliye imbalanced data par accuracy dekhna dhokha hai — precision, recall aur F1 dekhne chahiye.

ROC curve alag-alag thresholds par true positive rate aur false positive rate dikhata hai, aur AUC us curve ke neeche ka area hota hai. AUC 1.0 matlab perfect classifier, 0.5 matlab random guess.

  • Accuracy: balanced data par theek, imbalanced par bekaar.
  • ROC-AUC: threshold se independent comparison ke liye achha hai.
  • Confusion matrix hamesha dekho — wo batata hai model kahan galti kar raha hai.
Q07 Overfitting aur underfitting kya hain? Bias-variance tradeoff ko kaise samjhoge?

Underfitting matlab model bahut simple hai — wo training data par bhi achha nahi kar paata, isme high bias hota hai. Overfitting matlab model training data ko rat leta hai, noise bhi seekh leta hai — training accuracy bahut high, test accuracy low, isme high variance hota hai.

Bias-variance tradeoff ka matlab hai: model ko na bahut simple rakho, na bahut complex. Dono extremes me test error badhta hai; beech me ek sweet spot hota hai.

  • Underfitting fix: zyada features, complex model, kam regularization.
  • Overfitting fix: zyada data, regularization, early stopping, cross-validation.
  • Learning curves dekhkar pata chalta hai problem bias ki hai ya variance ki.
Q08 Gradient descent kya hai? Batch, stochastic aur mini-batch me kya farak hai, aur learning rate kyun important hai?

Gradient descent ek optimization algorithm hai jo cost function ko minimize karta hai — model ke parameters ko dheere-dheere us direction me badalta hai jahan loss kam hota hai. Learning rate decide karta hai har step kitna bada hoga.

  • Batch GD: poora dataset ek step me use karta hai — stable lekin slow, bade data par mushkil.
  • Stochastic GD: ek example par step leta hai — fast lekin noisy, local minima se nikalne me madad karta hai.
  • Mini-batch GD: chhote batches use karta hai — speed aur stability ka best balance, deep learning me standard hai.

Learning rate bahut bada ho to model diverge kar jaata hai, bahut chhota ho to training bahut slow hoti hai. Isliye learning rate schedule ya adaptive optimizers use karte hain.

Q09 SVM kya hai? Margin aur kernel trick ko simple tareeke se samjhao.

Support Vector Machine wo decision boundary dhoondhta hai jo do classes ke beech sabse bada gap (margin) banaye. Boundary ke sabse kareeb wale training points ko support vectors kehte hain — wahi boundary ko define karte hain.

Kernel trick ka matlab hai: data ko bina asal me transform kiye, ek higher-dimensional space me le jaakar linearly separable bana dena. Jaise RBF kernel gol (circular) boundaries bhi bana sakta hai.

  • Margin bada: generalization behtar, naye data par zyada robust.
  • C parameter: margin ki chaudaai aur galtiyon ke beech tradeoff control karta hai.
  • Kernel: linear, polynomial ya RBF — data ki shape ke hisaab se chuno.
Q10 SVM aur logistic regression me se kab kisko choose karoge?

Dono linear classifiers hain, lekin unka focus alag hai. Logistic regression probability deta hai aur fast, interpretable hota hai. SVM margin maximize karta hai aur kernel se non-linear boundaries bhi bana sakta hai.

  • Logistic regression chuno jab probability chahiye ho, model ko samajhna ho, ya data bahut bada ho.
  • SVM chuno jab classes ke beech clear margin ho, features zyada hon aur samples kam hon, jaise text classification.
  • Large datasets par SVM slow ho jaata hai, wahan logistic regression ya linear SVM behtar rehta hai.

Interview me ye bhi batao ki pehle dono try karke cross-validation se compare karna best practice hai.

Q11 Decision tree kaise kaam karta hai? Gini impurity aur overfitting se kaise bachte hain?

Decision tree data ko feature par sawal poochh-poochh kar split karta hai — jaise pehle age, phir income — jab tak leaf nodes me ek hi class zyada na ho jaaye. Har split wo feature chunta hai jo data ko sabse achhe se alag kare.

Gini impurity ya entropy measure karte hain ki ek node kitna mixed hai — split ka goal impurity kam karna hota hai. Tree ko bina rok ke badhne do to wo training data ko rat leta hai, matlab overfit kar jaata hai.

  • Pruning: max depth, min samples per leaf jaise limits lagakar tree ko chhota rakho.
  • Regularization: max_features aur min impurity decrease se bhi overfitting kam hoti hai.
  • Fayda: tree interpretable hota hai aur feature scaling ki zaroorat nahi hoti.
Q12 Bagging aur boosting me kya farak hai? Dono kab use hote hain?

Bagging me kai models ko data ke alag-alag random samples par parallel train karte hain aur unke predictions ko average ya vote se milate hain. Isse variance kam hoti hai. Boosting me models ko ek ke baad ek train karte hain — har naya model pichhle model ki galtiyon par focus karta hai. Isse bias kam hota hai.

  • Bagging: models independent hote hain, parallel train ho sakte hain, overfitting kam karta hai.
  • Boosting: models sequential hote hain, accuracy zyada milti hai lekin overfitting aur training time ka risk rehta hai.
  • Example: Random Forest bagging hai, Gradient Boosting boosting hai.

Interview me ye farak ek line me batana kaafi hota hai: bagging variance ghataata hai, boosting bias ghataata hai.

Q13 Random Forest aur Gradient Boosting me kya antar hai? Stacking kya hoti hai?

Random Forest bahut saare decision trees ko bagging se train karta hai — har tree data ke random sample aur random features par banta hai. Prediction sab trees ka vote ya average hota hai, isse overfitting kam hoti hai.

Gradient Boosting chhote trees ko ek ke baad ek train karta hai, har tree pichhli galtiyon ko sudhaarta hai. Ye aksar zyada accurate hota hai, lekin hyperparameters tune karna mushkil hota hai.

  • Random Forest: fast, robust, kam tuning chahiye, parallel training.
  • Gradient Boosting: zyada accuracy, lekin slow aur overfitting ka risk.
  • Stacking: alag-alag models ki predictions ko ek aur model (meta-learner) se milana — ensemble ka sabse powerful tareeka.
Q14 Curse of dimensionality kya hai aur PCA isse kaise solve karta hai?

Curse of dimensionality matlab hai: jaise-jaise features badhte hain, data space itna khaali ho jaata hai ki points ek dusre se bahut door ho jaate hain, distances ka matlab khatm ho jaata hai aur model ko bahut zyada data chahiye hota hai.

PCA (Principal Component Analysis) data ko naye axes (principal components) par project karta hai, jo sabse zyada variance capture karte hain. Pehle kuch components me hi zyada tar information aa jaati hai, baaki ko hata sakte hain.

  • Fayda: training fast hoti hai, visualization (2D/3D) easy hoti hai, noise kam hota hai.
  • Zaroori step: PCA se pehle features ko scale karna must hai, warna bade scale wale features dominate karenge.
  • Components kitne: jitne se 95% variance explain ho jaaye, utne rakhna common practice hai.
Q15 PCA aur t-SNE me kya farak hai? Dono kab use karte hain?

PCA ek linear technique hai jo variance ko preserve karte hue dimensions kam karti hai — ye fast hai aur naye data par bhi apply ho sakti hai. t-SNE ek non-linear technique hai jo kareebi points ko kareeb rakhne par focus karti hai, isse clusters visualization me bahut achhe dikhte hain.

  • PCA: preprocessing, denoising aur fast dimensionality reduction ke liye.
  • t-SNE: sirf visualization ke liye, naye data par apply nahi hoti aur slow hoti hai.
  • Manifold learning: jab data kisi tedhi-medhi (curved) shape par pada ho, to non-linear methods behtar hote hain.

Interview me ye batao ki t-SNE se cluster ki distances ya sizes par conclusion nahi nikaalte — wo sirf local structure dikhata hai.

Q16 K-Means aur DBSCAN me kya farak hai? Anomaly detection kaise karte hain?

K-Means data ko K clusters me baantta hai — har point sabse kareebi cluster center ko milta hai. Isme K pehle se batana padta hai aur clusters gol (spherical) hote hain. DBSCAN density dekhkar clusters banata hai — ghane (dense) areas clusters hote hain, akeli points ko noise mana jaata hai.

  • K-Means: fast, simple, lekin outliers se bigad jaata hai aur K choose karna mushkil hota hai.
  • DBSCAN: K nahi chahiye, kisi bhi shape ke clusters dhoondhta hai, outliers khud identify karta hai.
  • Anomaly detection: jo points kisi cluster se door hon ya density bahut kam ho, wo anomalies hote hain — jaise fraud transactions.

Clustering ke results ko evaluate karna mushkil hota hai kyunki labels nahi hote — silhouette score jaisi metrics use karte hain.

Q17 Neural network aur Keras me MLP kaise kaam karta hai? Activation functions kyun zaroori hain?

MLP (Multilayer Perceptron) me input layer, ek ya zyada hidden layers aur output layer hote hain. Har neuron pehle wale layer ke outputs ka weighted sum leta hai, phir us par ek activation function lagata hai.

Bina activation function ke poora network sirf linear hi rehta — chahe kitni bhi layers laga lo, wo ek simple linear model jaisa hi behave karega. Activation function hi network ko non-linear patterns seekhne ki taakat deta hai.

  • ReLU: hidden layers ke liye standard — fast aur vanishing gradient kam karta hai.
  • Sigmoid: binary classification ke output ke liye, value 0 se 1 ke beech.
  • Softmax: multiclass output ke liye, saari probabilities ka sum 1 hota hai.
Q18 Regression aur classification ke liye Keras model me kya alag hota hai?

Keras me dono ke liye architecture ek jaisa ho sakta hai, lekin output layer aur loss function alag hote hain. Regression me output layer me ek neuron hota hai aur koi activation nahi hoti — loss ke liye mean squared error use hota hai.

Classification me output layer me classes ke barabar neurons hote hain. Binary classification me sigmoid + binary cross-entropy, aur multiclass me softmax + sparse categorical cross-entropy use hoti hai.

  • Regression: single neuron, linear output, MSE loss.
  • Binary classification: sigmoid, binary cross-entropy.
  • Multiclass: softmax, categorical cross-entropy — metrics me accuracy dekhte hain.

Interview me ye bhi batao ki data ko normalize karna neural networks ke liye bahut important hota hai.

Q19 Vanishing aur exploding gradients kya hain? Weight initialization se kya farak padta hai?

Deep networks me gradients backpropagation ke dauraan layer by layer multiply hote hain. Agar ye bahut chhote ho jaayein to pehli layers seekhna band kar deti hain — ye vanishing gradient hai. Agar bahut bade ho jaayein to training unstable ho jaati hai — ye exploding gradient hai.

Weight initialization iska bada solution hai: weights ko layer ke size ke hisaab se scale karke start karte hain, taaki activations aur gradients na bahut chhote hon na bahut bade. ReLU wali layers aur tanh/sigmoid wali layers ke liye alag-alag standard initialization schemes hote hain, jo activation ke hisaab se weights ko scale karte hain.

  • Vanishing gradient fix: ReLU activation, sahi initialization, batch normalization, residual connections.
  • Exploding gradient fix: gradient clipping, chhota learning rate.
  • Symptom: training loss atak jaaye ya NaN ho jaaye to gradient problem ka shak karo.
Q20 Batch normalization aur dropout kya karte hain? Early stopping kab use karte hain?

Batch normalization har layer ke inputs ko normalize karta hai — har mini-batch ka mean zero aur variance one kar deta hai. Isse training fast aur stable hoti hai, aur zyada learning rate bhi use kar sakte hain.

Dropout training ke dauraan randomly kuch neurons ko band kar deta hai, taaki network kisi ek neuron par depend na kare. Isse overfitting kam hoti hai — ye ek tarah ki regularization hai.

  • Batch norm: training speed aur stability badhata hai, thoda regularization bhi deta hai.
  • Dropout: sirf training me active hota hai, inference me band rehta hai.
  • Early stopping: jab validation loss badhne lage to training rok do — sabse simple aur effective overfitting fix hai.
Q21 Custom training loop kya hota hai? GradientTape kab use karte hain?

Keras ka standard fit() method bahut se kaam ke liye kaafi hota hai, lekin jab training par poora control chahiye — jaise custom loss, do optimizers, ya GAN training — to custom training loop likhte hain.

GradientTape TensorFlow ka tareeka hai gradients ko record karne ka: tape ke andar forward pass chalao, loss nikalo, phir tape.gradient() se gradients lo aur optimizer se weights update karo. Ye eager execution me automatic differentiation deta hai.

  • Custom loop chahiye: jab ek step me do models train karne hon, jaise GAN ka generator aur discriminator.
  • fit() kaafi hai: standard supervised training ke liye — custom loop likhna extra complexity hai.
  • tf.function: custom loop ko fast banane ke liye use karte hain, ye graph mode me convert karta hai.
Q22 Custom loss function, metric ya layer kab aur kaise banate hain?

Jab standard loss ya metric business problem ko capture na kare, to custom banana padta hai. Jaise agar ek tarah ki galti dusri se zyada mehngi ho, to loss me uska weight badha sakte hain.

Keras me custom cheezein banana simple hai: loss ek function hota hai jo true aur predicted values lekar ek number deta hai, metric bhi aise hi banti hai, aur custom layer ek class hoti hai jisme call() method me computation likhte hain.

  • Custom loss: jab galtiyon ki cost barabar na ho, ya regression me robust loss chahiye ho.
  • Custom layer: jab koi naya operation chahiye ho jo built-in layers me na ho.
  • Custom model: jab forward pass me branching ya multiple outputs hon.

Interview me ye batao ki custom code likhne se pehle check karo — aksar built-in loss ya layer hi kaafi hoti hai.

Q23 tf.data pipeline kya hai aur training ke liye data load karne ka best tareeka kya hai?

tf.data TensorFlow ki data pipeline API hai jo bade datasets ko efficiently load karti hai — data ko RAM me poora load kiye bina, batches me stream karti hai. Isse training fast hoti hai kyunki GPU kabhi data ka wait nahi karta.

  • map(): har example par preprocessing lagao, jaise image resize ya text tokenize.
  • shuffle() aur batch(): data ko shuffle karke batches banao.
  • prefetch(): agla batch pehle se taiyaar rakho, taaki GPU idle na rahe.
  • cache(): chhota dataset ho to memory me cache kar lo, har epoch me dobara read nahi hoga.

Best practice hai preprocessing ko pipeline me daalna, taaki training aur serving me wahi preprocessing use ho.

Q24 Structured aur unstructured data ko TensorFlow me kaise handle karte hain? Feature preprocessing ke main tareeke kya hain?

Structured data (tables) me numbers aur categories hoti hain — numbers ko normalize karte hain aur categories ko one-hot ya embedding se represent karte hain. Unstructured data (images, text) ke liye Keras me preprocessing layers hoti hain jo model ke andar hi chalti hain.

  • Numerical features: normalization — mean zero, variance one karna.
  • Categorical features: one-hot encoding chhoti categories ke liye, embeddings badi categories ke liye.
  • Text: tokenization aur vectorization — words ko numbers me badalna.
  • Images: rescaling (0-1 range) aur augmentation — model ke andar preprocessing layer se.

Preprocessing ko model ke andar rakhne ka fayda ye hai ki serving ke waqt wahi steps automatically lagte hain.

Q25 CNN kaise kaam karta hai? Convolution, pooling, stride aur padding ko samjhao.

CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) images ke liye bana hai. Convolution me ek chhota filter (kernel) image par ghumta hai aur har jagah pattern detect karta hai — pehle edges, phir shapes, phir poori objects. Har filter ek feature map banata hai.

  • Stride: filter kitne steps me aage badhega — bada stride output ko chhota karta hai.
  • Padding: image ke chaaron taraf extra pixels lagana, taaki borders ki information bhi bache aur size control me rahe.
  • Pooling: feature map ko chhota karta hai (jaise max pooling sabse badi value rakhta hai) — isse computation kam hota hai aur model thoda translation-invariant banta hai.

Deep CNN me pehli layers simple patterns aur aakhri layers complex objects seekhti hain — ye hierarchical learning hai.

Q26 Transfer learning kya hai aur image tasks me data augmentation kyun zaroori hai?

Transfer learning matlab hai kisi bade dataset par pehle se trained model ko apne kaam ke liye use karna. Pehli layers general features (edges, textures) seekh chuki hoti hain, isliye sirf aakhri layers ko apne data par train karna kaafi hota hai.

Data augmentation matlab hai training images ko randomly badalna — rotate, flip, zoom, brightness change — taaki model ko lage uske paas zyada data hai aur wo overfit na kare.

  • Feature extraction: pretrained model ki layers freeze karke sirf naya classifier train karo — jab apna data chhota ho.
  • Fine-tuning: baad me kuch layers ko unfreeze karke chhote learning rate se train karo.
  • Augmentation: test time par nahi, sirf training me use hoti hai.
Q27 RNN, LSTM aur GRU me kya farak hai? Sequences ke liye vanishing gradient kyun problem hai?

RNN sequences ko ek step par process karta hai aur pichla state yaad rakhta hai, isliye ye text ya time series ke liye bana hai. Lekin lambi sequences me gradients peeche jaate-jaate gayab ho jaate hain — purani information bhool jaata hai.

LSTM me gates hote hain jo decide karte hain kya yaad rakhna hai, kya bhoolna hai aur kya output karna hai — isse lambi dependencies seekhna possible hota hai. GRU LSTM ka simple version hai, kam gates ke saath, fast train hota hai.

  • RNN: chhoti sequences ke liye theek, lambi me fail hota hai.
  • LSTM: lambi dependencies ke liye best, lekin slow aur heavy.
  • GRU: LSTM jaisa performance, kam parameters, fast training.
Q28 Sequences ke liye 1D CNN aur RNN me se kab kisko choose karoge?

1D CNN sequence par chhote filters ghumakar local patterns dhoondhta hai — jaise text me 3-4 words ke phrases ya time series me chhote trends. Ye parallel chalti hai, isliye RNN se bahut fast hoti hai.

RNN sequence ko order me padhta hai aur pichla context yaad rakhta hai, isliye lambi dependencies ke liye behtar hota hai. Lekin ye sequential hoti hai, isliye slow train hoti hai.

  • 1D CNN chuno: jab local patterns kaafi hon aur speed chahiye ho, jaise text classification.
  • RNN/LSTM chuno: jab order aur lamba context matter kare, jaise language modelling.
  • Aaj ka trend: bahut se sequence tasks me transformers ne dono ko peeche chhod diya hai.
Q29 Attention mechanism aur Transformer kya hai? Ye RNN se behtar kyun hai?

Attention ka matlab hai: model har output banate waqt input ke har hisse ko alag weight deta hai — jo hissa relevant hai, us par zyada dhyaan deta hai. Jaise translation me ek word ka matlab samajhne ke liye sentence ke sahi words par focus karna.

Transformer poora attention par bana hai — isme recurrence bilkul nahi hai, sirf self-attention aur feed-forward layers hain. Isse poori sequence ek saath process hoti hai, isliye training bahut fast hoti hai aur lambi dependencies bhi achhe se seekhi jaati hain.

  • Self-attention: har word baaki sab words se apna relation khud nikaalta hai.
  • Parallel training: RNN sequential hoti hai, Transformer parallel — GPU ka poora fayda milta hai.
  • Aaj ka standard: modern language models aur bahut se vision models Transformer par hi bane hain.
Q30 Word embeddings kya hain? NLP pipeline me tokenization aur pretrained models ka kya role hai?

Word embeddings words ko dense vectors me badal dete hain — aise vectors jinme similar meaning wale words paas-paas hote hain. Jaise king aur queen ke vectors kareeb honge. One-hot encoding me ye meaning wali information nahi hoti.

Tokenization text ko chhote tukdon (tokens) me todna hota hai, kyunki model numbers par chalta hai, words par nahi. Aaj ke models subword tokenization use karte hain, taaki naye ya rare words bhi handle ho jaayein.

  • Pretrained embeddings: bade corpus par pehle se seekhe vectors ko apne task me use karna.
  • Transfer learning NLP me: pretrained language model ko apne task par fine-tune karna — chhote data par bhi achha result deta hai.
  • Masked language modelling: pretraining ka popular tareeka — chhupe hue words ko predict karke model language seekhta hai.
Q31 Autoencoder kya hai? VAE kya hota hai aur anomaly detection me autoencoder kaise use hota hai?

Autoencoder ek neural network hai jo input ko pehle ek chhote representation (latent space) me compress karta hai aur phir wapas original jaisa banane ki koshish karta hai. Chhota bottleneck use majboor karta hai ki wo sirf sabse important features seekhe.

VAE (Variational Autoencoder) me latent space ko ek distribution mana jaata hai, isliye isse naye samples generate bhi kar sakte hain — ye ek generative model ban jaata hai.

  • Denoising: noisy input se clean output banana seekhna.
  • Anomaly detection: normal data par train karo — anomaly par reconstruction error bahut bada hoga, kyunki model ne waisa pattern kabhi dekha hi nahi.
  • Dimensionality reduction: autoencoder PCA ka non-linear version mana ja sakta hai.
Q32 GAN kya hai? GAN aur diffusion models me kya farak hai?

GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) me do networks ek dusre se compete karte hain — generator nakli (fake) data banata hai aur discriminator batata hai ki data asal hai ya nakli. Dono ek dusre ko behtar banate hain, aur aakhir me generator bahut realistic data banane lagta hai.

Diffusion models alag tareeke se kaam karte hain: pehle data me dheere-dheere noise milate hain, phir model noise hatana seekhta hai. Generation ke waqt pure noise se start karke step by step clean image banate hain.

  • GAN: fast generation, lekin training unstable hoti hai aur mode collapse ka risk rehta hai.
  • Diffusion: training stable hoti hai aur quality bahut high hoti hai, lekin generation slow hoti hai kyunki kai steps chahiye.
  • Aaj ka trend: image generation me diffusion models standard ban gaye hain.
Q33 Reinforcement learning ke main concepts kya hain? Agent, environment aur reward ko samjhao.

Reinforcement learning me ek agent ek environment me actions leta hai. Har action ke baad environment agent ko ek naya state aur ek reward deta hai. Agent ka goal hota hai lambe samay me total reward maximize karna.

Ye supervised learning se alag hai kyunki yahan koi sahi answer pehle se nahi diya jaata — agent ko trial-and-error se seekhna padta hai, aur ek action ka fayda turant nahi, baad me mil sakta hai.

  • State: environment ki current situation jo agent dekhta hai.
  • Policy: wo rule jo batata hai har state me kaunsa action lena hai.
  • Examples: game khelna, robot control, recommendation systems.
Q34 Q-learning aur policy gradients me kya farak hai? Exploration vs exploitation kya hota hai?

Q-learning ek value-based method hai — ye har state-action pair ke liye ek value (Q-value) seekhta hai, jo batati hai us action se aage kitna reward milega. Agent hamesha sabse zyada Q-value wala action chunta hai.

Policy gradients seedha policy ko optimize karte hain — policy ko ek neural network se represent karke gradient ascent se uske parameters update karte hain. Ye continuous actions wale problems me behtar kaam karte hain.

  • Exploration: naye actions try karna, taaki behtar option mil sake.
  • Exploitation: ab tak ke best action ko use karna.
  • Balance: sirf exploit karo to behtar option kabhi milega nahi, sirf explore karo to reward kam milega — isliye epsilon-greedy jaisi strategies use karte hain.
Q35 Model ko production me deploy kaise karte hain? TF Serving kya hai aur model versioning kyun zaroori hai?

Model deploy karna matlab hai use ek service ke roop me available karna, taaki applications usse predictions maang sakein. TF Serving ek battle-tested model server hai jo TensorFlow models ko efficiently serve karta hai — ek saath kai models aur unke kai versions handle kar sakta hai.

Model versioning ka matlab hai har trained model ko ek version number dena. Naya model aate hi purana turant hata nahi dete — pehle naya version test karte hain, aur agar problem aaye to purane version par wapas ja sakte hain.

  • SavedModel format: model ko deploy ke liye standard format me export karte hain.
  • Canary deployment: pehle naya model thode se traffic par test karo, phir poora traffic do.
  • Monitoring: predictions ki quality aur input data par nazar rakho — data drift hote hi model retrain karna padta hai.
Q36 Bade models ko scale par train aur serve kaise karte hain? Distribution strategies aur quantization kya hain?

Bade models ko ek machine par train karna slow ya impossible hota hai, isliye training ko kai devices par baantte hain. Data parallelism me har device data ka alag hissa lekar model ki copy train karta hai aur gradients share karte hain. Model parallelism me model ko hi tukdon me baantkar alag devices par rakhte hain.

Quantization matlab hai model ke weights ko kam precision me badalna — jaise 32-bit float se 8-bit integer. Isse model chhota aur fast ho jaata hai, aur mobile ya edge devices par chal sakta hai, accuracy me thoda sa hi nuksaan hota hai.

  • GPUs/TPUs: deep learning training ke liye standard hardware hain.
  • Mixed precision: training me 16-bit aur 32-bit ka mix use karke speed badhate hain.
  • Serving par: quantization aur model pruning se latency aur cost dono kam hote hain.
